Very nice experience to sit in the kitchen and observe how the kitchen works with many chefs in it. They are great as a team.

Food. I like the dessert dish of peach very much. The courses showcase some culinary skills, but I am looking for more sophisticated ingredients and transformations at the price point of 300$ per person. Disappointingly, I found the savory dishes are way over powered by butter.

While sitting in the kitchen, I noticed that the chefs are reusing their utensils across that they tasted the dishes, which is somewhat disturbingly not hygienic to me.

We had a phenomenal experience at this restaurant. The food was outstanding—creative, diverse, and deeply seasonal. Every dish felt thoughtful and inspired, showcasing not just technical skill but a real sense of culinary joy.

One of the highlights was getting to dine in the kitchen. It was a rare treat to experience things up close, and the interaction with the chef was both personal and insightful as each dish was described. You can tell the team takes pride in what they do.

Service was excellent from start to finish—attentive without being overbearing. The wine list was a standout as well: detailed, curated, and refreshingly different. Mostly biodynamic bottle from small family-run wineries in Europe, but they said they also have a domestic selection.

Highly recommend this place!  Just make sure to book ahead. We’ll definitely be coming back.

Wow - what a night! My wife and I had the pleasure of dining at Ambra, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences we've ever had in Philly.

Ambra offers a single seating per night, featuring a multi-course tasting menu and wine pairings, with the entire experience lasting approximately 3.5 hours. That might sound long on paper, but trust me - the evening flies by. Every course was beautifully presented and full of flavor, with clear Italian influence but lots of creative, modern touches. The wine pairings were fantastic -- each one felt like it elevated the dish in a really thoughtful way.

The setting is also what makes Ambra special. Everyone sits around a communal table, which honestly could have gone either way, but ended up being such a highlight. Besides the couple we came with, we met two other couples during dinner, and we all ended up really hitting it off. It felt more like a dinner party than a restaurant -- but with food and wine on another level.

Service was smooth, attentive, and well-paced. The team knew the dishes and wines inside and out, and they explained everything with just the right amount of detail - never too much, never too little. It's clear they care deeply about what they do, and it shows in every part of the experience.

If you're looking for a special night out - something beyond the usual dinner - I can't recommend Ambra enough. Between the food, the wine, the setting, and the great company, it was truly unforgettable. Already looking forward to going back.

One of the best dining experiences in Philadelphia. Such creative food with local connections. The service and attention to detail is unmatched.

Highly recomended!

Best meal in Philly - hands down. Michelin-level food and service with a casual elegance perfectly reflective of Philly. Each dish is memorable, with bites that I still think about from the first time we ate here in 2019, and they have only gotten better. The wine is exceptional, and pairs with the food incredibly well. Chef Chris D'Ambro is so talented, and also fun and welcoming. Dont miss out!

(also ignore the bots)
customer_insights: Ambra Restaurant offers a unique dining experience with a focus on upscale Italian cuisine and a communal dining setting. The multi-course tasting menu is complemented by an exceptional wine selection, making it ideal for special occasions like anniversaries or first dates.

googleReviews:
We had one of our best dining experiences here.

The snapper ceviche and lamb chops were some of our favorite. The sweet potato dish was amazing.

I give the service 7/5 but it didn’t let me select more than 5 stars

An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. Sitting at the counter was a highlight — watching the chefs work with precision and grace was a show in itself. The service was warm, attentive, and thoughtful. Every dish impressed, from the oysters and blue crab to the thai spiced lamb chops and pasta special. We were even surprised with a complimentary serving of the grilled shrimp. The blueberry pie was the perfect ending — just sweet enough with a beautifully flaky crust and basil ice cream on top. A standout meal in every way.

Vernick is probably the most conflicted 4-star review I've ever given. There is absolutely no doubt that they serve great food with impeccable service in a wonderful space. However, for a special occasion dinner where we spent a lot of money, there were many small details in nearly every course that added up over the evening that frustrated us, especially considering that most dishes were on the verge of greatness. Despite some incredible moments that we loved, it did fall a bit short.

Our cocktails were fine, I enjoyed the "iris" as a walnut forward manhattan riff, though my wife's "jade tiger" tasted like a daquiri I could have easily made at home. We are also treated to an amuse-bouche of a tiny shot of butternut squash soup and a gougere. It was actually very baffling, as the soup was unremarkable and the gougere was dry and hollow/empty. It was fine, but we both agreed the meal would have been better if they simply had omitted it.

Fortunately things picked up nicely for the appetizers. Nearly every toast on the menu sounded amazing, and we ended up going with the foie gras which was beautifully rich and the grapes complemented the dish well. It was a bit clunky in its presentation as there was too much of each component overflowing and constantly falling off when trying to take a bite, but it was elevated and pleasant. The king salmon was solid with pear, lime crema, and basil, though again came across clunky with awkwardly torn herbs and odd cube chunks of pear.

The best, and simultaneously most frustrating app was the octopus. It was magnificently charred, and when you had a bite of the octopus with the pickled lemon and olive it was a perfect dish. Unfortunately, there not even remotely enough of the pickled component on the plate, meaning that two out of three bites were just lacked any acid and was just the octopus, which wasn't great on its own. It was somewhat emblematic of the entire experience - so close to being great if there had been just 15% more care and thought taken.

For the mains, I had the smoked duck breast, which was absolutely perfect in every way and is one of the top entrees I've had in the entire city. The duck was beautifully tender and the incredible rich pear mostarda was tangy and zesty. Underneath some nicely pickled cabbage were charred tropea onions that tied everything so well together. I strongly recommend this dish! Unfortunately, my wife's entree was a completely different story. The grilled sea bass's skin was so excessively charred that it completely overpowered any other flavor. Despite the fish itself being tender and flavorful, it was close to ruined and difficult to enjoy. We also ordered the roasted beets with ham and fig which my wife enjoyed.

Service was excellent and helpful, making recommendations and being attentive throughout the evening. Though we didn't end up ordering dessert beyond a glass of port, they were kind enough to bring over a tiny jelly candy with a candle on the plate to mark our special occasion which was thoughtful and appreciated.

In summary we certainly enjoyed our meal and I have no doubts that others may have had a "best in the city" type experience. The duck dish in particular made it worth it! But for the premium we paid, it would be difficult to justify returning soon when there are other similar-quality experiences with a smaller price and lower expectations.

Came here solo per a recommendation from the bartended at Friday Saturday Sunday. Had SUCH a good time! The salmon, sweet potatoe, chicken, Sazerac, and chocolate bitters cocktail were amazing! They also made me an off menu affogato for desert. Can’t recommend this place enough! Amanda the bartender was so great.

There are always a few “reference” points that exemplify what an experience should be. Vernick has been that reference point for me since it opened more than a decade ago. Somehow they have managed to maintain “peak” experience over time. I am seriously never disappointed. I cannot recommend the kitchen bar seating more highly. This is where you get the vibe and the show. It’s like The Bear without the yelling and dysfunction. Chef de Cuisine Billy is breathtaking in his confident but exacting presence. This is where you will see the great chefs of the next 50 years refining their skills.
I exhort you to Pay Attention. Put your phone down and soak this up as the extraordinary experience that it is. Alex, who was my attentive server tonight, and every single part of the staff will show you what peak performance looks like.
customer_insights: Vernick Food & Drink offers an exceptional dining experience with a focus on high-quality ingredients and attentive service. While the food is generally praised, some guests have noted inconsistencies in dish execution, making it a place for special occasions rather than casual outings.

googleReviews:
We celebrated our wedding anniversary at The Capital Grille in Philadelphia last month, and it couldn’t have been a better experience. My steak was cooked to perfection—tender, flavorful, and exactly as ordered. My wife, who’s vegetarian, enjoyed a lineup of sides (mac and cheese without the lobster, mashed potatoes, and spinach with garlic), all of which were excellent.

What really stood out, though, was the service. Our waiter, Bob, was exceptional—attentive, personable, and genuinely enjoyable to talk with. The highlight of the evening was when he and the manager surprised my wife with her very own crumb sweeper after she mentioned how fascinating it was to watch him use one throughout dinner. They even gave me a steak knife so I wouldn’t feel left out! Small gestures like that highlight the great service which truly differentiates the Capital Grille from other steakhouses.

Five stars all the way for both the meal and the outstanding service. We’ll definitely be back!

From start to finish, my birthday dinner at The Capital Grille in Philadelphia was truly outstanding! The experience was unforgettable thanks to Chef Wydia, whose culinary expertise ensured every dish was delicious and beautifully presented. Manager Rene went out of their way to make us feel special and celebrate the occasion, while Server Zach provided attentive and friendly service throughout. The ambiance was elegant, the food was exceptional, and the personalized birthday dessert was the perfect finishing touch. Highly recommend this location for any special occasion, these three made my birthday dining experience the best I’ve ever had!

Such an awesome place. Came here for the Generous Pour experience. So worth it! Lots of flavors in every single one. Wedge salad and ribeye were outstanding.
Shout out to Janelle, such an awesome waiter, made it a memorable experience.

I found this place on google and saw the reviews so I had to check it out myself. I was there on my birthday today and the service didn't disappoint. I was greeted by an employee in the front and was served by an amazing server (I forgot his name, but he was really really great!). He was very knowledgeable about the meals and was extremely friendly to me and my mom.

The manager came in and greeted us 3 times! I have never had a manager do that before. He sprinkled birthday decorations for me as well.

It didn't take for all of our food to arrive, the meal was fantastic! They also give you a complimentary dessert on your birthday, which was a great surprise. Out of all the restaurants I've been to, this is by far one of the greatest experiences. Will definitely be returning!

I had never eaten at The Capital Grille before my birthday 8/4/25, and although I don’t have money like that to go frequently, I wish I did! We had excellent service, and the food was so good that my friend and I felt giddy, practically high, from the deliciousness of what we ordered, and I didn’t know they go above and beyond for birthdays. It was a pleasant surprise to come up to our table and see confetti and a special note. Then afterwards, a complimentary dessert sampler platter and then they took my picture, and gave it to me in a physical card! Can’t beat that for birthdays (as far as I know)! I’m happy to come again and have a large snack at the bar with Jamie when I can. Love this place
customer_insights: The Capital Grille in Philadelphia is an upscale dining venue known for its exceptional service and high-quality steaks. Guests frequently celebrate special occasions such as birthdays and anniversaries, highlighting the restaurant's attention to detail and personalized experiences.

googleReviews:
Saloon is a Philly institution that I just got around to trying!

My friends and I booked a reservation out a month in advance. We absolutely loved the ambiance - upscale, vintage, cozy yet chic… definitely feel like you’re in South Philly.

We started with an appetizer sampler of grilled prawns, clams and poblano peppers. The clams stood out to us, they were delicious and flavorful. The prawns did not have a lot of meat on them and the poblano peppers weren’t hot enough (temperature wise). For $30 per person, we did not think it was worth it and would just order the clams by themselves in the future.

I got the linguine with blush sauce for my main, which was simple yet great. My friends got the angel hair with lump crab meat and lobster fettucine. The angel hair was a nice summer time pasta - light and refreshing. The lobster fettucine was good but not great, and at the high price tag of $44, my friend said he would not reorder it again.

None of the desserts interested us unfortunately. We found some of the options on the menu to be lackluster and wish there was more variety. We did enjoy what we had but weren’t blown away by anything.

I would like to come back in the future and order a cocktail at the bar, as I do love the ambiance.

Had a lovely birthday dinner at Saloon. Nicky made parking super easy and was a great face to welcome us into the Saloon experience. Our waitress Kittee knew what we wanted before we did and food was incredible. Happy to end the night chatting with Nicky again. HIGHLY recommend

The aesthetics of the restaurant are beautiful. We went based on ratings- the food was average. The filet mignon was tender but had no seasoning or flavor, mashed potatoes very bland. Husband had chicken parm, it was good but bang for buck I’ll keep Scannichios for best chicken parm ever. The peach salad was good, but expected cooked just a little more. Carrot cake likely not made inhouse. Icing fell off like old cake, no flavor. The ambiance is awesome, the service was good, food average. Best part was Dom the valet- he’s a keeper for this place. For me, this was a one and done. I can find many places less expensive and better food/ food choices in my opinion.

The short review: this is my favorite Philly restaurant. I always neglect to get actual pictures in Saloon because the food hits the table and everyone is on it. The vibe is unmatched - authentic, unique, South Philly energy. Perfect cocktails, plus I’ve yet to be let down by any dish, whether it’s salad, seafood, filet, chicken, THE PESTO with the bread. And of course, the every time, must order, Veal Parm. I’ve brought many different friends and family to Saloon and it’s always a winning night. Never change Saloon.

Really wanted to love Saloon but I think the food falls a little flat on flavor. Nothing stands out as excellent except the pesto with complimentary bread. I think the building is gorgeous, and there is a lot of cool decor & ambiance and that is what you’re paying for. I appreciate that it’s an institution but there is so much good Italian food in Philadelphia, I think if I came back I’d sit at the bar for a drink instead
customer_insights: Saloon Restaurant is a beloved institution in Philadelphia known for its upscale ambiance and vintage charm. While the atmosphere receives high praise, the food quality is mixed, with some dishes standing out while others fall flat. It's a great spot for special occasions and gatherings, but diners may find better value elsewhere.

googleReviews:
What a fantastic experience dinning in the Rittenhouse area of Philadelphia on a Tuesday night with a client and two EVP from my company. Extensive opportunity to have a continued conversation about our partnership.

The manager and hosted understood our need for privacy and a quiet setting. So we had the Rittenhouse room. What a fantastic room for a private dinner and had appetizers, to Wagyu fillets to wonderful desserts.

With a select Bordeaux of two we had a fantastic meal with tremendous attention to detail including vegetarian requirement ls and allergies.

I will be back again and you can have a marvelous experience for business or pleasure.

I had the pleasure of dining at Ocean Prime last night and was very pleased with the overall experience. I ordered the special halibut main course, which was expertly cooked flaky, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. The cocktail I chose was both well crafted and beautifully presented, a great complement prior the meal.

A nice surprise was the bread served alongside the main course, which added a thoughtful touch. The ambiance of the restaurant was spot on elegant yet comfortable and the staff was attentive and professional throughout the evening.

The dessert menu looked tempting, though I did feel the pricing was a bit on the high side. At $17, it seemed slightly steep, and something in the $12–15 range might have felt more appropriate.

That said, the wine list was strong, with a solid selection to choose from, and I was able to find something that paired nicely with the meal.

Overall, it was a great dining experience, and I’d definitely return! On the side note, there is a lot of homeless on the streets i would recommend driving or walking as a group.

Since it was our first visit, tried a pre-fix menu for 2. Honestly, it was a lot of food for the price! Started with cocktails; we loved the Paper Plane and the Hot & Dirty martini! Cocktails weren't included in the price but the cost was appropriate for the drinks we received. Shared the Dynamite roll and it was spectacular! French Onion soup was amazing! Steak and lobster tail with butter was cooked perfectly. Sides of whipped potatoes and broccoli were flavorful. They gave us champagne and a dessert for a birthday at no charge! The dessert was huge! Creme brulee can easily be shared between two people. Collectively, the service was really fantastic. They were very accommodating for any dietary restrictions. The management, servers, and support staff all worked well together. We felt like we were completely taken care of. I would definitely return here when I visit Philadelphia again!

We just got back from our anniversary dinner there and absolutely loved it. Beautiful ambiance, delicious food, and such attentive staff. I will forever be thinking about the bacon creamed spinach! They made our little celebration out a memorable one, and we will definitely be back :)

My wife and I went to Ocean Prime for our anniversary. We set up reservations using Open Table. Although I had to make a few changes to the timing the restaurant was accommodating. The ambiance and atmosphere were amazing! The place was clean. The food was delicious! Everything we had we enjoyed it tremendously. The steak was cooked the way we wanted it too and at the end we were full from our meal, which means acceptable portion sizes. The staff there were very nice and polite. Our waiter was extremely friendly and professional. They did set our table up for our anniversary and they provided dessert for us on the house!

Food items we had were: Speciality Sushi Roll, Shrimp Sauté, Lobster Bisque, NY Strip Steak, Lobster Tail, Side of Garlic Whipper Potatoes & Bacon Creamed Spinach. And to end off the night with some delicious Crème Brulée.

The only con’s I had were that they have valet parking, which isn’t the bad thing but the sign showed $26 but the valet charged me $33 and didn’t explain himself but I also didn’t ask. Also, even though the staff and everyone was kind and polite, I felt that the service could’ve been slightly more faster, but it could’ve been a busy night so I didn’t think it was such a big deal.

Regardless, of that I would HIGHLY recommend this place, all around everything went well!
customer_insights: Ocean Prime in Philadelphia offers an upscale dining experience with a focus on seafood and steak. The ambiance is elegant and romantic, making it suitable for special occasions like anniversaries and first dates. While the prices are on the higher side, the attentive service and quality of food make it a worthwhile choice for both business and pleasure.

googleReviews: The food lived up to its reputation—absolutely perfect. Every dish highlighted the natural flavors of the ingredients, and the seasoning was spot on. The only minor issue was that the staff sometimes spoke or acted in a slightly inappropriate manner that didn’t quite match the restaurant’s elegant atmosphere. With a little extra training, this could easily be improved. Still, there’s no doubt this place truly deserves its Michelin one-star rating.

Had an amazing meal here with my Girlfriend to celebrate her birthday. Each course on the tasting menu was a culinary delight after another. I especially enjoyed the fish course with halibut with sauce and flat bread, the short drip, and the duck. This intimate experience is the perfect spot of a special occasion, and I hope to be able to dine here again soon

Truly incredible dining! The service is great and while it’s definitely fine dining, there’s an air of casualness that makes you feel comfortable. The food was out of this world. The flavors mix so well and the order in which they come out just works!! We love the duck dish and the strawberry tarte.

Hello!!!! to the whole team! You guys are wonderful people!! You are rocking it! Best! Very welcoming experience! The Food!!! OMG!!! Words cannot describe!!! Keep doing what you are! I will be back for sure! Every dish was a true experience in my palate! The combination of unique flavors! Next time I will do the wine pairing as well! And also try the food at the bar!!! I am beyond grateful for all the hard work and effort you put into your restaurant! The experience is amazing! I wish you successful years ahead!!!

Every dish is excellent. The best tasting menu I had in Philly so far— not like the others that are swimming in the deadly butter. The rice dish is so good that it is comparable to the best Michelin Gohans in Japan.
customer_insights: Friday Saturday Sunday is a fine dining establishment known for its exquisite tasting menu and intimate atmosphere, making it ideal for special occasions like anniversaries and first dates. While the food receives high praise, some reviews note that staff behavior could be improved to match the restaurant's elegant vibe.

We were invited to a Private Memorial for a Family friend. Stephanie the bartender served us excellent drinks while we waited for the room to be ready. We will be back! 👍🏽

Our server was great! Loved the lobster bisque and then presentation was awesome!  My dad's lobster was great and so was my steak. We had a gift card for my dad's 91st birthday and server made is feel very special about that! Really 4.75 stars if that were an option!

We have come here every year for our anniversary. Tonight was by far the best! Our food was phenomenal. Everything cooked perfectly and delicious. Our server Allie was spectacular. We rented the Liberty Room for our daughter’s micro-wedding!!! What a great choice! Michelle, Stephen, Regan, Nadine were so accommodating and made us feel so special! The room looked beautiful second only to the delicious food!! Thanks, Chef!! I would highly recommend!!! It was magical!! Thank you!!
customer_insights: Eddie V's Prime Seafood offers an upscale dining experience with a focus on seafood and steak. Guests consistently praise the attentive service and elegant atmosphere, making it a popular choice for special occasions like anniversaries and birthdays.

googleReviews: I was super impressed with the food, ambience, and everything.  A hidden gem in Old City - recommend to anyone in the area looking for authentic and delicious Italian.  I enjoyed the happy hour appetizers & pasta bites.  Great happy hour, 4:30-6pm, at the wine bar only.  Excellent wine selection, apparently top-rated nationally.  Cheers—

Excellent time for a group of 7. Everyone left totally satisfied with appetizers, wine, main dishes, sides and even dessert. Not a single plate was left with any food. The brosoil with gnocchi was just fantastic both tender and delicious. For appetizers the calamari and barrata were the shining stars. Highly recommend this restaurant!

Panorama was the perfect final stop for our group’s Dine Around through Old City. From the moment we arrived, their team impressed us with a beautifully set table, custom-printed menus (even reflecting last-minute adjustments made earlier that day), and warm, attentive service throughout.

Their team was more than willing to work with us to coordinate the details of the visit and were truly wonderful to collaborate with. Our guests were blown away not just by the food and wine, but by the history and ambiance of the space. Learning about Panorama’s world-record wine collection added such a memorable touch to the experience.

As a food tour company that’s guided hundreds of groups around Philadelphia, we can confidently say that Panorama stands out. And we’ll absolutely be back!

Thank you Panorama!!

We had dinner at Panorama in Old City on Friday night with a group of 10, and everything was perfect. Bill and the team took great care of us — super friendly, attentive, and made the whole night easy.

The antipasto and bruschetta were the perfect start, and the food just kept getting better. Everyone loved their meals — from the gnocchi and scallops to the NY steak. The cocktails and wine were top-notch too. One of our guests said it was “the best Manhattan I’ve ever had,” and we all agreed it was amazing.

Great food, great drinks, great service — we’ll definitely be back!

Genuinely the perfect restaurant. Wonderful atmosphere with a great staff working it and food that absolutely never disappoints. I cannot rave over the food enough, don't even get me started on the wagyu meatball. Favorite restaurant in philly...
customer_insights: Panorama is a highly rated Italian restaurant in Old City, known for its exquisite food, impressive wine selection, and elegant ambiance. It is ideal for various occasions, including dates and group gatherings, with a welcoming atmosphere that encourages both relaxation and celebration.

It was an unforgettable dinner. The moment I stepped inside, I felt as if I had been invited to a close friend’s or family member’s home for a warm, intimate meal. The space is small, cozy, and wonderfully personal. The two chefs prepared and served each course with perfect timing, offering fresh, beautifully crafted dishes one after another without a single moment of dullness.

It was a joy not only to taste the food but also to watch the careful, thoughtful preparation behind every plate. The flavors were excellent, the progression of courses felt seamless, and I left with that perfect feeling of satisfied fullness.

There is no doubt that this restaurant fully deserves its Michelin one-star rating. A truly memorable dining experience.

The only thing I found disappointing was that, although I mentioned it was our wedding anniversary when making the reservation, nothing was acknowledged at all. The staff’s prepared guests’ birthday cakes, special party hats, cards and even a moment where the lights were turned off so everyone in the room could celebrate together. In contrast, our table didn’t receive even a simple mention of our anniversary.

Unique experience, but for what we paid, the food was not good enough to make me want to return. Some of the dishes were truly excellent, such as the seafood salad. Some others were a bit bland (red drum), or too salty (rabbit rillette croquette).

This is not to say that I would not recommend Her Place. I absolutely would! I still very much enjoyed the experience, but when something is this hyped I imagine its hard to live up to the expectation. The philly food scene is very competitive these days.

Love it! Love it!! ❤️ ❤️ it has been a while since I am so excited to rate a place! I found this place on Instagram and ranked #1 restaurant in Philly, so had to try.  Got lucky and book it the last min. So glad I went. No sense to talk about what I ate, because the menu changes every 3 weeks. You have to trust the chefs👩‍🍳 . You will have to eat what they cooked, like when you are visiting friends.

When I walked in, it is a small place with 11 tables. Feel very welcomed, like went to someone's house for dinner.  It is a fixed menu, no substitute, you eat what they cook. And everything was great! very fresh and just good! I don't know how to describe it. It feels like fancy home cooking.. very unique experience. For sure I will go back again! I would love to try their new menu!

What I ate: started with cheese made cracker with foie grass and jam, seafood salad ( the scallops was very unique, I had to eat a bit to figure out), rabbit  croquettes (soft tender in the middle, crispy outside), salad (refreshing with a little bitterness to balance out the deep fried croquettes), squash ravioli (oh the skin is so chewy and the squash was just taste so yummy), skate wings( wow mix the meat with the sauce.. heavenly), and finished with apple walnut cake ( my favorite!!! My god it was so moist... I need to figure out how it was done) oh we all got a little cookie and pretzel at the end.. for sure it was one of my best restaurant experience. Not only the food, but the entire experience.  Forgot we got extra chicken sausage,  it was good, but was too much food for me.

Verdict: I will be back! #4 restaurant in my Beli list

This was a special experience!
We enjoyed the description of each dish by the chefs and appreciate that most of the ingredients are sourced from local farms and vendors.
The menu changes every 3 weeks and there are no substitutions. They’re open Mon-Fri, with 26 seats, and 2 seatings, so reservations aren’t easy to get.
The energy was great and the food was excellent! I highly recommend!

Best dining experience in Philly and this is coming from a Philly resident. Everything was perfectly seasoned, the music selection was fabulous, the ambiance was lovely, the service was top notch, and the dishes were creative and absolutely delicious. Super seasonal and fresh. Highly recommend!
customer_insights: Her Place Supper Club offers a unique and intimate dining experience with a focus on seasonal, locally-sourced ingredients. While the food quality is generally praised, some guests have noted inconsistencies in flavor and service, particularly for special occasions.

googleReviews:
This review is for our only experience my fiancee and I had at this cozy, respectable, and classic neighborhood Italian restaurant back in JULY 15, 2023. Whenever I become fond of a place, trust me, I nearly always rate it FIVE stars here on Google.  I unfortunately cannot do this for this place. I will explain on the Service paragraph. I will focus on the food part first like I believe I am supposed to.

The food was definitely delicious. Its owners are NOT wrong whenever they claim its cuisine is authentically Italian-American. Since we were already tired of gravy sauce coming down from New York City, we chose seafood instead. We started our food journey here with some cheesy garlic bread and Shrimp Scampi. It was really to die for. We accompanied them with a Peroni beer to water these down. The entrees were so much better, of course.

My fiancee ordered Chicken Lorraine with Rigatoni pasta because she saw the lady next to us eating that dish. Again, we refused gravy because we already ate it back in NYC. She was enormously satisfied with her dish. I was with mine too. I ordered a Pasta Di Linguini, which is a House favorite. I did NOT regret it at all. Like I said in the paragraph above, they DO serve authentical Italian-American cuisine. The service Ronny provided us contributed to make it more authentic, but Carol diminished everything he was striving to build with us.

Ronny is an amazingly attentive gentleman who does his best to accommodate your needs. Carol, on the other hand, seemed like she was NOT comfortable serving a Hispanic couple like us and she did not hesitate to demonstrate it. Carol wanted to rush us to order despite we had NOT read the menu. She acted like she was TOO busy to take care of us because she was conversing with the other patrons seating in front of us. When she bought us our entrees, we asked her to please take a picture of us with our meal. She refused us TWICE claiming she was "too" busy.

We expressed Mr. Pippy DeLuca, the restaurant owner, our disatisfaction with Carol. We told him we wanted to leave a tip for Ronny but NONE for her because of the way she treated us. He understood our situation and told us we did NOT have to leave a tip for the service; which really pained us because Ronny came economically undone as a result. We had to withdraw money from their in-house ATM because one must pay them in cash. That specific part of their service is still back in the era when they started. Just like the atmosphere of the restaurant.

Besides the deliciousness of the food, the atmosphere of the restaurant makes you want to enjoy their delicious cuisine right there. It definitely takes you back to the times Mr. Pippy's parents founded the restaurant. The lightning at night is appropriate for patrons to immediately feel welcomed at their restaurant. The DeLuca family, as veterans of the neighborhood, truly show you the scenes of an Italian-American restaurant. You immediately feel inside a mafia movie like The Godfather Part I (1972), Goodfellas (1991) , or The Irishman (2019). We enjoyed the ambiance even more when we ordered a Tartuffo to share with our coffee.

Despite my disatisfaction with Carol's service, I would still give this amazingly classic restaurant another try on a future visit to Philadelphia. I would just refuse Carol serving me because I do not give my business to a prejudiced individual. However, I would only ask for Ronnie to serve me some of those delicious Italian-American dishes this place has earned its reputation for. Next time, I want to try their VIlla Salad, Ziti & Meatballs, Shrimp Scampi over Linguine, Sausage Genovese, Veal Bella Bucca, Chicken Neapolitan, or a Steak My Way. All these at their classic atmosphere.

I've been going to Villa Di Roma for over 30 years now. I love the location and the old school atmosphere. This place is simple and very good!
My wife and I always start with clams casino and fried asparagus. I love the Meatballs with either Spaghetti or Ravioli. My wife likes the Linguine Abbruzzi and Eggplant Parm. We are never disappointed and always stop back. Try Villa Di Roma for great South Philly Italian food.

These were hands down the best meatballs I’ve ever eaten. I should have stuck with them from appetizer to entrée but we ventured out and tried new things. My husband got the fish special and the pasta was perfectly cooked and it was an amazing portion size. It was a tad oily but he was very satisfied. I got a pasta dish with veal and chicken and tbh I didn’t see any veal (maybe it was mixed in with the sauce) and the chicken was kind of cubed and dry. Not my favorite dish but good enough to take it home for leftovers! Our waitress Michelle was so sweet and also part of the wonderful Italian family who owns the place. We will be back!
11/15/25: Delicious, authentic food. Friendly staff. Isabella is a great hospitality professional. Dishes were hot out of the kitchen.

Our trip to Philadelphia was to go to a Phillies game and we had a great time. However, one of the biggest highlights of the trip was our dinner here, at Villa Di Roma. It's located on 9th Street in "The Italian Market" and the street alone set the tone for what was to come as we entered this restaurant. The decor was old school, it made me feel like I was on the movie set of a good mob movie and/or Frank Sinatra was about to walk in. The service was fantastic and the food was amazingly authentic Italian. We started with an order of Garlic Bread which was mouth watering good. I ordered the Sausage & Peppers and Renee had Chicken Marsala. Our meal was flavorful and felt like "My Nona" cooked it. I'm not Italian but my "Grandma" was a great cook. I'm not sure when we will return to Philadelphia but whenever that is we will definitely return to Villa Di Roma.
customer_insights: Villa di Roma is a classic Italian-American restaurant known for its authentic cuisine and nostalgic atmosphere, reminiscent of old-school Italian dining. While the food receives high praise, service experiences can vary significantly, with some patrons noting exceptional service while others report less favorable interactions.

A Delightful Dining Experience

La Nonna Ristorante BYOB, located at 214 South Street, Philadelphia, PA 19147, is a family-owned gem where fresh pasta is made daily.

The light and pillowy gnocchi come in a variety of imaginative sauces. We tried the Garlic Alfredo Gnocchi, which was very filling and tasted terrific. The veal parmigiana was a standout, with a crisp, flavorful crust and a light homemade sauce.The Pompano special was another highlight, perfectly cooked with gnocchi and vegetables in a delicate white wine and garlic sauce. For appetizers, we enjoyed the crispy but not oily calamari, grilled octopus with capers and garlic for a salty-lemony taste, and Burrata with soft cheese, grilled peppers, and tomato.

Our meal ended on a high note with their light and flavorful tiramisu, lemon cake, and ricotta pistachio cake, the perfect finale to a satisfying dining experience.

Stepping into La Nonna Ristorante BYOB, you're not just a guest, you're part of the family. The owner, a beautiful young woman, has inherited her father’s legacy of hospitality and a keen eye for quality. Her dedication to ensuring every guest feels welcomed and valued is evident in every aspect of the dining experience.
customer_insights: La Nonna is a cozy, family-owned Italian restaurant in Philadelphia known for its fresh, homemade pasta and warm atmosphere. Guests rave about the delicious dishes, particularly the gnocchi and desserts, making it an ideal spot for romantic dinners and special occasions.

Can’t wait to return!
