We did receive olive oil with the bread but it was pretty bland so we just dipped the bread in the entree sauces.

We ended up finishing our meal still waiting for the focaccia to come and never did. So we asked the bus girl (very loud at cleaning up the plates by the way) who gave us the sour dough if we were still going to get our focaccia. She looked confused and said that they don’t have anymore and that we can have another helping of regular bread instead.

The waitress quickly came over and clarified that they are out of focaccia. She did not offer to take it off our bill so we had to ask to which she took off the entire bread service. Not only did she not tell us that there was no focaccia but was going to charge us for it, claiming that the sour dough was excellent enough even though it was cold and burnt.

Overall the meal was good, but it was definitely an interesting experience. We still tipped her well because we did feel that she may have been having an off day and we didn’t want to make it worse, but damn.

Outstanding meal and I can’t stop thinking about it. We had the Fazzoletti with Duck Ragu, Pasta with nettles and the macaroni with pork and I was stunned by how great each were. Hearty, fresh, complex flavors and incredibly delicious. Definitely on par with meals I’ve had in Italy. I know it’s not fair to compare restaurants but I never came away from Fiorella or Misi or other celebrated pasta go-to spots with the same desire to return. I don’t know why I waited so long to come here but I regret that. Staff was great and informed about their menu.

Super lovely spot, especially on the patio! Had the arrosticini, the roasted eggplant triangoli, the  saffron cavatelli, the zucchini sformato, and the mushroom side.

Really loved it all, but the eggplant triangoli and arrosticini were what stood out most of all. Both were really flavorful and nicely prepared. I’d still order all the dishes our group tried again.

They have a nice wine list and indoor seating available as well. The menu is a fun way to try some different Italian flavors from an often under represented region of the country when it comes to Italian restaurants in the states. Really nice menu!

Went early on Saturday pm place was full and we didn't have reservations but were seated within a few minutes.   Our waitress was outstanding with drink and food choices and checked in on us not too much  but just enough again she was so friendly even with the place being busy.  Cute neighborhood to stroll around before and after diner.   Food was outstanding!  My friend ended up getting a 2nd boul of the soup we both ordered! Pics posted
customer_insights: Le Virtù offers an authentic Italian dining experience with a focus on house-made pasta and unique regional flavors. While the food receives high praise, service can be inconsistent, and the ambiance is described as dimly lit, making it suitable for intimate dinners but potentially challenging for larger groups or casual outings.

googleReviews: Great Music, History and Food. We are part Italian, so we love a good Italian joint. This place is so classy. We all enjoyed our meal. I had Veal Parm, I’m a sucker for veal. The meat was super tender, the portion was huge, and the sauce was spectacular. I had gelato between pizzelles for dessert. Make sure to have a lemoncello after your meal.

It was great to eat at the oldest Italian restaurant. The food was great and authentic. It was on my bucket list and it was great that I was able accomplish it. I agree with Matthew Nelson below, the service was strange. I am glad that I had the opportunity, but I probably will not be returning despite the food be great and authentic. Service means a lot to me. It was okay, but not outstanding.

The four of us tried more things on the menu, and always the meatballs. Excellent again. The pow pow pow referenced below was for the mussels. Had clams in white this time not as pow pow but equally delicious.
Three weeks ago:
Excellent all around. Pow pow pow of flavor. Kudos to the staff who carry food up from the basement.

The resturant was a little dated, but cozy and warm.   The service was absolutely amazing. I ordered the Chicken saltimbocca, and the chicken was cooked to perfection and tender enough to cut with a fork.   The chicken and sauce was a little under seasoned but still very tasty.

Quintessential dinning experience. Trust the staff, get a chef special or recommendation and you will be blown away. You can tell they use fresh ingredients and quality ingredients by the sharpness and depth of every flavor. The environment will transport you to a nostalgic, youthful, and optimistic version of Philly. Loved every second of my meal here.
customer_insights: Ralph's Italian Restaurant is celebrated for its authentic Italian cuisine and rich history, making it a must-visit for food lovers. While the food receives high praise for its quality and flavor, some customers have noted inconsistencies in service. The ambiance is cozy and upscale, ideal for romantic dinners or special occasions.

googleReviews: Staff was engaging and fun. Cocktails were creative but not pretentious, just interesting twists on the classics. The ravioli with sage butter: chefs kiss. Plus you can have a top notch lamb chop and a stromboli in the same meal?!

Great atmosphere and chill vibe. Sat next to wonderful people at the bar to chat and chuckle with. Food was fabulous. I loved the octopus, split the ravioli w/my friend-awesome, meatballs were great. My friend loved her gnochetti rage and we split the ricotta cheesecake-WOW!! That’s all I can say-WOW! Albert made my day, lots of personality-love him!! Our bartender Nick, also great, full of personality and fun. Can’t wait to go back!

This place was amazing and definitely exclusive. With its speakeasies vibe we truly enjoyed our time!!! From, Albert at the door, Dan and Gabirela and Jorgen, and of course Kevin was our super star. The ambiance and vive was nice. Unforgettable night! The food was spectacular We'll be back!!

Classic Philly Italian club for eating, drinking, socializing and polishing your Italian since 1918. Close your eyes, sit down and wait while the 1950's waves inhabit you. Priceless. You'll need a local guide to get in - members only.

One of my favorite restaurants in Philly, in general. The staff is accommodating, friendly and knowledgeable. The food is consistent and has more flavor and soul than most restaurants you go to these days. In general, Palizzi is fantastic for dates, casual drinks, or a full-blown meal with a few friends.
customer_insights: Palizzi Social Club offers a unique blend of upscale Italian dining with a speakeasy vibe, making it perfect for intimate gatherings and special occasions. The engaging staff and creative cocktails enhance the experience, while the food consistently receives rave reviews for its flavor and presentation.

googleReviews: Bellini, a delightful dining experience, was the perfect venue for celebrating my husband’s birthday. The food was delectable, the ambiance was enchanting, and the service was exceptional. Our hosts greeted us warmly and personally confirmed the dessert surprise. One of them shared an intriguing story about the ceiling paintings, adding to the ambiance. Our server, Nico, went above and beyond to ensure our celebration was memorable. We eagerly plan to return to Bellini when we visit Philadelphia again. With gratitude, G & C

We walked in on a Saturday night without a reservation and were pleasantly surprised to find two open seats at the bar. We split the penne vodka and an appetizer, and the penne vodka was especially good—rich, flavorful, and perfectly cooked.

I ordered an espresso martini and a glass of wine, and both were excellent. The service at the bar was quick and friendly, making the experience even better.

The atmosphere was elegant but still comfortable, striking a nice balance between upscale and relaxed. Overall, a great spot for a casual night out with quality food, great drinks, and welcoming service.

Dinner before Eagles vs Green Bay on Monday night with a group of 5 who have been friends for over 50 years. Michael was our server and he was fabulous. Very attentive, knowledgeable, personable and professional. Their bread is so light and delicious. All of our meals were fresh and delicious. I had a great Caesar salad and their Polo Bellini. Great place to stop in if you are in the area.

Recently went for a family birthday dinner. Food was exceptional, staff friendly and our waiter Andy so sweet and helpful! Part of our family is Gluten Free (celiac) and the had great options and crème brûlée for dessert. Our first time but not the last! Loved the Veal Parmigiana and the Linguine with Lobster!

Great place, with good ambiance, not to noisy. Very friendly staff, keep checking if your ok.
Duck is delicious! No smell, not too salty, juicy inside, sauce not too strong. Very enjoyable. With a glass of pinot noir (staff can recommend wine if you like).
And of course desert. Love the affogato.
customer_insights: Bellini in Philadelphia offers a delightful dining experience with a focus on Italian cuisine. Guests appreciate the exceptional service, elegant ambiance, and quality food, making it suitable for various occasions, from casual nights out to special celebrations.

address: 34 S Front St, Philadelphia, PA 19106, USA
googleReviews:
A Perfect Engagement Celebration!

We recently hosted an engagement lunch for our son at Spasso Italian Grill, and it was absolutely wonderful. From the start, the team was warm, professional, and incredibly easy to work with. They partnered with me and my husband to create a customized menu that fit the occasion perfectly.

The appetizer table was a standout, beautifully arranged with arancini, fresh fruit, crab cakes, and an elegant veggie tray that looked as amazing as it tasted. Every course was delicious, and our guests are still talking about how good the food was!

The service was exceptional; attentive, friendly, and seamless throughout the entire event. The atmosphere was relaxed yet festive, just right for a celebration.

Thank you to the entire Spasso team for making our family’s special day so memorable. Highly recommend for private events or simply a great meal in the heart of Philadelphia
Most amazing dining experience ever! Food✔️Wine✔️ Service ✔️✔️✔️. Sam was amazing. One of the best restaurants and overall experience. And I'm a very picky eater!

We had an amazing experience at this Italian restaurant! The fresh pasta was outstanding — the penne was perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The veal parm was absolutely delicious, tender and perfectly breaded. We also loved the Spasso house wine — smooth and paired beautifully with our meal. Our waiter, Sam, was exceptional — friendly, attentive, and made the night even more enjoyable. Highly recommend!

Spasso Italian Grill was a great option for our first visit to Philly. It was within walking distance from our hotel located near Liberty Square. Casual dining experience good for families. We had the bruschetta for an appetizer, it looked plain when it came out, but the tomatoes were full of flavor!  My meal, the Penne Spasso, was a satisfying choice. There was a mix of mushrooms, peas, and bacon that gave it a ton of flavor. My son had the butter noodles with parmesan cheese and he ate every bite! This place has a great wine selection as well.

Got the Chicken Parmesan pasta — really good and i loved the al dente texture of the linguini. The portion, though, felt a bit small for the price. $33 for a plate of pasta feels steep, even if it was tasty.
customer_insights: Spasso Italian Grill is a highly recommended dining spot in Philadelphia, known for its delicious Italian cuisine and exceptional service. The restaurant offers a relaxed yet festive atmosphere, making it ideal for celebrations, first dates, or family gatherings.

address: 1415 W Porter St, Philadelphia, PA 19145, USA
googleReviews: Beautiful indeed. Going inside makes me feel like I'm truly in Italy, the waĺls, decoration, setup of the tables everything was great. The food is one of a kind and thats what makes this place amazing, the brightness, color and texture is on point. Truly recommend this place for an Italian night. The only thing that sucks is that there isnt any regular drinks so its only wine.

Sat outside on a beautiful September night. We would’ve sat inside but they were full. I did make a reservation two weeks earlier but outside was the only availability. When I went inside to tell them that we have arrived no one approached me. I had to approach one of the waitresses. They told me to choose any seat I want outside. When we chose our seat and sat down, our server immediately approached us and we were off. It is a BYOB. So we chose our appetizers which our server recommended. We chose the grilled calamari as well as the smoked mozzarella. Both were outstanding. Then for our entrées, I choose Asobucco (it was a special.) the veal was cooked to perfection. It fell off the bone. The pasta was homemade and excellent. Would definitely recommend. The other entrée pictured was shrimp and lobster with linguine. It was also excellent. For dessert we chose chocolate mousse cake. It was very good. As far as the service it was very good. My only complaint is that we asked for bread several times before it was brought to our table. Like I said, in the beginning, we sat outside so I did not get a chance to review the inside. It is very small so make sure you make your reservations early. Parking is not easy as well. It is free street parking but not many spots available. Uber if you can. For four people, our bill came to $240.

Absolutely amazing food. Great atmosphere and staff. I had the lamb shank special (I'd try and spell it but I'd do it no justice) in red sauce and pasta. The meat was so tender it fell off the bone just by looking at it.

If you want great food and atmosphere then come here and feast. 10/10 would go back every time I'm in Philly. Skip the chain restaurants that serve fake Italian and come here instead. You won't be disappointed. Also get yourself a Canoli to finish it off.

Update: was recently back in Philly and of course I had to get some more Italian from L'Angolo.  Got the  Orrechiette Duck and an awesome Caesar salad.

Food and service were both excellent, the seating is a bit tight, but not too bad. We had three courses, and every item was prepared well and full of flavor. I haven’t had a beet salad in a while and it was tasty. The grilled octopus was perfectly seared. Lobster ravioli and veal parm both delicious. Ended with the pistachio dessert. BYOB is nice as well. Will definitely return.

I can honestly say L’Angolo is the best Italian restaurant in the city. The food and ambience are top tier and the staff goes above and beyond to make you feel welcomed. Incredible experience and can’t recommend coming here enough.
customer_insights: L'Angolo Ristorante offers an authentic Italian dining experience with a cozy and upscale atmosphere. The food is consistently praised for its quality and flavor, making it a perfect spot for romantic dinners and special occasions. However, it is BYOB and does not have a wide drink selection, which may limit pre-dinner options.

googleReviews:
Recently visited this Italian restaurant and overall had a nice experience. We ordered the penne vodka and the lobster and crab ravioli Portofino. Both dishes were good—solid Italian comfort food—though not overwhelmingly great. We also tried a few cocktails(recommend the espresso martini), which were very well made and definitely a highlight of the meal.

Another big plus is the ample parking, which is especially convenient if you’re heading to the stadiums for an event.

Our food came out surprisingly fast, but the overall service throughout the meal was a bit slow. That said, the staff was very friendly and welcoming.
An excellent Italian restaurant. The olive oil served with the bread is outstanding, and the eggplant dish is both creative and delicious.
Food was excellent and great wine menu. I loved that they had parking and it’s beautiful indoors. I got the chicken saltimbocca it was absolutely delicious. I will definitely be back.

Well all I can say is that this place is a one and done for me. Waitress was non- existent most of the meal. Food is mediocre and when you have to eat your dessert with a knife that’s really a problem. I will definitely never visit this restaurant again. Plus no bread was ever given and we were never offered coffee or tea. There are plenty of restaurants you can spend over $200. In and get a much better meal.

I’ve been to this restaurant before, over a year ago. The food was good at that time. I revisited this restaurant with my family to celebrate my grandson tonight. The food was not that great and the service was very slow and unwelcoming. We had to ask for bread and the oil which is normally given at an Italian restaurant from the beginning, we also asked for Parmesan cheese for our entrées, which was surprisingly a shaker of powdered cheese. We’ve been to cheaper Italian restaurants that have grated real cheese.
No manager came to the table the entire time we were at the restaurant and staff show little concern about our Group being happy with our experience. We will not be returning.
.
customer_insights: Popi's Restaurant offers a casual yet upscale Italian dining experience with a focus on pasta and a good wine selection. While the ambiance is generally pleasant and suitable for romantic occasions, service inconsistencies and mixed food reviews suggest that guests should manage expectations regarding their dining experience.

googleReviews: My first time here and I loved it! The only thing is the seatings are sooooo closed to each other it feels really tight. We decided to have a seat at the love chair for a more intimate happy hour experience even though it’s besides the restroom but it didn’t bother us. The prices were reasonable and I love how if you have a seat at a happy hour table you can also order from their standard menu. Let’s take a deep dive on everything I tried. The love knot cocktail was sooo good it reminded me of a lemon drop. The shrimp tacos were really gooooood. The edamame dumpling was my absolute favorite because I loveeeee truffle flavor. The shrimp tempura was good as well I just wish there was spicy mayo we could’ve add on top, the spicy tuna was spicyyyyy but flavorful and delicious! The tuna crispy rice was another one of my favorites I love the two textures together of the crispy rice and spicy tuna. The oysters was another good one it had a burst of spicy flavor with a nice buttery taste to the oyster. & to end my meal I finished off with a cocktail I forgot the name of it but it was a similar taste to the rose cocktail but a little more sour. All in all our server Olivia was amazing the service was top tier, food was delicious for happy hour prices! Another thing I would like to add is I collect matches from restaurants that I’ve tried and this restaurant was the only one on this block that did not have any.

We came to Double Knot for our 5 year anniversary after having multiple people recommend it to us, and we did not leave disappointed. The atmosphere was so warm feeling I loved the underground sort of feel, though I wish there was a smidge more space between tables as we felt a little cramped. We had actually gone to Sampan last year and did the chefs tasting menu, so decided to do the same at Double Knot. You get 10 dishes. We chose the Tuna Tartare for our cold, not my personal favorite but still very good. Wagyu soup dumplings for our small which similar to Sampan their dumplings are delicious. We actually got 3 robatayaki because of an accidental miscommunication so we got the Tokyo scallion, lamb chops, and salmon scallops which we agreed was our favorite thing as it was full of flavor and melted in your mouth. For the crispy we got the Japanese Fried Chicken which was my second favorite it was so crispy and had some tangy flavor to it, it paired very well with the aioli it came with. We did pork tonkatsu for the meat, and you can't go wrong with a good pork tonkatsu. For the fish we did the Japanese Scallop, and as someone that typically doesn't love scallops they were very good. Our side was the shrimp udon mazeman, which my partner really loved, they kept saying how delicious it was. We got the yellow tail sashimi which the orange and the Serrano pepper it comes with really paired well together. For our sushi we went with the Double Knot Big Eye tuna, which may have been the best sushi I've ever had. Our meal finished with our dessert a miso and caramel ice cream which was such a delicious blend of sweet and savory.

Another absolutely wonderful dinner from Schulson collective, with a great atmosphere, excellent friendly service, and delicious food. I personally prefer Sampan just a smidge above Double Knot, but still very much enjoyed Double Knot.

This spot is a must for happy hour - their menu is fantastic. Everything I tried was delicious and the prices were unbeatable. I ordered the Kim chee fried rice, the salmon scallion robatayaki, the Japanese fried chicken, and the shrimp tempura roll. Every dish was flavorful, and the smaller portions made it easy to sample multiple items. I shared two dishes with a friend, and she also ordered two additional happy hour plates for herself. We left feeling full but not overly stuffed - the perfect balance - and all at a great price.

The only downside was that the bar seating felt a bit tight during happy hour, but considering how packed it was for a Tuesday, it’s easy to see why.

This is my second time here, my first experience was a few years back and it was wonderful. Myself and three friends wanted to dine here while visiting Philly and this was a good choice. Our waiter Mike was so very pleasant he made our experience so worth while. He was very fluent with the menu options and steered us in the right direction with our food choices. We ordered multiple dishes to share which is always a good thing to do. Edamame to start, those were super delicious seasoned perfectly. The spicy baked scallop and crab my fav so delicious as well.  It was the tables fav as well because everyone ordered that dish. Very appealing as well. A good fried rice is always a plus , we chose the mushroom truffle fried rice and the Japanese fried chicken to pair it with , good pairing. Wild mushroom gyozas were apart of the spread as well. Last but not least the broiled oysters , super bomb! All of drinks were perfect as well with our dishes. Please be aware it is very dark in there. Overall we had a grand time!

- Service: Fast and friendly. They are very knowledgeable about their menu and their food.

- Ambiance: Very nice ambiance but it's very dark. It makes me feel like I'm in Diagon Alley in Harry Potter.

- Food: There're two prices for tasting menu- $69 & $79. $79 offers more quality of meat and cut (?) if I remember what our waitress said right. However, we just went for a la carte since we had a late lunch.

- For robatayaki: We got ribeye scallions and scallops. The ribeye is so tender! Nice charcoal grill taste added to it, and I didn't know scallions could be paired so nice with beef. Scallops are sweet and slightly salty which is perfect.

- Specialty sashimi: We got Toro and Yellowtail. I love the Toro more, somehow it's thicker and the soy sauce with wasabi going so nice together. Yellowtail dish was overpowered by the yuzu and citrus sauce. The selections of special sashimi are pretty decent and very refreshing.

- The other dishes we ordered were just alright, they didn't impress at all.

- Overall, $175 included tax and tips for this whole meal but still left me a bit hungry, so I would say this restaurant definitely lean into more expensive side. We were also excited for the miso soft-served ice cream but unfortunately, they were out of it, which is weird for a Friday night. Easy to make reservations. Hard to find parking. I would recommend it for people who want to experience new and nice restaurants in Philly. For me myself, I think it's a nice experience but not impressive enough to come back soon.
customer_insights: Double Knot offers a vibrant atmosphere with a unique underground feel, making it a great spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The menu features a variety of flavorful dishes, particularly known for their robata and sushi, with an appealing happy hour that attracts a lively crowd.

googleReviews:
Really good omakase and we’re accommodating about swapping out certain fish which is super kind.

The sushi was great!

My only thought is that I did feel a little hungry before leaving so I ordered 2 more pieces but probably could have used a few more in the omakase itself.

It’s a BYOB omakase spot in the city that requires reservations. The 15 course menu features premium ingredients like foie gras, king salmon, otoro, and A1 wagyu beef. I really like how each piece is paired with unique supporting elements that highlight its flavor. The entire experience lasts about 1.5 hours and $95/ person before tax and gratuity, they also provide an a la carte menu to add on the experience. They can accommodate some dietary restrictions, but since it’s primarily a sushi focused menu, vegans may want to skip this one. A great spot to celebrate a sophisticated birthday.

Tried omakase for a birthday dinner. IMO I wished there was more attention to detail & quality ingredients, such as using exotic limes instead of regular Mexican lime, they used premade wasabi instead of freshly grated wasabi. I think the fish wasn’t comparable in quality to other omakase places I’ve had in Philly. The sushi chef wasn’t as skilled, cutting uneven pieces of fish, even to an untrained eye can observe. Many pieces I’ve had wasn’t memorable. The service was a miss at various points during service, we were not given a dessert spoon, dinner was a rush for the meal price we paid, towards the end our whole dining group was rushed out like a herd of cattle right after the dessert piece was served, this tampered the ambiance of our dinner. Overall, this was an OK experience but I wouldn’t call this a true omakase.

Celebrated my husband’s birthday. 16 courses for $100 each person.

Insanely good! Great variety. Went at 5PM on a Friday because we had a babysitter. We booked the “upstairs indoor” seat and it was amazing. Were the only guests at this table and the chef prepared every course in front of us. Staff was very attentive. Reminded me of Michelin dining.

If you're looking for a sushi experience that’s high-quality, Kichi Omakase IS THE PLACE!! Every piece I had was extremely fresh and the flavor was well balanced. Despite my gluten restriction, the chef went out of their way to make sure I could enjoy the full experience, which was truly amazing. Inside was cozy and beautifully decorated. The chefs are not only skilled but also engaging. The staff were very welcoming, polite, and attentive! My experience here went very smoothly. I can’t wait to come again!
customer_insights: Kichi Omakase offers a refined dining experience with a focus on omakase-style sushi. While many patrons praise the freshness and creativity of the dishes, some reviews indicate inconsistencies in service and ingredient quality. Ideal for special occasions like anniversaries or first dates, the intimate setting enhances the overall experience.

googleReviews:
Royal Sushi has been a raved about place for as long as I’ve been in Philly, just got around to trying it. This review is for the main dining room and not the omakase tasting.

Walk-ins only, there’s about 10 tables with 3-4 of those being for large parties. Bar fits 15 or so people. Tight space and pretty dim lighting. Hostess was nice, bartenders weren’t the most attentive but nothing negative.

For drinks, we got the kappa punch and ginger mint smash. The kappa punch was outstanding. Fresh, sweet but not too sweet and so well balanced. I could’ve drank several. My mom enjoy the n/a ginger mint smash as well.

We started with the edamame. Hard to go wrong with that - cooked well and not stringy. The ebi (shrimp) shumai was a let down. The presentation was beautiful, but there was no flavor other than an overload of salt when I bit into it. I didn’t taste any spicy mustard. I wouldn’t reorder. Then, we had the nasu dengaku. Japanese eggplant, miso glaze and pickled cauliflower. These were delicious. Savory and warm, they felt like a hug.

Lastly, the sushi we got was the spicy crab tempura. The presentation was extremely underwhelming, it looked like sushi that we get from a grocery store. It also was so bland… there wasn’t anything spicy about it as advertised. It did taste fresh, but that was all it had going for it.

Overall, we left feeling underwhelmed considering the rave reviews this place receives. I am considering coming back in the future after doing more research about some of the stand out dishes.

Royal Izakaya is a fun dining experience for sharing and trying many cool dishes. The Tuna guacamole was super fresh and their Chicken Katsu Sando was my favorite of the meal. The Duck was good, kinda like a cold cut platter but imo the Mustard was extremely overpowering. All affordable and inside a nice dining space, this spot is very legit and is worth the try.

We’ve been to Royal Sushi & Izakaya more times than we can count and not once have we had anything less than an incredible experience. This place has become a personal favorite for my wife and I, and honestly, it might just be our favorite Japanese restaurant ever.
The vibe are always spot-on; lively and fun on the izakaya side, with incredible energy, yet still intimate enough to enjoy a thoughtful meal. Every dish we’ve ordered, from small plates to sushi, is packed with bold flavors and precise execution. The fish is consistently fresh and expertly prepared, and even the cooked dishes never feel like filler — everything has intention.
We’ve even ordered takeout multiple times, and the quality never slips. Pickup is a breeze, there’s a small window on the side of the restaurant where you just give them your name, and within seconds, the staff brings out your order.
My wife is completely obsessed with this place and especially with Chef Jesse Ito. She follows his every move on social media, and it’s become a bit of a tradition for us to talk about one day finally scoring seats at his legendary omakase. It’s at the top of our culinary bucket list, and until then, the izakaya keeps us more than satisfied.
Royal Sushi & Izakaya isn’t just a restaurant, it’s a temple of culinary excellence. Every meal here is a reminder that food can be art, ritual, and joy all at once. The precision, the passion, and the soul that go into every bite put Royal in a league of its own. If you have the chance to go, don’t hesitate. Just go. Again and again.

My honest review of Royal Sushi and Izakaya in Old City.  I was eager to try some of their a La carte items because getting a reservation for their omakase seems almost impossible to get one of their limited 8 seats! My friend and I were happy to find that there was only a 15 minute wait before we were seated.  Our waitress recommended 3-4 items per person, and including our tasty dessert, we left feeling cozy and pleasantly full! We ordered the spinach gomaee (first photo & second photo, top-right) which was amazing - black sesame is such a decadent flavor and paired so well with the spinach. We also got their tuna guac (second picture, bottom) and the tuna was so fresh and soft, it practically melted in my mouth and meshed so well with the tasty guacamole. We also ordered one of their kitchen specials, grilled trumpet mushrooms (second picture, top-left). The mushrooms were tender, but we needed a knife to make bite-sized pieces because it just wasn’t easy to bite into, but they were marinated in this savory sauce and it was absolutely delicious! We got their uni cream pasta (photos 3 & 4) which was incredible. The sauce had this Parmesan mascarpone taste with a hint of some kind of acidic lemon flavor; and it was such a perfect blend of flavors. Best of all, to our total surprise, it was topped with gold leaves! First time eating gold and it was a bougie and magnificent treat 💅 Their agedashi nasu tofu (photo 5) came in a very tasty but simple broth. It almost tasted like chicken broth but it was a perfect balance for the tofu and all the green onion-type garnishes. I’ve also never had saba shioyaki (salt-broiled mackerel, photo 6) and I was pleasantly surprised to learn that I kept coming back for more. The fish was so fresh and perfectly salted. With a bite of rice in between every few mackerel bites, you just can’t go wrong. Their karaage wings (photo 7) were cooked to actual perfection. The skin was super crispy with the meat being so tender and juicy inside. Sadly, not pictured was one of the stars of the evening which was the kamo rosu (duck breast). This was another first for me and it was incredible. The duck was so soft and the tare sauce had an umami element to it that really elevated the dish. It also came with karashi which is a Japanese hot mustard and was such an excellent dipping sauce, it tasted like a well-balanced blend of mustard and horseradish. To finish things off, for dessert, we got their royal sundae (photo 8) which was a super tasty sweet corn ice cream with actual corn throughout, and topped with a salty caramel sauce and dollops of mascarpone. It also had these really tasty cookie bites that seemed familiar but we just couldn’t place the flavor. We also ordered their yuzu cake (photo 9) that came with the most amazing sauce that had a slight taste reminiscent to lemon curd. The spongy cake was baked just right and the light sauce was the perfect touch to a delectable treat.

The pasta was WAY too salty. Some things had no taste while the others had too many salt. Not worth the price and it’s def over hyped

also we did walk in as the third party in line and they tried to seat us by the door when the entire dining room was empty. like why do we need to ask to sit further away from the door so we don't freeze...
customer_insights: Royal Sushi & Izakaya is a popular dining destination in Philadelphia known for its vibrant izakaya atmosphere and fresh sushi offerings. While many customers rave about the quality and creativity of the dishes, there are mixed reviews regarding specific items, indicating a need for careful selection. Overall, it is a great spot for casual dining and sharing plates with friends or for a romantic evening.

googleReviews: I’ve been to this place countless times, it’s my go-to spot for a quick lunch or a casual hangout with friends. The whole experience can take as little as 10 minutes from start to finish: you get seated, grab your dishes straight from the revolving belt, return your plates through the slot, and check out, all fully automated! They also have a great rewards program. My favorites are the conch and the bluefin tuna toro, but they’re not always available.

My so and I tried the revolving sushi spot on Chestnut Street in Philadelphia, and it was definitely a fun experience. The concept is simple but entertaining—sushi plates come around on a conveyor belt, and you just grab what you like. Drinks are served by a robot, which adds a cool, futuristic touch.

Each plate is $3.75, and there’s a reward system where you get a prize at 15 plates and another at 25. It makes dining feel playful, though it also makes you more aware of how much you’ve eaten. We ended up with 28 plates plus a chicken ramen, which was surprisingly good, and the total came to around $125 for two people.

The sushi itself was fine—not the best in the city, but good enough for the experience. Overall, it’s more about the novelty and fun atmosphere than gourmet quality. For me, it’s a one-time try, but if you like interactive dining, it’s worth checking out at least once.

It had been a while since we visited a revolving sushi restaurant, and the concept here is quite interesting. You can either order from a tablet or scan a QR code at your table, or you can grab items directly from the conveyor belt as they pass by. While we didn't take anything from the revolving belt, it was great to see what the different dishes looked like. Our orders were delivered directly to our table via an upper conveyer system, and drinks were brought out by a robot! If we needed anything else, we could request a human staff member through the app.

The food was good, and they have some unique preparations and specials. We went for lunch, so the fact that they don't serve alcohol was fine, but we probably wouldn't go for dinner for that reason. The restaurant is definitely family-friendly and a huge hit with kids.

Went here with a work buddy and had a great time! The sushi was fresh, flavorful, and there was an impressive variety to choose from. Even the cheesecake and butter pie were delicious — a sweet surprise at a sushi spot. Highly recommend for both quality food and a fun atmosphere!

I enjoyed my time here at Kura Sushi. I was actually surprised to see one here in Philly. I had to come and try it out. The service was good and the food was fresh. I loved the different kinds of sushi they have available just rotating around. This did bring me back to when I was in Japan (懐かしい). I will definitely come back again and encourage all the sushi lovers to come along. They also have ramen as well among other things to try. この場所はすばらしい。
customer_insights: Kura Revolving Sushi Bar offers a unique and interactive dining experience with a conveyor belt sushi concept. It's a fun spot for casual hangouts, suitable for families and groups, though the sushi quality is more about the experience than gourmet dining.

googleReviews: Have been coming here for years and the evolution of the menu is real ! So glad they have added back more veg/vegan rolls. I think my 2 favorites will always be Old School and Sweet Meadow but tried KFC today and I think it may have earned the title of 3rd favorite! Great place to come with veg/non-veg mixed party since there are the same number of non-veg sushis as veg sushis.

We’ve been loyal customers of Fat Salmon for a long time and have always loved it, but on recent visits something feels different. It seems like the recipes, quality, and even portion sizes have changed—and unfortunately, not for the better. What used to be one of our favorite go-to spots now feels inconsistent compared to the high standard they once had. We really hope they can return to the level of freshness, flavor, and generous portions that originally made this place so special, because it’s disappointing to see the experience slipping.

Most amazing selection of vegetarian sushi and all were great. Wish had more lighting but vibe was cool nonetheless. Highly recommend.
Service was good also. The Sake flight was little too fruity for me

This is easily my favorite sushi place in Philly, and fancy sushi is my favorite roll (but lots of them are really good). Honestly so lucky to live nearby so I can come back often! Also vibes are great, so cute, for dine in
The food was delicious and there were plenty of options.  Great staff and a cute vibe!
customer_insights: Fat Salmon Sushi is a popular casual dining spot in Philadelphia known for its diverse sushi offerings, including a strong selection of vegetarian options. While many customers appreciate the evolving menu and vibrant atmosphere, some have reported inconsistencies in food quality and portion sizes during recent visits.

googleReviews: We like the sushi, they torched the salmon, so it's not really raw. Wagyu fried rice is very tasty and the portion is not bad for the price. Tempura is not really our favorite, only two pieces of shrimp and the rest only fried veggies. The ramen is good because of the very good broth, very rich and not too thick. It's perfect! The pork is very tender and delicious. Overall, we enjoyed our dinner  there. Even though, the store is very crowded, they serve fast. Bathroom is very clean and smells very nice.

new favorite sushi restaurant in Philly! location is super easy to get to being near Reading Terminal and the BYOB aspect is great with wine and spirits around the corner. Haris and Mitsu created an awesome spot with a wide menu. the specialty rolls were truly interesting and a great combination of fresh and savory. Winnie was our waitress and gave perfect recommendations and was overall amazing service! Will be back soon and often

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Nakama and overall, it was a fantastic experience. The sushi itself was absolutely top-tier, every bite was fresh, flavorful, and thoughtfully crafted. You can really taste the quality and attention to detail that went into each course.
Nakama is BYOB, they do offer some in-house drink options (like teas or non-alcoholic pairings), which were also quite good.
That said, a few elements of the experience could be improved. The ambiance, in particular, didn’t quite match the elevated tone that omakase typically calls for. The music leaned heavily on rap and other lyrical tracks, which felt a bit jarring in contrast to the refined nature of the food.
Also, while the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, at times they were a bit too present.
The staff often hovered while we took each bite, which made it slightly uncomfortable to react naturally. I understand and appreciate their passion, but a little more space to enjoy the food privately would have made the experience feel more relaxed and less performative.
All in all, Nakama is a must-visit for sushi fans in Philly, and with just a few tweaks to the ambiance and service approach, it could easily reach that next level of fine dining excellence.

Simply the best Omakase in Philadelphia!
The recently opened Nakame Restaurant has owner and long time Philly resident Chef Matsu preparing this wonderful Japanese dining experience for you. He adds his own uniqueness in choices of fish and preparation giving it a surprising delicious culinary twist.
The friendly team members are also big Eagles fans with jerseys and pictures decorating the walls. We will definitely be back!
If Omakase is not for you, the restaurant also serves delicious home made ramen and other dishes.

Staff was friendly and efficient. The waitress tried to unobtrusively pick my wife’s coat back up off the floor.

The food was tremendous. Had elegant miso soup with deep smoky and seaweed flavors

Three told each one tastier than the previous.
Started with a simple shrimp tempura roll but the special sweet and savory sauce added extra to the excellent and fresh shrimp.
Then we enjoyed two specials which took it to another level. We enjoyed the Alaskan roll which combined crab with strips of fresh salmon and spicy mayo.
Then closed with an iggle roll that combined tasty tuna with mango and avocado and garnished with shredded crab meat and spicy mayo and sprouts
customer_insights: Nakama Japanese Cuisines & Omakase offers a unique dining experience with a focus on high-quality sushi and a BYOB policy. While the food is highly praised, some diners noted that the ambiance and service could be improved for a more refined experience.

address: 310 Market St First Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19106, USA
googleReviews:
From start to finish, everything was incredible! Chef Andy was personable and skillful, as was our server. I really couldn't have asked for more! So many different varieties of fish I've never tried before, as well as the best tuna I've ever tried.

The otoro nigiri was legitimately the best piece of sushi I've ever tried. The Canadian lobster was another highlight. Loved that they had Maine as well as Hokkaido Uni, highlighting the different tastes of each. The dessert was an amazing Japanese take on a s'more alongside some super sweet melon.

Absolute pleasure, one of the best meals I've ever had! Reminded me of my time in Japan, but was even better in many ways. The price was very reasonable for the value of the food and experience.

Exquisite. I have so few words for this experience. It was a birthday meal and I had spent a few weeks researching the best Omakase the city has to offer. This restaurant was prominent in social media,but was also featured in the Philadelphia Inquirer that dived into Chef Ogawa’s Michelin recommended restaurant in Washington DC. Raw Fish is very hit or miss for me, and I wanted to give it a proper chance by trying some of the freshest the area has to offer. In this case, many straight from Japan.

Very few of the fish had a strong seawater flavor, instead many were perfect. Some were dry aged, others were brined, and others were braised, all of which exquisitely done. The eel was amazing. The little crabs gave me a fright at first, but was very pleasantly surprised that they did indeed taste and feel in texture just like a potato chip with old bay seasoning. The eel was one of my favorites.

What I will advise is the full beverage pairing, which comes with a highball, Japanese whiskey, and sake tailored for each entree. With Omakase, you’re always taking a bit of a risk that you won’t like something, the definition of it is of course allowing the chef to decide for you. In this case, the success rate was extremely high, enough to justify a visit by someone who sometimes shies away from various fish.

Overall an excellent experience. Wishing everyone well.

I been wanting to come check this place out for a while now. Came here Saturday night with my friend visiting from abroad and hubby to celebrate. It’s a 23 course omakase meal. Everything was so fresh and tasty. Our chef Carlos was amazing and all the servers were very attentive. They constantly came around to fill our sake glasses. My favorite is the tamago egg. It taste like sponge cake it’s so fluffy

My boyfriend and I booked an omakase night here for our anniversary and it was so delightful! The staff and chefs were so friendly and kind, making such great conversations between all of us at the bar. The food was excellent and I didn’t even realize two hours had gone by! Our favorite place for omakase atmosphere-wise!

My wife and I visited this place to celebrate our 19th wedding anniversary, and we couldn’t be in a better restaurant. We were warmly welcomed and very well taken care of by the entire team. The owner “V” even came personally to greet us — such a kind and gracious person. This is definitely a place we’ll recommend to many friends and acquaintances, as the experience was truly wonderful from start to finish.
customer_insights: Ogawa Sushi & Kappo offers an exceptional omakase dining experience with a focus on high-quality, fresh fish and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Ideal for special occasions like anniversaries and first dates, the restaurant is known for its attentive service and unique culinary offerings, making it a standout choice in Philadelphia's dining scene.

venueName: UNI Japanese Cuisine | Japanese, Hibachi & Ramen Restaurant
googleReviews:
Ordered an avocado and cream cheese roll, no cream cheese. Paid extra for fast delivery and even the pickup driver said they took forever in making three cold rolls. Would not recommend the hot dog roll. They also package the ginger with the wasabi in a small container which renders the ginger inedible.

I’ve eaten here in person and it was very nice. Wouldn’t recommend late night delivery.
This place is a hidden gem!! Their food is amazing. My husband and I normally stop by for lunch on Sunday. Unfortunately, they removed their lunch special menu :( which I absolutely love

The hibachi chicken was a solid choice – tender and flavorful, with that classic savory hibachi taste. The salmon mango roll offered a delightful combination of fresh, buttery salmon and the sweet tang of mango. It was a refreshing and well-balanced roll. The spicy tuna sushi rolls delivered a nice kick of heat and had a good texture. As for the sides, the salad was crisp and the dressing was light, a nice palate cleanser. The miso soup was warm and comforting, with a good depth of umami flavor. Overall, Uni offers a satisfying Japanese meal with fresh ingredients and well-prepared dishes.

Absolutely amazing. I can’t believe they were able to hit a home run on every dish with such a robust menu. The sexy girl and south philly roll were 🔥🔥🔥. The chicken udon and hibachi were 10/10. Highly reccomend and will be back. Huge shoutout to our server, Angela, who provide 10/10 service. Her service and the fire food will bring us back!

This place is awesome, my new go-to spot for late night dinner. They have takeout beer, snacks, and you can dine in until 2 am!! I sat at the adorable little bar as soon as you walk in but there’s also plenty of seating in the back of the restaurant. I dined in at 12:30 am & my food came out super fast. Great quality sushi, & you can’t go wrong with ramen.
customer_insights: UNI Japanese Cuisine is a lively and trendy spot in Philadelphia, known for its delicious sushi, hibachi, and ramen. While the late-night delivery service has received mixed reviews, the in-person dining experience is highly praised for its quality food and vibrant atmosphere, making it a great choice for casual outings and late-night meals.

googleReviews:
Ordered the 18-piece premium set and it was incredible. The food is so tasty! The fish had great variety and was balanced really well.

I sat at the bar, and the pieces were served one by one by the sushi chef, which was a nice touch. The environment is cozy and comfortable.

Definitely recommend this spot—it's a real hidden gem.

Forgot a couple of photos but this a must check out place. I had the Tuna Sampler Sushi and Blackened Cod. Both where amazing. The truffle tuna sushi melted in mouth like filet mignon. Good cocktails as well.
Very tasty Sashimi and Sushi. Hamachi Kama is awesome. Hokkaido Uni is definitely the best. Oysters are also fantastic. Deserves 5 star rating.

Went with a group of friends to Shiso a few nights ago, and it was an awesome experience. There were 7 of us and we all ordered the premium chef sushi menu. It hit the mark! A great variety, amazing quality and flavor; and if possible, even better presentation with the sushi chef delivering the sushi piece-by-piece as he made them just a few feet away. One of our group avoids shellfish and the chef happily adjusted the tasting to make it a great night for everyone.

Water glasses and sake carafes were never empty.

Super lovely atmosphere, great service, and tasty sushi!
I generally enjoyed the meal. Service was good. Didn’t have a busy restaurant vibe. Maybe picked a bad time. The bun and the udon stood out to me. Might give it another try
customer_insights: Shiso Noodle and Sushi Bar is praised for its exceptional sushi and cozy atmosphere, making it a great spot for both casual dining and special occasions. The attentive service and unique presentation of dishes enhance the dining experience, appealing to sushi lovers and those looking for a relaxed night out.

googleReviews: My favorite sushi spot of all time! I always pass by here but never had the chance to try. And damn I wish I had gone here earlier. Atmosphere is giving traditional Japanese sheek. The service is impeccable—waiter regularly checking in and I appreciate the food runners explaining each dish without asking to. The yuzu salt endamame was flavorful but a little too salty for my liking (and I love salt). The agadashi salad was great. The king crab roll topped with scallop was amazing! And to think there couldn't be a better roll the crunchy truffle eel wrapped in daikon was THE BEST maki roll I've ever had! It surprisingly blew my expectations. I'm definitely returning to see what the lunch service has to offer.

I found it to be more gimmicky than actually good. The menu is very interesting in theory, but in reality nothing was excellent. Salmon on salmon roll the top was not very pleasant to eat. The extra crunchy is also strange. Calamari salad was very good, but the NY stip steak was quite bad. Service was so-so. I don't think I would visit again.

Zama is an unassuming restaurant right off Rittenhouse Square that has some incredible Japanese cuisine. I came for the first time and had such a great experience!

Started with the lychee cocktail, it wasn’t overly sweet and was strong enough to give me a buzz off one. For an appetizer, I had the udon noodle soup with was salty and rich with umami flavor. It was excellent and I’m going to crave it in the fall & winter!

I also got the salmon and eel fiesta roll. The avocado salsa on top was fresh, the eel bbq sauce added a nice sweetness. Difference textures and flavors all worked together to create a perfect roll.

Peter was our server and he was great. So attentive and helpful with the menu. The restaurant was incredibly clean and well kept, loved the decor. I can’t believe more people aren’t talking about this place - I’ll definitely be back!

We definitely enjoyed dinner at Zama. The food was fresh and high quality. I do wish the seating arrangement was less cluttered. But the food was worth the try. We made a reservation but they let us sit 15 min early.

It had been a good while since I returned to this stalwart center city restaurant and everything was as good as I remembered. The lunch specials still are an amazing deal, with a well-made udon noodle soup, salad, the standard bowl of edamame, and a generous plate of sushi or nigiri.
The atmosphere, with lots of warm wood, is lovely, especially in the back of the restaurant. Small selection of sake, as well as a couple good local craft beers.
customer_insights: Zama is a highly regarded Japanese restaurant known for its fresh sushi and upscale atmosphere. While many patrons rave about the quality of the food and attentive service, some reviews suggest mixed experiences with specific dishes. Overall, it's a great spot for a romantic dinner or special occasion.
