googleReviews:
I tried their Omakase in a group setting, we had a private room and shared plates, so it was a bit different from the smaller group experience. I believe they take reservations for Omakase only. You can also order from their regular à la carte menu as well.

Out of all the dishes, the most memorable ones for me were the fish liver since it’s not a common ingredient, and the mini squids, both of which were delicious. Other than those, I think most of what we had are also available on the regular menu. The chef also came out to prepare hand rolls for us in person, making sure the seaweed stay ed crisp and fresh as we ate.

Just had the most incredible omakase in Philly! The chef is a true artist—every piece of nigiri was perfectly crafted and exploded with flavor. You can really feel his passion and skill. To top it off, the manager was incredibly welcoming and kind, which made the whole evening feel special. This place is a gem. I will definitely be coming back again soon!

Hidden Gem Worth Discovering – Umami Steak & Sushi Bar

A friend was visiting and suggested we try Umami Steak & Sushi Bar—a spot I’d never heard of, surprisingly tucked away in the basement at 7th & Walnut. I must have walked past it countless times without noticing, but I’m glad we gave it a shot. Six of us went in with open minds and left completely impressed.

The verdict: the food was excellent—we’ll definitely be back and happily recommend it to others.

We sampled a wide range of dishes, and here’s what stood out:
•	Karaage – crispy and flavorful
•	Mini Black Cod – surprisingly good for a small plate
•	Grilled Eggplant – another pleasant surprise, deeply savory
•	Salmon Tartare – a favorite of the table
•	Coconut Shrimp Roll – another favorite, unique and delicious
•	Spider Roll – solid, though a bit expected
•	Tuna Avocado Roll – more of a basic filler
•	Surf & Turf Special – not a fan; lacked cohesion and overpriced at $35
•	Koji-Aged Ribeye – incredibly juicy and flavorful
•	Koji-Aged NY Strip – tender and delicious, a standout steak
•	Pan-Seared Salmon – well-cooked and nicely plated

One of the highlights: when you order steak, the chef brings it tableside and slices it in front of you. Great presentation and service touch. The steaks were served with wasabi mashed potatoes—an unexpectedly perfect pairing.

Final takeaway: Umami is a hidden gem worth checking out. If you enjoy creative sushi and top-quality steak, this spot delivers.

Must Visit!!! Alex made us feel very welcome. His warm & genuine character will generate memories. Food was delicious and is prepared using superior quality ingredients. You will definitely enjoy your time spent here. Your tummy will thank you for it.

Fresh fish, perfect steak, and the friendliest staff — a must-try! My boyfriend finally brought me to his favorite sushi + steak spot and wow, I get it now! We were greeted so warmly by Alex and sat at the sushi bar—definitely recommend reservations just in case if you’re coming during peak hours. The 18-course omakase by Chef Kenny was incredible, every piece of fish was perfect, and the porterhouse steak (flamed and cut right in front of us) was cooked to perfection. Add in plum wine, green tea ice cream, friendly staff, and a great vibe… easily one of the best meals I’ve had. This is definitely our go to sushi and/or steak spot. We’ll absolutely be back!
customer_insights: Umami Steak and Sushi Bar offers a unique dining experience with a focus on high-quality sushi and steak. The atmosphere is upscale and trendy, making it suitable for various occasions, from first dates to girls' nights out. Guests rave about the omakase experience and the attentive service, particularly praising the chef's skill and the welcoming staff.

address: 146 N 10th St floor 2, Philadelphia, PA 19107, USA
googleReviews:
Made a spontaneous stop at this Nori shop and we were impressed from the quality of the hand rolls, sake selections to the friendly service.

It was like watching an art piece to be crafted while sitting by the sushi bar having the chef  piece together the hand rolls.

Price is not cheap but you get what you pay for, the portions are generous and I got full after 3 rolls. I am sure others can eat more than me, but 3 is my max 😂

Intimacy atmosphere, nicely decorated with semi automatic Izakaya vibe. Clean seatings. A great place to enjoy some quality rolls with refreshing sake.

Highly recommend by @WineDinenVacay

Genuinely one the best meals I’ve ever had. You have to try this! If you like umami and savory sushi that melts in your mouth you have to come here. My favorite was the miso cod and salmon and truffle edamame. And for the quality and experience, it is so reasonably priced. It’s like a humble version of omakase but just as delicious. I’m still thinking about this meal!!!

Overall really good food! I loved all the different handrolls I ordered, everything tasted fresh 🍣. They also stuff them full with filling!! It’s a handroll bar so all the seating is at the counter where they make it right in front of you. There was a bit of a wait since it’s first come first serve with no reservations. My only complaint is the service felt a bit rushed, so docking a star for that, but still worth trying! I would come back as this seems like a really great handroll place in Philly!

Initially very excited to try a handroll spot but unfortunately our experience was very underwhelming. Right when you walk in, you’re confused whether or not you should seat yourself or wait to be seated. No host/hostess to be found, just the sushi chefs at the bar. After a few minutes, the host appeared and asked if we were doing hotpot or sushi and seated us. Server came by with hot sake and I thought it was on the house but everyone was confused because nobody ordered it so we waited for a few minutes until the server came by and apologized that it wasn’t for us and then they gave it to another table. Not very sanitary because if we touched it, it could have been an issue. $6 for steamed egg, it’s not bad. Egg was silky smooth topped with the ikura sauce. The salmon cups were the highlight of the meal. Spicy salmon with a truffle topping, would recommend this as a starter. Mind you $10 for a handroll, you would expect good quality and or good quantity. Ordered the snow cali roll and they gave a sliver of crab meat. Could not taste any other ingredient besides the tamago. The miso cod was sweet and soft. Spicy shrimp tempura was mid. I bit into it halfway and it looked undercooked and grey. Spicy yellowtail had finely minced yellowtail that resembled chicken and it did not look very appealing. Had a difficult time trying to bite into the seaweed as it was not tearing like it should. Waited for a server over 10 minutes to be checked out. Had to get up to find someone. Overall, if you’re going to charge $10 for a handroll, atleast have a good amount of filling or ingredients should stand out. You won’t get chubby at Chubby Nori, you’re gonna leave starving.

The restaurant has an amazing atmosphere! The miso butter cod, eel, and blue crab is soooo goood. I personally recommend the spicy shrimp tempura. I really like how they put lemon in their water to make it taste better. It is a must-visit spot
customer_insights: Chubby Nori offers a unique handroll experience with a focus on quality and freshness. While some reviews praise the intimate atmosphere and generous portions, others express concerns about service and consistency. Overall, it's a trendy spot ideal for casual dining and special occasions.

googleReviews:
Bleu Sushi might be one of my favorite cozy sushi restaurants now in Philly. Me and my boyfriend came here at night and when we first walked in it was very beautiful — the ambiance was so nice and the waiters were very attentive.

Our starters was the torched white tuna with crispy garlic and we also got the shrimp & veggie appetizer. For the white tuna I would say that dish itself wasn’t worth it. It really just tasted like a balsamic glaze on tuna. It wasn’t an “Japanese” flavor — the dish itself felt/tasted more American. (Something you would put on a salad). Nonetheless it was decent. The tempura app was actually very good. The portion is nice and we were almost full before even ordering our mains!
We got the Orange Lover & Sushi Bleu — both were very good and tasted fresh we saw the chefs making our dish which was nice.
The staff was very attentive and very classy. I loved everything about the aesthetics, food, and service.

The sushi was good, but the entrees were just ordinary. The place is nice and dimly lighted. The food is a bit too pricey for me. If it’s not because of the groupon promotion, I would not give it a try.

I’ve gotta say, this place is awesome. I walked in not really knowing what to expect, and they absolutely crushed it.

The vibe is relaxed, the food comes out fast, and everyone working there is super friendly. Jonah was amazing, genuinely welcoming, and just made the whole experience feel even better. You can tell he really cares about the customers.

And the sushi? AMAZING.
Everything was insanely fresh, the fish was buttery and flavorful, and the rolls were made perfectly. Even the simple stuff tasted elevated. Their specialty rolls are fun, creative, and honestly some of the best I’ve had.

Prices are reasonable, portions are great, and the whole spot just hits all the right notes.

If you love sushi, you’ll be obsessed. If you’re on the fence, this place will convert you.
Huge shout-out to Jonah, can’t wait to come back! 🍣🙌

Had an awesome time here! The sushi was top quality, super clean flavors, great texture, and you could tell everything was really fresh. I tried a few different rolls and every single one hit the mark.
Jonah was a huge part of why the experience was so good. He’s incredibly welcoming and really knows his way around the menu. His recommendations were spot-on, and he made the whole visit feel relaxed and enjoyable.
Definitely a place I’d come back to, and Jonah is absolutely someone you want taking care of you.

Food delicious, service was great (server was very kind, informative, and funny). Dumplings were fantastic, all be it small in portion but I’d definitely order them again. Sushi prices and portions were fantastic! We went on a double date w friends and would happily come back. Their mochi dessert was also delicious. Super fun, great music/atmosphere (just tight space) but overall some of the best sushi I’ve had in Philly since moving here in July!
customer_insights: Bleu Sushi is praised for its cozy ambiance, attentive service, and high-quality sushi. While some dishes may feel more American than traditional Japanese, the overall experience is enhanced by friendly staff and a relaxed atmosphere, making it suitable for various occasions.

googleReviews: Tried the all you can eat option. It’s only available Tuesday to Friday. The sushi we chose were good, just that the waiting was a bit long for the second order. I suggest ordering a lot at once if you’re sure you are able to finish all. There were only 2 servers while the tables were mostly occupied. I don’t really like the ambience since it’s not bright enough. Overall was satisfying.

Excellent downtown Rittenhouse area Japanese restaurant that has BENTO box dinners. Most places only have bento for lunch. The interior is super cool modern and exciting. Service was excellent. And the price... yes, the price for a bento was awesome!  We enjoyed our bentos and got out of there without breaking the bank for dinner.  Thank you!

Ordered lunch from Samurai today via Uber Eats and it was delicious! I had the three sushi rolls lunch special and a chicken katsu cutlet special (I’m a hungry guy what can I say?).

For the rolls I ordered the Striped Bass (YUM!), salmon (fresh and tasty and big ol chunks!) and boston (ay big and tasty shrimp!). The portion on the Chicken Katsu was large! Got to save most of that for dinner.

Definitely want to stop by with a group and go for that AYCE sushi special and get a karaoke room! I’ll be stopping by in person sometime soon. Until then, I highly recommend ordering for lunch, especially if theres an Uber promotion going on. The Katsu was $12, and I had a 50% off lunch coupon that stacked. I will order again regardless of if there’s a promotion or not though, it was that good! Thank you Samurai! 🙏

We did take out.. this was the worst sushi I’ve ever had. The fish tasted old and the added cream cheese in a roll was worrisome… why would you put a large glob of cream cheese in a sushi roll. Waste of money.

We tried the all-you-can-eat menu, available from Tuesday to Friday for $27. It includes a mix of sashimi and sushi, both fried and regular.
The tempura shrimp was fresh, and the salmon sashimi was very fresh, though limited to 5 pieces per person. The service was quick, and the staff were nice and professional.
My only suggestion is to have a pictured menu to help customers who may not know the ingredients, but other than that, I’d definitely recommend this place.
customer_insights: Samurai Japanese Restaurant offers a casual dining experience with a focus on sushi and bento boxes. The all-you-can-eat option is popular, especially for groups looking for a fun night out, though service can be slow during busy times. Overall, it's a trendy spot in the Rittenhouse area, ideal for a lively dinner with friends.

address: 2146 E Susquehanna Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19125, USA
googleReviews: If it’s your first omakase experience then you’ll like it. If you’ve had more expensive omakase before, then this one doesn’t really have the same experience factor. The quality of the fish was good but it was fast(less than 1h) and felt rushed. The sushi chef didn’t really explain anything other than state the obvious name of the fish. But it’s good for the price.
The Omakase was perfect!! The food, the service, the energy was so good! I definitely recommend this place. The Lychee Sake was delicious 🤤 Already want to go back

Came with all intentions of trying handrolls for the first time! and I was not disappointed.

This was my first "raw" seafood experience and I'm so happy I came to Yuhiro for that experience. The food was so intricately crafted that it all worked SO well with each other. The hot tea was delicious and so were the rolls!

The restaurant has a sleek and comfortable design and offers a sushi experience unlike most others in the city. The sushi comes with instructions, and at first I thought I didn’t need them— but it turned out to have some great tips for different kind of sushi rolls. The staff was also knowledgeable and helpful.

Especially now that Fishtown Izakaya has lost its liquor license, this is now my go to spot for sushi and sake.

Tip— go on Sunday for 20% off almost the whole menu. Try it, you won’t regret it.

My first omakase experience couldn’t have been at a better restaurant. This place offers 13 courses for $78 with ice cream dessert. Each piece was carefully cultivated for a homogenous flavor profile. The uni was a bit too mushy for my liking, but I am not the biggest fan of uni to begin with. The ikura was so fresh, no fishiness whatsoever. They also torched most of the fish including the salmon, which I feel I would have enjoyed better raw. I did feel like I was being rushed to eat quick even though we were given 90 minutes for the omakase experience. We were done with all courses in an hour. We had a 5pm reservation, which worked well for us as the restaurant was fairly empty for this reservation time. Parking is a bit difficult to find, but street parking is free.
happy_hour_details: 20% off almost the whole menu on Sundays
customer_insights: Yuhiro Omakase Sushi offers a unique sushi experience with a focus on omakase dining. While some reviews mention a rushed experience, the quality of the fish and the overall ambiance are praised, making it a great spot for sushi lovers, especially on Sundays for discounts.

address: 251 N Clarion St, Philadelphia, PA 19107, USA
googleReviews: The food was prepared to my satisfaction and was full of flavor. The atmosphere is vibrant and instantly transported me back to my visit to Osaka a few years ago. While the service was average and unremarkable, the unique design of the entrance stood out — understated and discreet, giving the impression the venue is closed. However, any seasoned foodie would recognize and appreciate the intentionality behind such a design choice.
Very nice authentic Japanese restaurant. We had takoyaki, sushi set, shrimp tempura roll, edamame and tonkotsu ramen. I think these were the best takoyaki I’ve ever had, in Japan or elsewhere.

Kirins House Restaurant has a very nice atmosphere and the staff was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. We started with Edemame and the Dragon Fire roll. They were fresh and tasty. My husband had  the Burning  roll for his entree and I had the bento box with chicken and broccoli. My box had two sides of spring roll and gyoza.

Visited from NYC—so I eat a lot of good sushi. This place is phenomenal! The drinks, the apps, and the specialty rolls are so fresh and yummy. There’s a roll for everyone, and plenty of platters for larger groups too. Not to be missed if you’re in Philly!

Food was amazing. I ordered the dragon roll I believe but it was a sushi burrito. Difficult to eat but still tasty!
Service was mediocre. I would have loved another blueberry lemon drop, it was phenomenal! But the server dropped our food and never returned. Had to ask for my check after her walking by without checking on us during the entire dinner.
customer_insights: Kirin House offers a vibrant atmosphere reminiscent of authentic Japanese dining experiences. While the food receives high praise for its freshness and flavor, service can be hit or miss, making it a great spot for casual outings with friends or a fun date night.

address: 2146 S Broad St, Philadelphia, PA 19145, USA
googleReviews: A gem in south philly and definitely the best sushi in the area. Super friendly service, always easy to get a table, and BYOB is a plus. The salmon lover's sushi entree is my go-to and is accompanied by a salad and soup. Haven't been disappointed with any of the rolls - always the perfect rice-to-fish ratio and all of the ingredients are super fresh.

Stuffed Jalapeños with tuna. Incredible.
Spicy Tuna hand roll was huge. Delicious.
Everyone’s meal looked amazing and they all said it was.
Very good service.
BYOB so come prepared if you choose to.

I am trying to upload photos for this review as proof for my experience on 04/13/25. I love sushi, so I was standing outside reading the menu posted on the window. The atmosphere of the restaurant looked nice, so I spent $39.37 on the mango roll, miso soup (tastes okay), and pineapple fried rice with chicken and shrimp (tastes good). I was so excited, I ate the mango/caviar off the top because it looked so pretty and that tasted delicious. Then I separated the roll and I became nervous about the appearance of the salmon and tuna rolls. Against my better judgment I ate them and now I'm not feeling well. Anything for a buck, they should be shut down. I won't bother going back to contest this, but I do believe in warning other potential customers. Although the restaurant looked nice, I should have paid attention to the fact the restaurant was empty.🤦🏽‍♀️

I’ve been wanting to come check this place out for a while and finally able to stop by today on a Saturday for lunch. They have lunch specials from Monday to Saturday until 3pm. It’s reasonable priced so come give them a try. I had the lunch bento with the steak hibachi. The steak was a bit overcooked to my liking and a bit on the chewy side. But it is well seasoned. You also get a soup or salad with the lunch combo. Our server was very friendly and attentive. She came by a couple times to check up on us. I would definitely come back to this place

Love this BYOB spot in South Philly. Quality food, service and very reasonable cost. Although I’ve moved out of the area I regularly take the drive to patronize this spot even over the local and more “upscale” venues  in my area.  5 Stars all around!
customer_insights: Kiku Sushi is a beloved BYOB sushi spot in South Philadelphia, known for its fresh ingredients and friendly service. While the atmosphere is casual and suitable for groups or dates, some reviews indicate inconsistency in food quality. Overall, it's a great choice for sushi lovers looking for a relaxed dining experience.

googleReviews: A good neighborhood spot; we were able to do a walk in! The specialty rolls section is definitely the place to go! Sushi came out super quick! Very tasty sushi, the rice and fish were both fresh! The garlic ramen was wicked tasty, they had asked if I wanted spicy and I said yes, but it wasn’t very spicy, would have preferred them to give me chili oil so that I could have dosed it myself. Unfortunately, the server was no where to be found when I was eating the ramen and wanting more chili oil; nonetheless, the broth was incredibly savory, the noodles were perfectly thin and a heavy portion! The egg was perhaps a bit overcooked, but otherwise went well with the dish! Great spot to visit and seems like they do quite a bit of take out as well!

Very fresh and tasty sushi! Make sure to try their spicy mayo on the side with the sushi!! A bit cramped inside for sitting down but they now have a second side where there are more private booths. Would not recommend sitting at the 2 persons sitting arrangements. But other than that, amazing food and service!

Tried this cozy spot for the first time in September 2025 and had a great experience. The servers are detailed and thorough, the food comes out SUPER quick and is delish! Would def recommend for a pre-show meal at the Arden or FringeArts.
Tomo has the best vegan ramen I have had in the city. Their prices recently increased but are still affordable. The vibe is intimate and interesting. I have never been disappointed by a dish :)

This restaurant was on my list of places to try and  it was worth the wait. They have options for mixed diets. I’m vegan and my friend isn’t.

Had a little mishap with which door to go in for the sit down restaurant. There were people eating at tables on the side that was apparently designated for take out. It took a while for someone to come and acknowledge us to tell us to go to the other door to see the hostess to dine in.

Once we got to the other side we were seated promptly and the service was great. I ordered the avocado salad, veggie on fire and harvest rolls. My friend ordered the spicy tuna and rainbow rolls.

The food was delicious! I tore that avocado salad up. The rolls were yummy and filling. We both took some to go and ate them the next day. The rolls kept just fine.

I will definitely be back and now know which door to go to.
customer_insights: Tomo Sushi & Ramen is a cozy neighborhood spot known for its fresh sushi and flavorful ramen. The venue is suitable for casual dining and pre-show meals, making it a great choice for groups or a relaxed date night.

address: Hidden Inside of Yanaga Kappo Izakaya, 637 N 3rd St, Philadelphia, PA 19123, USA
neighborhood: Hidden Inside of Yanaga Kappo Izakaya, 637 N 3rd St, Philadelphia
googleReviews:
Had an absolutely incredible omakase experience with Chef Kevin and the entire team at 637 Supper Club. The food was phenomenal from start to finish—fresh, thoughtful, beautifully executed, and truly memorable. The service was just as impressive: warm, attentive, and perfectly paced, making the whole evening feel special and effortless.

Thank you to Chef Kevin and the team for delivering such an amazing experience. I’m already looking forward to coming back and enjoying some great fish with all of you again.

We had such a wonderful time at 637 Philly Sushi Club. Chef Yanaga is an absolute delight, engaging, fun, and clearly passionate about his craft. The menu was thoughtful and creative, with a sake pairing that felt both special and intentional. Service was flawless from start to finish, attentive without being intrusive.

The first bite, mochi and Brie wrapped in seaweed, was pure magic and something I’ll think about for a long time. The amuse bouche trio of shrimp, tuna, and oyster shooter was another standout moment, each executed beautifully and setting the tone for an exciting meal ahead.

While the experience was overall fantastic, a few details kept it from being a perfect five stars. The scallop in the chawanmushi was unfortunately overcooked to the point of being unrecognizable, the miso soup with tiny shrimp leaned a bit too fish forward for my taste, and the pastry to foie ratio in one bite featuring a pastry cup felt slightly off because there was too much pastry tart. The cheesecake also didn’t quite live up to the rest of the meal’s high points.

Even with those small misses, the creativity, quality, and service made for an exceptional night out. We left happy, impressed, and already talking about coming back soon. 4.5 stars.

I just had an exceptional meal here last night and I’m already dying for more. This marked my 3rd omakase experience and I can easily say without a doubt it was The Best. The atmosphere was welcoming and relaxed, being there really makes it feel like you’re a part of something special and more intimate. The food was also of course, Outstanding. It feels impossible to narrow down a favorite, as every part of the menu flowed together perfectly. The standouts were definitely the otoro + caviar, the amuse bouche, and arctic char bozushi. We were also served the best dessert I’ve had to end an omakase with. The food stood out on its own but it was made even better by Chef Kevin Yanaga. His humor and love for his craft is was really sealed the deal on making this an unforgettable meal. I could not recommend this experience enough, and if it’s not in the budget, I also so highly recommend YKI itself. 637 Sushi Club gets a 1 million out of 10 from me!

Incredibly special 8 seat omakase hidden inside Yanaga Kappo Izakaya restaurant! Chef Kevin spoiled us with incredible quality fish and seafood (plus some wagyu and foie gras mixed in). We had over 10 creative small plates and 11 pieces of beautiful crafted nigiri with some unique toppings. I felt it was an excellent value at 150 per person for the amount and quality of food you get. Sushi snobs, be aware that the fish for nigiri was sliced before we arrived. I found the fish to be excellent and not dried out but I know some would clutch their pearls at that. The menu attached doesn’t include some special extra dishes we received like a wagyu and toro sandwich. We also were given inari sushi to take home as well as cookies along with the menu.

One of the best parts was chatting with Chef Kevin who is very friendly and funny. I really appreciated how happy he seemed to be to answer any questions you might have about any dish after he presents it. We’ve had a few omakase experiences where the chef barely tells you what you’re eating and this was much more fun and interactive. The service was also excellent! The waiter taking care of us always had water glasses filled or if you ever needed another drink.

For drinks, they have a sake pairing as well as lots of options like cocktails, mocktails, cider, beer from the bar at the izakaya restaurant. We came a little early so we could grab a drink at the bar and when it was time for our reservation, the hostess grabbed us and showed us to the hidden room for 636 Philly Sushi Club.

I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this experience, which takes around 2.5 hrs, to anyone who loves sushi!

I had the absolute best omakase experience at 637 Philly Sushi Club, and as a complete novice to omakase, I couldn’t have felt more welcome. From the moment we sat down, Chef Yanga and our server Nick made us feel like we were settling in at a friend’s kitchen counter. They took their time explaining each course, sharing how to enjoy the meal in a traditional way, and made what could have been a stuffy or overly “ritzy” experience feel warm, inviting, and genuinely fun.

The food itself was incredible—creative, thoughtful, and prepared with real intention. Every bite felt purposeful. I’m still dreaming about the prawn course.

The space also adds so much to the experience. You literally walk through a bookshelf to enter, and once inside, the shelves behind the counter are filled with personal items from the chef’s son, gifts from past diners, and collectibles from chefs who recognize the quality of his craft. It makes the whole night feel unique, intimate, and meaningful.

For the quality of the food and the personalized experience, the price is more than fair—easily one of the most reasonable omakase options in the city.

One last recommendation: have a drink at the bar beforehand. The staff is incredibly friendly, the cocktails are creative and delicious, and it’s the perfect way to set the tone for an unforgettable night.

I can’t recommend this place highly enough.
customer_insights: 637 Philly Sushi Club offers an exceptional omakase dining experience, characterized by high-quality, thoughtfully prepared dishes and a warm, inviting atmosphere. Guests rave about the engaging chefs and the intimate setting, making it ideal for special occasions like dates and anniversaries.

googleReviews:
Stumbled upon Shinto after a quick business meeting and decided to stop in—turns out it was their Grand Opening! Funny enough, I had just been talking about sushi the day before, so it felt like perfect timing.

The service was great—friendly, attentive, and welcoming. The decor is super cute, creating a comfortable atmosphere. I ordered the shrimp tempura and an avocado cucumber roll, along with a side salad. Everything was fresh, well-prepared, and delicious.

A lovely surprise find!

Run, don't walk to this place before everyone finds out about it and the line is down the street! They've only been open about three months and it is just what this area needed. They can only seat 14 people But the service is attentive and the ambience is wonderful. Best of all the food is fresh and delicious and everything is made to order. I'm so excited to be able to walk here from my place. And of course they are on all of the food delivery apps. Highly recommended!

Moved next door and so happy to see a Japanese restaurant just opened! Very impressed with all our food. The gyoza is fantastic and not heavy at all, so is the chicken & shrimp tempura. The yaki udon and the spicy edamame was excellent. I got the crispy rice with the spicy tuna and I will be back for more. The portions are perfectly sized for the prices. The service is good as well.
Incredibly fresh. We had edamame, miso soup, sashimi, Godzilla roll, and Santa roll. They were all amazing.

Got a large take-out party tray of assorted sushi for a birthday celebration. There was a good mix of fishes. We enjoyed this.

The restaurant is small but would be a nice spot to grab a quick solo lunch.
customer_insights: Shinto Japanese Sushi & Hibachi is a newly opened restaurant that has quickly gained popularity for its fresh and delicious sushi offerings. The intimate setting, with only 14 seats, provides a cozy atmosphere perfect for casual dining or a quick lunch. Customers rave about the attentive service and quality of food, making it a great spot for both solo visits and group gatherings.

googleReviews: A staple in Philly sushi scene - consistent quality and flavors. Service always good. Good variety of your usual and a nice twist to some old favorites. Ordered the gyoza soup, tuna ceviche, a la carte sushi. Street parking good throughout on Sunday and is free.

Visited at 5 pm on a Sunday and was the only person in the restaurant. Definitely not a super packed establishment. Was a little disappointed that they did not serve chicken karaage. Popcorn gyoza were delicious in flavor but left a little hue of grease behind on the plate! They were bite size and delete-able. Kamikase roll was incredibly tasty and fresh but rice fell apart as soon as it touched soy sauce. I would imagine that the rolls were not packed down very tightly. Kamikase roll was far better thank the inferno roll, kamikaze had far better textures paired with stronger flavors of shrimp and tobiko. Otherwise service was very good and they were very attentive.

We had a lovely dinner here recently, as my husband was craving sushi for his birthday. The service was good and the sushi was top notch. We also ordered a bottle of sake and some beers to go with our meal. The place was pretty empty, so we had the upstairs basically entirely to ourselves. The quietness may have bothered some other folks, but we enjoyed the private dining experience. I would definitely come here again!

The food here never disappoints. Always fresh and hot. We tried the crispy chicken and shrimp 🍤 this time around and it was really delicious 😋. Of you're in the area and are in the mood.for some tasty Japanese food, give them a try! P.s. the calamari is awesome 👌
Service was kinda slow (maybe they were short-staffed?), but they accommodated my request to move to a booth.  The decor is cozy. Atmosphere is casual.  The food was excellent.  I would recommend.
customer_insights: Fuji Mountain Japanese Restaurant is a cozy and casual dining spot known for its fresh sushi and attentive service. While it may not be bustling, it offers a quiet atmosphere suitable for intimate dinners or special occasions like birthdays and anniversaries.

googleReviews: Great food overall! We ordered a little bit of everything and most of it really hit the spot. The chicken katsu curry was divine and the spicy tuna rice crispy was even better. The kaarage fried chicken was delicious and perfectly cooked. Yki fries were pretty addicting. The blistered shishito peppers were nice and simple. The only thing I wasn’t crazy about was the veggie sando. Service was great so it’s definitely worth a visit.

My third time back and Yanaga, and it didn't disappoint! I love the mini tasting they offer - such a great deal since I can't always spring for the full omakase. The sushi is fresh and delicious, the cocktails are creative and complex, and the happy hour deals are so worth it! I tried the wagyu hot dog for the first time and even though I came there for the raw fish, that was a standout menu item for me.
The ambiance is laid back and fun, never pretentious. The waitresses and friendly and knowledgeable and never made me feel rushed.
I already can't wait to be back!

Yanaga Kappo-Izakaya has a cool, kitschy vibe with anime, wall art, and neon decor. The sushi is creative (Northern Libs Trio) but also offers standard cut hand rolls as well. A good selection of drinks (sake juice box!) and mocktails. The soft serve green tea ice cream was a nice ending to our meal. Next time, we'll try the omakase. A unique choice for Japanese food if you're in Philly.

We’ve been multiple times for omakase, the regular dining room, and takeout and have never been anything less than delighted. The food is fresh, imaginative, and absolutely delicious - from sushi to larger entrees. Cocktails and sake selection are also 10/10. Such a great addition to the NoLibs restaurant scene!

LOVED dining here! Casual spot with great service. We made a reservation and were glad we did as almost every table was full.
The cocktail list has some interesting drinks on it and we enjoyed what the server recommended. We had four dishes and were full by the time we left. We started with the shishito peppers and gyoza and the portions were good and gyoza was some of the best I’ve ever had. Ponzu butter roll was very large and simple but great as well. We ended with the hibachi rice and it was a good portion for two people to split plus tasty as it’s made with duck fat!
Will definitely be back here again and hear they have a great happy hour!
customer_insights: Yanaga Kappo Izakaya offers a vibrant and casual dining experience with a diverse menu that includes both traditional and creative sushi options. The atmosphere is friendly and laid-back, making it suitable for various social outings, from casual dinners to pregame gatherings.

googleReviews:
It’s a great spot to go with friends or family because cooking at the table makes the experience fun and interactive. Just a heads up it gets really hot around the grill.
Most of the food we ordered was really good.

The things I didn’t love were the fried chicken bites (the texture felt strange and the inside looked a bit purple) and the ramen the broth just wasn’t for me. But that might be personal preference.

Besides that, everything else was good, and I still think it’s worth going at least once for the experience. It’s a nice place to try with a group and enjoy the grill style cooking.

It’s a great spot for Japanese style food. The calamari appetizer is amazing. You can find good sake and drinks with hotpot and bbqs. The service was a bit slow with some of the items and bar area unavailable.

We did all you can eat and the service was quick and great. Nice waiters. Atmosphere can be better though as it was really hot inside the restaurant especially the last room where there's actually no AC, so they kindly seated us somewhere else. They should  have a better AC system esp with all the grills plus kitchen in the restaurant. Meat qualities were pretty good (marinated ones were bit too sweet for my liking) but we got the boba ice cream mochi dessert, and the texture was really abnormal/dry/crumbly that a mochi should not be. Tbh I'm pretty sure that mochi ice cream was around 5 years old judging by the texture and how the mochi just fell apart after taking a bite. I know it's a meat restaurant so who cares about the dessert but we were really turned off by it at the end of our meal.

I went with a group of 6 and we ordered the set menu for 6 to make the check easier and also so we didn't have to make as many decisions. The menu is LARGE. They did let us swap the pork and shrimp for chicken and beef to accommodate dietary restrictions in the group which was nice of them. We were sat in the back dining area, sharing the space with a VERY large party, which was unfortunate because it was incredibly loud as a result. But it was the only open table big enough for our group so they weren't able to move us. Several couples came in to be sat at the remaining table and asked to be relocated and they were, so if they have the space they'll accommodate that sort of request. It was also very warm with all the grills on so wear removable layers.
They tell you how long each dish should be cooked on each side when they bring the plate out, which was helpful, but we absolutely had no idea which cut of beef was which so couldn't tell you which ones I would or wouldn't recommend from the selection we had. The chicken was harder to get to the right doneness versus the beef though so I probably wouldn't get that one in the future. No one seemed to be a fan of the soup either but it was still worth it to get the set menu, next time I might ask if the soup could be exchanged for more salad or edamame instead. Ending the meal with smores was also a fun touch.

Staff were attentive and quick to refill side dishes and drinks. They offered grilling tips for first-timers, which made the experience smooth and enjoyable, The setting was clean and cozy, with a sleek grill at each table. Soft lighting perfect for groups or date night. If you don’t finish the meat they charge additional but overall great experience
customer_insights: Gyu-Kaku Japanese BBQ offers a lively and interactive dining experience, perfect for groups looking to enjoy table-side grilling. While the atmosphere can get quite warm and some dishes may not meet everyone's taste, the overall experience is fun and engaging, making it a great spot for casual outings with friends or family.

googleReviews:
I went with a group of 6. The service was wonderful and they were very sweet about us all coming in at different times and not making us wait to sit til the whole party arrived.
The presentation of the food was so pretty. The stoplight roll in particular is so bright and fun. Their rolls are very non-traditional so be prepared for that. I do enjoy the creativity but it's not the best sushi I've had.
Pictured is what I ordered: the crispy rice tot (you get a single piece per order, which the server did warn us about, which was nice of her) and 3 rolls, the ping pong, eternal sunshine, and spicy tuna.
Overall an enjoyable time and worth the visit.

The food here is amazing and is prepared perfectly. The manager/Our server (Geordie) was also absolutely amazing from the time you make the reservation to the moment you leave the restaurant.  The oyster shooters  are a must-try and the sushi rolls we got (krakken, traffic light, and ping pong from left to right in the picture below) were all amazing but the traffic light was indeed my favorite.  We also got the seafood paella and the pad Thai, both of which were very tasty! I've been here twice and will definitely be here again!

The rolls were excellent for the price point. The fish to rice ratio was good. The fish tasted fresh, had good flavor and texture. The waitress was extremely rude to us very shortly after we arrived and inquired about a table for three. Rather than simply specifying a wait time, she snapped that it would be "a long time" and then told us to sit at the bar. There were three open tables the entire time we were at the restaurant.

The restaurant is cute and cozy! The food was great, I’ve never had a better vegetable roll. Only issue is my waitress was so rude, I understand she was probably stressed because it was busy but she was very blunt and talked with us as if she was annoyed. She came to our table very slow and rushed us each time. I had to go to ask for a wine opener and she responded in an annoyed tone “it should just be on your table did you check?” Then proceeded to not come back

Recommended.
Beautiful & Delicious Cuisine.
Nice Ambiance, Friendly Staffs.
♥️🌟
customer_insights: Umai Umai offers a trendy and cozy atmosphere with a focus on creative sushi rolls and Asian fusion dishes. While the food presentation and flavor are generally praised, service experiences can vary, with some guests noting issues with staff demeanor during busy times.

googleReviews:
Beautiful way to spend an evening!

We went for the Omakase meal and it was absolutely phenomenal. Everything was prepared in front of you by the chef and each bite was delicious and delicate. By the end of the extensive menu (about 15 courses!) we were pleasantly full and we couldn’t stop talking about it.

The cocktails were very good as well. We most enjoyed the jasmine and matcha tea cocktail. We also asked for their recommendation on sake which was a wonderful pairing with the sushi courses. It is pricey but well worth it for special occasions.

My wife is gluten free and allergic to uni, and the chef and kitchen took special care to create full replacement dishes and keep her items separate as needed. They took such care!

Third time’s the charm — and Kissho House just keeps getting better.

I made my third trip to Kissho House last night and finally got to try their new Artisan DIY Platter. Let me just say—it did not disappoint. For $79, this platter is an absolute steal. You get to build your own hand rolls exactly how you like them, with super fresh fish and a beautiful spread of ingredients. It’s interactive, fun, and honestly, it feels like a mini culinary event.

The platter also comes with a comforting bowl of miso soup that just warms you up from the inside. Everything about the experience felt thoughtful.

I also added an extra order of uni still as sweet and delicate as I remember from previous visits. So fresh and satisfying.

Their cocktails were very good too ！ highly recommend.

We came here for dinner with my kids tonight, and it was an absolutely perfect experience!！As a parent, finding a restaurant that genuinely pleases both adults and children can be tough, but this Japanese restaurant hit it out of the park.

My kids absolutely LOVED the sushi!They couldn't get enough – it was incredibly fresh, beautifully presented, and tasted authentic. Seeing them enjoy their food so much (and ask for more!) was fantastic. Even my pickier eater was completely won over.

Beyond the amazing sushi, the entire meal was excellent. The atmosphere was welcoming and comfortable for a family, and the service was attentive and friendly throughout our visit. Everything flowed smoothly from the moment we sat down.

this place. It truly made for a wonderful, stress-free, and delicious dinner out with the family. We left feeling happy, satisfied, and will definitely be back!

A fantastic Omakase experience. Chef Jeff is very friendly and professional. The menu is different every day, determined by the chef. The arrangement of the menu has been carefully designed. Transport new fish four days a week from Japan and Spain. The ingredients are fresh. Sea urchins and crab meat are not fishy. The preparation of sushi is very thoughtful.

A small suggestion, it would be even better if a hot seafood soup could replace the misso soup nearly the end of the meal.

Absolutely fantastic dining experience! From the moment we walked in, we were impressed by the elegant and cozy atmosphere — the perfect setting for a relaxing evening. The food was outstanding; every dish was beautifully presented and bursting with flavor, especially the skewers and the fresh sashimi bowl. The salmon tartare with chips was also a creative and delicious touch! The service was impeccable — friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable staff who made us feel genuinely welcome. Highly recommended, and definitely a place I’ll be coming back to!
customer_insights: Kissho House offers an exceptional dining experience with a focus on omakase and sushi, making it perfect for special occasions and family outings. Guests rave about the attentive service, fresh ingredients, and the interactive nature of the dining experience, particularly with their DIY platter.

address: 330 Goddard Blvd, King of Prussia, PA 19406, USA
googleReviews:
I recently dined at this Japanese hibachi restaurant and was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The atmosphere was warm, modern, and sophisticated—perfect for a night out with friends or a cozy date night.

The food overall was good, with fresh ingredients and solid flavor. The standout for me was definitely the yum yum sauce—it added the perfect touch to every bite and had me going back for more!

Service was friendly and attentive, contributing to an enjoyable dining experience. However, I did notice that our chef wasn’t very mindful when it came to distributing the food among the guests at our table. It wasn’t a major issue, but a little more balance would have made the meal feel more complete.

All in all, it’s a great spot with good food and a welcoming vibe. I’d go back, especially for another helping of that yum yum sauce!

PS- I heard the chicken nuggets were amazing.

Shay’s Steaks: A Rare Kindness & an Unforgettable Experience

I visited Shay’s Steaks yesterday, and it was truly something special. Scott, the owner, reminded me that kindness is rare, and when you feel it, you don’t forget it. He walked over, placed his hand on my shoulder, and welcomed me like we’d known each other for years. That level of hospitality is unmatched.

The food? Outstanding.
Prime meats delivered fresh daily — never frozen — cooked to order, paired with perfectly fresh-cut fries. You can literally taste the quality and the pride.

Then Scott took things to another level:
He brought out a whole s’mores kit and made s’mores for every customer. 😂🔥

And in memory of his parents, who created this establishment many years ago, he blessed everyone with free fries and drinks. That gesture speaks volumes about the legacy he continues.

Blessings to him, the memory of his family, and the establishment they built.
In a world where kindness is rare, places like Shay’s Steaks remind you it still exists.

If you’re in the Philly area — visitor or local — do yourself a favor and stop by. Highly recommended.

🔥 Behind the Grill at Shay’s Steaks 🔥

When passion meets the griddle — magic happens.
Freshly sliced steaks, sizzling onions, and layers of melted cheese — the real deal Philly cheesesteak experience. No shortcuts. No frozen meat. Just craftsmanship, flavor, and heat.

I had the chance to step behind the counter with the founder Scott at Shay’s Steaks, where every sandwich is truly custom-crafted. Watching the team work the grill — from the perfect slice to that iconic cheese melt — you understand why this place has earned such loyal fans.

🥖 Soft sesame roll
🥩 Thinly shaved steak
🧀 Melted perfection
🍟 Crispy golden fries

This isn’t fast food — it’s food made fast, with heart.

Grabbed a classic cheesesteak to go.
Easy to order with the touchscreens, and it was pretty quiet on a Monday night, so my order was ready quickly.
My cheesesteak was delicious, the meat juicy, the cheese not the star of the show but a great binder, and the caramelized onions perfect. The sesame seed bread was decent too.
Not the cheapest cheesesteak in town, but there's definitely more quality.
customer_insights: Shay’s Steaks is a beloved fast-casual spot in Philadelphia known for its high-quality cheesesteaks and exceptional customer service. The owner, Scott, is praised for his personal touch and hospitality, making it a memorable dining experience for both locals and visitors.

googleReviews: Top notch all the way. Upscale but not stuffy or pretentious. The decor is like a modern rustic mixed with artsy. The food is outstanding, from the starters to desert. Exec Chef Sonny and his team make everything in house, they butcher their own meats, they even grow their own mushrooms! The steaks are AMAZING. The sampler steak was fine, just not as memorable as the other dishes. Overall, a great place for a satisfying meal.

Urban Farmer is a modern upscale steakhouse.  It has farm to table choices.  There are beers on tap and a nice wine list.  Our group had the grass fed ribeye, ARKA Salmon, sea bass and the double cut pork chop.  The truffle tater tots were fabulous as was the grilled broccolini.  The food was all outstanding.  The service was excellent and they split our checks as requested.  It was a lovely dinner.  The cornbread is excellent.

I visited Urban Farmer a while ago, and it left me with mixed impressions. It tries to bring a farm-to-table, modern steakhouse vibe. Some parts worked well, but others felt a little less polished.

🍴 Food Experience
The food was very good—steaks cooked well, sides flavorful, and everything felt like it was made with care. What I especially appreciated was that it wasn’t just about the main course—coffee, dessert, and drinks were all excellent, which made the meal feel complete.

🍹 Drinks & Service
The service stood out—attentive, professional, and friendly without being overbearing. The drinks were also well put together: solid cocktails, good wine options, and nothing felt rushed or sloppy.

🚗 Parking & Access
Parking can be tricky. Nearby garages are an option, but planning ahead is wise.

🏛 Atmosphere
Here’s where things felt a little off. The space has potential, but the atmosphere was just okay. Seating is a bit close, and while it tries for farmhouse chic, some parts feel slightly dated. It’s not uncomfortable, but compared to the food and service, the setting didn’t quite match up.

✨ Overall Experience
For me, Urban Farmer delivered with good food, great coffee and desserts, and attentive service. The atmosphere was fine but not a standout, and parking could be easier. Still, if you’re looking for a reliable steakhouse in Philadelphia, it’s worth the stop—you just have to go in knowing the strengths are more on the food and service side than the vibe.

I’ve eaten at Urban Farmer many times and even brought friends and family along. They haven’t always been consistent with temping proteins, which is why I was so happy my striped bass was cooked to absolute perfection tonight. Everything on the plate was balanced and flavorful, easily the best meal I’ve had here.

The atmosphere and service added to the experience. I did order a whiskey sour with Maker’s Mark that came out to $26 — definitely on the pricey side — but overall the quality of the meal made the visit worth it. Urban Farmer is more hit than miss, and tonight they absolutely nailed it.
customer_insights: Urban Farmer Philadelphia is an upscale steakhouse known for its farm-to-table approach and high-quality meats. The atmosphere is modern and rustic, making it suitable for romantic dinners and special occasions, though parking can be a challenge. While the food and service are consistently praised, the ambiance may not fully match the high standards set by the menu.

🥩 Geno’s Steaks vs Pat’s King of Steaks

Geno’s Steaks
✨ The vibe is bright, bold, and full of energy.

Being the tourist I was when visiting Philly and having heard about these “rivals” I tried both  Geno’s and Pats, to see which I thought was the best. I have to say I was sorely disappointed. Both are well below average Philly cheesesteak sandwiches that I have had throughout my life. If these are representatives of what the Philly cheesesteak sandwich should be like, then the city and state and all those that take any amount of pride that a sandwich has your name on it, should hold their heads in shame. Both Pat’s and Geno’s steak had no flavor, seemed steamed or boiled. Geno’s had very little cheese or onions and the bread was tough and chewy. Pat’s had good amount of cheese and onions. I do not recommend either, I would suggest finding the local favorite because my son had mentioned even before I went to Philly that people he knows that went to both said they were not good, but because I fell into the rivalry and wanted to see who I thought was better, I went any way. All I got out of it was now I can say I tried them both, if it ever comes up, and they both sucked. Save yourself time and money and pass.

I recently had the pleasure of trying Greedy Soul Food Restaurant, and the meal was genuinely excellent. I ordered the smoked turkey wings, mac & cheese, yams, and collard greens mixed with cabbage. I have often been disappointed by other soul food spots in Philadelphia that seem to skimp on quality ingredients, particularly in their mac & cheese, but this restaurant was a delightful surprise.
The mac & cheese deserves special mention. Making great mac & cheese requires a commitment to quality cheeses, and unfortunately, many restaurants cut corners by using insufficient cheese or cheaper substitutes like Velveeta, which just lacks flavor. Greedy Soul Food, however, deliver flavorful and cheesy mac&chesse. You could distinctly taste a sharp cheese, the texture was perfect, and it was seasoned to absolute perfection.
The rest of the meal was equally fantastic: the turkey wings were cooked perfectly with great smoky flavor, and both the greens and the yams were a 10 out of 10.
The service was also wonderful—the young lady who took my order both over the phone and in person had a great, lively, and bubbly personality.
The only negative feedback I have is regarding the ambiance; the dining area felt quite stale and very uninviting. I would never dine-in based on this reason.
Overall, I rate this place highly. If you are simply getting takeout, this is one of the best soul food experiences I have had in a long time. As a Philadelphia native who cooks well, I know good soul food, and this place delivers.

During a recent visit to Philadelphia, I stumbled upon a place that felt like a slice of home — Ol’ Boys Soul Food, tucked away at 5148 Locust Street in West Philly. From the moment I arrived the rich aroma of seasoned goodness and slow-cooked comfort filled the air.

Their Southern fried chicken was golden, crispy, and tender inside — just the way it should be. The fried whiting, tilapia, and shrimp were cooked with a master’s touch, flavorful and satisfying. Every side dish was a hit at my family’s table: baked mac and cheese oozing with cheesy perfection, collard greens and cabbage cooked just right, and potato salad that tasted like it came straight from a family reunion picnic. And that cornbread — moist, sweet, and buttery — tied the whole meal together.

The service was fast, friendly, and genuine, making the experience even better. In a city known for cheesesteaks and pretzels, Ol’ Boys brings something different — a soulful reminder that Southern cooking isn’t about fancy plates, but about heart, heritage, and flavor that lingers long after the last bite.

The Mac was soooo dry it was crazy. Yams gave canned vibes and had no flavor. Cabbage were pretty salty but they were ok. The only thing that was ever room temperature were the hot honey wings. They were ok, but I got a bone that was sauced but had no meat.

The food was terrible. The sweet potatoes weren’t cooked through. They were hard. The Mac and cheese was not tasty. They are stingy with the fish. My mom didn’t get her potato salad and her collard greens were bad. I didn’t even ask my grandmother about her food. What for? There are better soul food restaurants.
customer_insights: Ol' Boys Soul Food Restaurant offers a mix of experiences, with some patrons praising the comfort and flavor of the Southern dishes while others criticize the quality and preparation of the food. The atmosphere is casual and family-friendly, making it a suitable spot for a laid-back meal, but it may not be ideal for special occasions or pre-nightlife activities.

I dined in for an early dinner and ordered the Brown Stew Chicken w Yams & Collard Greens, Fish Soup, and Watermelon Juice. Everything was very tasty! The yams didn’t have much additional flavor though but I didn’t mind because as a side they just absorbed the sauce from the Brown Stew Chicken and got flavored that way. Also they seem to use pretty fresh produce so all the produce had more of its own natural flavor - yams, collard greens, as well as the cabbage and carrots in the Stew, and the okra in the Fish Soup. The flavors in the Fish Soup seemed unique to me and I really enjoyed it. The soup came with a tasty dumpling in it as well (not sure if there is a different name for this dumpling but I will be doing more research on Caribbean cuisines). I also liked that there were not bones in the soup as I often expect bones when ordering most meats from Caribbean restaurants but I’m not a fan of dealing with them. The Brown Stew Chicken while very tasty and flavorful, does have bones in it. Everything was well seasoned and salty, but not to an offensive extent at all - just perfect and as expected.  Last but not least, the Watermelon Juice was a very refreshing addition to the meal that was much appreciated after walking in hot weather. It tasted like fresh fruit and was sweet but not too sweet! It was honestly a real necessity at the time, so I’m glad I found this place. I definitely want to come back and try more of their food.

The service was also great! Everyone working there seemed friendly, which is definitely not always the case, and I felt welcome. Someone (the chef?) came out to personally take orders to speed up the line which wasn’t even long, so they seem committed to getting people their food fast (despite “island time” existing in Caribbean cultures). The menu is simple which allows them to have everything ready quickly & at a high quality. The quality of the food is what matters above all, and it seems they understand that. Also be ready with cash as it is Cash Only.

I love the cozy vibe and the old school diner/lunch counter aesthetics, but I felt like the dining room/bar space should be better utilized. I understand this situation isn’t even necessarily their fault as we are in the era of takeout, and they clearly put their money towards making sure the food is good, which is obviously most important. I also understand they are dealing with the fact that their menu isn’t super conducive for the bar/lunch counter setting, and it’s detached from the kitchen, but it has a purpose - it’s where they make and serve the homemade juices. Something as simple as pictures of the main ingredients in the juices could be a low cost way to liven up this area and serve a practical purpose as well. They have big, comfortable tables which some restaurants in the area don’t even offer anymore, so I appreciated that.
customer_insights: Little Delicious is a cozy Jamaican eatery known for its flavorful dishes and homemade juices. While many patrons praise the food for its authenticity and taste, there are mixed reviews regarding consistency, with some expressing disappointment in recent visits. The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, making it a comfortable spot for a laid-back meal.
