My past 6 orders have been BLAND and the rice is overcooked, it’s laziness on the cooks part because why isn’t the food simply seasoned? You guys need a new cook, get back to being the best African restaurant in Philly!

I drive from jersey and get the fufu and egusi. I used to come all the time BUT the egusi used to be waaaaay to spicy so I stopped coming. Yesterday, my man said let’s try them again but this time let’s get a bottle of milk to eliminate the spice lolol well we went back after 6months and there was no spiciness in it THANK YOOOOU!!! We will be back again every week now. That spice was too much for us before but this time was perfect.
customer_insights: Le Mandingue African Restaurant is well-regarded for its authentic African cuisine, particularly dishes like jollof rice and fufu. While many customers praise the food's flavor and generous portions, there are mixed reviews regarding consistency and seasoning, indicating a need for quality control in the kitchen.

googleReviews: The food was delicious. We had the Lamb and Tilapia with Jollof, the onions on top add so much flavor. The Maafe with Chicken was also very good. We order plantains as well that were freshly fried and sweet. The Ginger and mange drink was taste amazing. They also had live music which added to the atmosphere. 10/10 experience

We brought a group visiting for a work conference as part of a food tour all around Philly and this was an exceptional experience. We focused on the diversity and representation of our multi-cultural city, of which none of our visiting guests had ever eaten West African food before. They all came back for multiple services of the Yassa Philly chicken, meat patties, and Senegal cocktail. Youma personally welcomed our group and shared some of her backstory - which was our favorite part of the whole experience. We can't wait to bring many MANY more groups back to Kilimandjaro. Thank you Youma and Abiche!!!

Let me start by saying how beautifully decorated the restaurant is. The vibrant colors and decor make you feel welcomed and happy., the customer service is excellent and the wait staff were very friendly. The FOOD.... I can't say enough how good the food was; it's African food (Senegalese ) everything was so flavorful and cooked right. I've had Liberian, and Nigerian food but this was amazing. The red snapper was delicious and grilled to perfection; I really didn't care for the athieke. It was over cooked and mushy, the plantains were amazing! It was paired with sweet carrots and onions in a tomato based sauce. My friend loved all of her food, she had the chicken and jollof rice which she stated that everything was full of flavor and delicious. My only complaint is that they did not have dessert.... We had to go somewhere else for a sweet treat. The menu selections are not much but what they do have is worth the visit. I recommend this beautiful restaurant to everyone please try 🙌🏽❤️

Had such a great experience here. The atmosphere was relaxed and welcoming, and the food was packed with deep, comforting flavors. Everything tasted homemade in the best way—rich spices, tender meats, and perfectly cooked rice.

The decor at Kilimandjaro is devine. The food is delicious. And, the service is superb. Conveniently located in West Philadelphia the space is pristine, even the bathrooms are beautiful. Second visit to measure consistency and was not disappointed. The ginger drinks are a great palate cleanser as well as refreshing. I had the salad with the homemade dressing and was impressed with the freshness of the ingredients as well as portion size. Ordered two lamb dishes -!chops that were grilled and succulent sautéed lamb. You must try the Thieboudienne but order before 3pm since this popular dish runs out early. Special touches were fresh cut flowers changed out from casual lunch bunches to dinner bouquets. This family run establishment is a hit!
customer_insights: Kilimandjaro offers a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere with delicious West African cuisine, particularly Senegalese dishes. Guests appreciate the flavorful food, friendly service, and live music, making it a great spot for group gatherings and cultural experiences.

googleReviews:
I've been seeing this on tiktok for the past 2 weeks and decided lastnight to try.
When I came in I had to greet the lady working.  Didn't like that, I'm coming in to spend my money. Welcome would've been nice! She didn't even ask could she take my order.  My husband and I seen a kiosk and placed our order.  The food was a 6/10.
Jollof rice was flavorless, steak was chewy and had fat/Gristle on each piece.
The salad that came with it was good along with the plantains. The potato greens were watery and ok.  Overall I love supporting my people businesses but I probably won't be back.  Respectfully

Came here with friend. Treated them to west African food for their birthday. We arrived around 730 which was right on time. After we ordered our food on the kiosk and set down a big crowd came in. So many people came to order food before the night was out. The food was delicious. The white suya sauce was good with hot drumsticks. I was super impressed with the food. Even my friend.  I also had cornbread with my meal and the corn bread was delicious too.
Both of our food together was about 40 to 45 dollars. Very reasonable.
When you dine in. Your food does come on a sturdy paper plate.  Felt authentic and home vibes.

You can see the food being prepared which I love so much.

Unsure if they have a restroom for the public.

I ordered online, and my food arrived fresh and hot, which I really appreciated.

I tried the Beef Suya (spicy) platter with plantain, cabbage, onion, and jollof rice. The jollof rice was definitely the best part it was flavorful and perfectly cooked. The beef Suya was tender with a nice texture and good spice, though I found it a bit too salty. I have a high spice tolerance, but even for me the heat built up and made it tough to finish, so I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone sensitive to spice.

Portion-wise, I wish there had been more plantain and onion, as the serving felt small compared to the generous amount of rice.

I also ordered a chicken Suya leg on the side, and in my opinion, the chicken Suya was much better than the beef.

This African spot is amazing! Definitely try the Suya bowl because it’s a great deal and packed with flavor. Some of the dishes were spicy even at the lowest spice level, so watch out if you’re not big on heat. You HAVE to get the cornbread as a side. It’s seriously so good. Loved everything about this place and will definitely be back. Seems like it’s easier to dine in and let the food come out when it ready instead of ordering online.

Located in northern liberties, so parking can be a challenge. I wanted to like this food. The price isn’t awful, but it’s not the great either. I paid about $15 for the steak bowl with jollof and plantain, and then another $4 for a meat pie. Everything was lackluster. The meat pie ingredients tasted muddled, I did enjoy the crust tho. The jollof rice flavor was mild, I wish it stood out more… as in more tomato taste, more richness… anything to resemble Nigerian jollof. The steak suya was fine… it was a bit tough, and majority of the flavor came from the sprinkled suya spice over top. The plantain was light skin and hard and they weren’t very sweet. I’ve been meaning to try the restaurant and I finally did. I’m not impressed.
customer_insights: SUYA SUYA West African Grill offers a casual dining experience with a focus on authentic West African flavors. While some dishes received mixed reviews regarding flavor and texture, many patrons enjoyed the vibrant atmosphere and the affordability of the menu. It's a suitable spot for casual gatherings but may not be ideal for special occasions.

googleReviews:
Just visited for the first time, and my, am I glad I did! It was my 25th birthday and I wanted to go out to eat with my parents and siblings. I did a Google search for fine dining African restaurants in the city, and Chateau Rouge was one of the first ones to come up. As a fine dining line cook, I’m careful about where I go to eat out, but after reading the reviews, I had to try it out.
First, the restaurant is small but cozy in a home-y kind of way, so big thanks for Chateau Rouge for helping me arrange the reservation for all 10 of us to come. The decor was beautiful and not too much, from the pillows to the napkin holders, to the African masks and paintings on the walls. The chairs and tables are low, so if you have long legs or over 6’ like one of my brothers, it will be a bit uncomfortable after a while.
Secondly, the service was great. Our waiter explained the menu well and was helpful in choosing the right number of dishes for the table. Everyone was helpful all night in bringing out the food and drinks and clearing the table before courses.
Lastly, the food. THE FOOD. Bussin’ no discussion GOOD. We all ordered the pre fixe menu, $55 per person, 1 appetizer, 1 main, 2 sides and 1 dessert. You can pick from 3 appetizers, 5 main dishes and sides, and 4 desserts. Because it was 10 of us, we ordered a mix of everything so we could all share and taste everything. The puff puffs were great bread starters, not too sweet and bread-y. The veggie salad was dressed well, on the sweet side with the raisins and pineapple but balanced out with palm, bamboo and mixed greens. I would have liked more lettuce, but that’s my opinion. The pastels were very flavorful, I had to remind myself that it was tuna inside! The suya wings were so good! My siblings loved them so much, I need to get the recipe now! We all had the virgin pina colada from the bar, which was nice, a bit much on the mint and low on the coconut, but again, my opinion. The coconut sauce and the peanut sauce with the suya brochettes and the grilled chicken elevated the dish’s flavor to a new level. My siblings don’t like fish, but they liked the texture of the grilled fish and I liked the flavor. The yassa poulet and the haricot saute were some of the best dishes I’ve had in a while! The chicken so tender, it was falling off the bone. The flavor was new but familiar and comforting at the same time. The beans cooked to perfection, and so so good! Plantains and sweet potatoes were fresh and naturally sweet. I could tell the produce in the ratatouille was out of season and some of the rice was undercooked, but that’s because I have some experience in the industry. The dessert just completed the meal: the lava cake was light and chocolate rich, the fruit salad was fresh and naturally sweet, the banana flambé and caramelized pineapple were just delicious. This was not a tasting menu, so all the portions are the are the same are the à la cart menu, which are good sized if you’re a little hungry. This also isn’t a Michelin fine dining restaurant with the portions and platings, so don’t come expecting it. However, do come expecting flavorful food, you won’t be disappointed.

Just had dinner at Chateau Rouge, an incredible West African BYOB with a French touch on South Street! 🔥

It's a charming Black-owned restaurant with a well-executed menu that features several dishes with spices that come directly from Cameroon!

They serve incredible entrees, but have a stellar 4-course tasting menu that's only $55.

As you can see, it's worth a visit. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a truly great meal here. We had 3 different kinds of chicken and all of them were delicious, but brochettes were our favorite. Definitely do not forget to leave room for dessert, the caramelized pineapple and banana flambee were both fantastic. Great atmosphere inside (didn't see the outdoor seating), and super friendly service. Can't wait to return.

My wife and I had a great meal at Chateau Rouge last Thursday. Steven was a wonderful server and the fixed price option is great menu. Our food and drinks were fresh and excellently prepared. I ordered the chicken skewers to start, followed by a whole grilled fish. It was delicious. We will definitely be back.

Where do I begin, I went here with a friend and the food was pretty good. Upon entry we were greeted by kind friendly staff members. For a first time experience i enjoyed it, the owner came to my table personally and introduced herself. The environment was clean and well decorated to fit the cultural aesthetic. I highly recommend making a reservation prior to arrival they do have outdoor seating if you find the indoor seating too tight. The space is fairly small.
customer_insights: Chateau Rouge is a cozy, Black-owned restaurant offering a unique blend of West African and French cuisine. Guests rave about the flavorful dishes and attentive service, making it a great spot for intimate gatherings or special occasions.

venueName: Eatwell Philly - African Restaurant and Lounge
googleReviews: I’m Puerto Rican with mostly Nigerian DNA (25% Nigerian. Everything else is 15 or less). The food is tasty. The rice isn't the same texture as traditional Puerto Rican, But the soul of the flavor is definitely there

Everything felt incredibly authentic and well done! The waitress helped up go through the menu and choose things that interest us without ordering in excess. I personally like my fufu on the side and not under everything. Some of the meats just weren’t my cup of tea but i’m sure others will like it. We recommend the Suya

First time trying Nigerian food. I took Efo Elegusi meal and jollof rice, I loved it. Food was so good. Good service and nice atmosphere (good music, not too loud). The place is very neat, I highly recommand.

Stopped into Eatwell for lunch and had a great experience! The food was fantastic, particularly the spicy suya, meat pies, and jollof rice. The menu was quite extensive, so there are plenty of options and we look forward to trying new things. It was our first time eating here, but the service was pleasant and helpful in explaining things on the menu. Overall, a great time!

I was walking when I spotted this place. I was excited to check it out as I am African and wanted to support an African restaurant. The Suya was a little dry to me, but I did still enjoy it. The puff puff was definitely worth it. The restaurant was clean and it wasn't too loud. I definitely recommend checking them out.
customer_insights: Eatwell Philly offers an authentic Nigerian dining experience with a friendly atmosphere and helpful staff. Customers appreciate the extensive menu and flavorful dishes, although some items may vary in texture and taste. Overall, it is a great spot for casual dining and cultural exploration.

googleReviews: We had African Small Pot deliver food to an event in Africatown, and they were extremely helpful. The staff was kind and the food was absolutely delicious. They made us vegetarian-friendly breakfast sandwiches, with eggs, peppers, onions, and garlic. Everyone who ate one thought they were incredible! They also gave us coffee and tea with the food. The delivery was on-time and the communication with the staff was reliable and consistent. Definitely consider ordering from them or giving them a visit!

My colleagues and I recently had the pleasure of visiting African Small Pot for the first time and everybody left with a smile. We had many different items from the menu (variety of fish, chicken, rice, greens, etc.) and everything was truly so delicious and flavorful! The entire staff including the chef and the owner were very welcoming and accommodating to us, as we were a large group. We are incredibly grateful! 🌟 See you again soon!

An absolute 10/10. The customer service was excellent, as well as the food. The owner was extremely attentive and made sure my friend and I were taken care of. I ordered some red snapper, with a side of rice, and some plantain. I will definitely be coming back.

This was my first time here, I came 20 minutes before closing. I ordered fried red snapper, and cassava leaf. The cassava leaf was good, the fried red snapper was nice and fresh the sauce was really good. I will be returning.

Food was great! Definitely recommend the grilled snapper and rice, absolutely delicious.
I typically order to go. I highly recommend that the owner of this restaurant redo the bathroom. Food is great but the atmosphere needs major improvement. I won't recommend dining in, just take out.
customer_insights: African Small Pot is highly praised for its delicious and flavorful food, particularly seafood options like red snapper. The welcoming and attentive staff enhance the dining experience, making it suitable for casual gatherings and group outings.

googleReviews:
The Saints has an amazing atmosphere as well as food. Especially the red snapper and grape salad. The fries were good and my coworkers were enjoying their pineapple wings.The owner and staff were really nice and accommodating.
I had a phenomenal time with my crew after our 10 hour work day . We went back the second day, with a whole different group of crew members, but they were closing earlier.

Came across this 5 star restaurant when looking for a resturant/lounge on a Friday night. After calling to confirm they were still byob & would have a dj we dropped in. The lounge vibe and music (no dj) was cool but that's about the end of the pros. There was only one young woman operating as host, waitress, bartender & cashier. She was nice but service was extremely slow. Between that & the dirty glassware we should've dipped but we stayed and ordered the suya beef & chicken, fries and kale. Everything came out lukewarm and the "suya" spiced meat just meant it came w/ a heavy dusting of cayenne powder. The fries were good. The final straw, the $50 per bottle fee that was added to our bill for our two bottles of wine. After explaining this fee was not listed ANYWHERE on their socials they gave us a "discount" and took one of the fees off. Crazy for $12 wine. The table next to us had the same surprise as they were giving the manager a piece of their mind as we left. I can't understand the 5 star reviews.

Googled "African restaurants Philly " & The Saints popped up so I wanted to try it. It's BYOB. Our waitress was attentive, she kept checking on us to make sure we were good and even offered to take pics. I had Suya chicken, jollof rice and plantains. Everything was tasty and it came out in a reasonable time. The decor is nice and the music was good. I can see it being a vibe once more people start patronizing. Can't wait to go back!!

I visited a few days ago. Cute vibes, decent food, but I will not be returning to this establishment for these reasons:
1. We were not greeted by staff upon arrival. The waitresses on duty weren’t as knowledgeable as they should’ve been. They were more occupied with smoking hookah.
2. Their website has several false advertisements:
There were only two main entrées that night where their website states four. I also asked for a salad, but they said they were out of the grape salad (not ceaser). That night they had snapper and lamb chops as main dishes. My party and I had to wait about 30 minutes for the food. I got the snapper. It was cooked well, the sauce they used tasted great, my only problem was the fish was not seasoned inside. The inside tasted bland. I also had a side of plantains and collard greens, which tasted well. My partner got the lamb chops. I was told that they were good. They had a side of jollof rice, which I tasted, and we both agreed it was extremely spicy. This was not the good type of spicy. It was the type of spicy where you had to focus on eating it instead of enjoying the meal. Also, nowhere on their website does it state that it's BYOB. The waitress told us it's a $50 cover charge if we brought our own bottle (…like huh??!). Their website states to “Unwind…with our signature cocktails, curated wines, and premium spirits”. We  didn't bring a bottle because we thought they would have drinks.  I tried calling their number several times to ask questions, but it went straight to message.
3. The music mix they had was very entertaining. However, the music was too loud! It's already a small establishment, the music should not be that loud. The waitresses placed us near the speaker. This could’ve been a contributing factor. It's a lounge not a club.I know they’re trying to create a vibe, but I shouldn’t have to be yelling across the table to have a conversation with my party.
4. This place does have the potential to be a really great scene, it just needs a little TLC. But, in the meantime, I will not be returning back in the near future.
Went here for my birthday and enjoyed the food. Fairly new so it wasn't busy. Currently B.Y.OB. Me and my party tried the snapper, chicken wings, tacos and salad.  Everything was delicious 😋
customer_insights: The Saints Restaurant and Lounge offers a vibrant atmosphere with a focus on African cuisine, particularly known for its BYOB policy and dishes like suya chicken and jollof rice. However, service inconsistencies and a lack of clear communication regarding fees and menu items have led to mixed reviews, suggesting a need for improvements to enhance the overall dining experience.

googleReviews: Amazing food, amazing service. 100% would go again. The attieke was amazing and the fish well seasoned.

Great food! Had the attieke fish and lamb, and everything was seasoned amazingly! Customer service was great, Aisatou was a great hostess, which always makes the experience even better.

Would definitely check out if you are around!
The lamb was really good. Their jollof rice was not good. The peanut butter soup and egusi were amazing. Alot of food for a decent price.

I went there because of the positive reviews. But my experience was not positive at all. I order jollof rice with lamb. No plantains and was still charge $20. They switch the price every time I go in there and the lamb was hard full of bones. Is a big No for me.
I love their food. very friendly and the food is amazing! Cassava leaf is the go to but trying other items on the menu was great me and babe love this place! Try them out!
customer_insights: Sahara Restaurant is praised for its authentic African cuisine, particularly the attieke and peanut butter soup, with friendly service enhancing the dining experience. However, there are mixed reviews regarding certain dishes like jollof rice, indicating variability in quality.

address: 428 W Olney Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19120, USA
googleReviews: We decided to dine in, and I have to say this place blew me away. From the start, the service was warm and welcoming. They brought out complimentary coffee and donuts, which were absolutely delicious and set the tone for the meal. When the food arrived, I had the Yassa with fish—and wow, it was hands down one of the best meals I’ve had in a long time. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Between the incredible food, the amazing coffee, and the top-notch service, I’ll definitely be coming back!

First time having Senegalese food -- but not the last! Got a dish called Yassa -- chicken, flavorful cooked onions, and rice. Amazing flavor. Also got a super fresh salad to start, and a really flavorful coffee. Constant flow of people coming in or taking out, so obviously a neighborhood gem I was missing out on. Staff was super nice too. Coming back for the lamb next time!

This is my first time trying Senegalese food. I got the lamb dibi with jollof and plantain. I spent around $23. The portion was fine. The lamb was delicious, and a hint of mustard. The plantain was very sweet, just a tad too greasy for my liking. The rice was my least favorite. Maybe it was the type of rice they used, I didn’t like the texture, it also didn’t have that much flavor.

This is my third time ordering from this store. The first time my order was correct. The second time I received different items then what was asked for over the phone and did not realize until I came home. This time I order a milk like purée that has black beans in it. Unknown to me, I thought this was the same item I’ve purchased from other ethnic African restaurants. I had bought 4 of these totaling $20 dollars. Even while in the store one of the products I had asked for I was told was a Guinean purée. I felt as though if the items I listed were Guinean they should’ve made me aware that the item I was getting was not the same as what they were selling. I tried calling upon eating the first bowl to resolve the issues of me mistaking a dish I commonly eat to theirs. The gentleman who answer couldn’t seem to understand how a simple mishap could have took place when similar dishes are served in Africa especially west Africa. He was very  ignorant and arrogant to tell me “that this was not a Guinean store” but still proceed to go through with the purchase I thought was similar to the Guinean purchase I usually buy. Will be disputing this charge because the other 3 items will have to be discarded. I was not informed of a no refund policy by this man who answered or anything just pure ignorance when I called.

Recently used the catering service everything went smoothly. Grateful for the care and intention that Ngone brought to every detail and answering every phone calls (even during her day off). The price was affordable and the food was amazing. Don't take my words for it go check it out you will not regret it.
customer_insights: TOUBA African Restaurant offers a warm and welcoming atmosphere with a focus on authentic Senegalese cuisine. Customers rave about the flavorful dishes like Yassa and lamb dibi, although there are some concerns regarding service consistency. Overall, it is a neighborhood gem ideal for casual dining and trying new flavors.

I’ve been coming to this restaurant for well over 10years I want to say about a year ago they switch owners. I was very disappointed with the customer service of this establishment. The owner was rude nasty speaking over me and yelling. I have been ordering here from years and actually enjoy the food, but the customer service is horrible. They make a lot of excuses and they are unprofessional. I will NOT be ordering from here again. This is my new favorite spot!!! The employees were so friendly and welcoming and had such  pleasant attitude. I tired the Palava soup with fufu and let me tell you 10/10 I normally get cassava leaf but after finding this gem I will be leveling up my taste buds 😋

I had potato greens from here before and they were good but it’s been awhile. I got some today and there’s not really any flavor. They just taste like oily spicy spinach. I also asked for no meat and they gave me meat.
customer_insights: Soul of Africa Restaurant has a mixed reputation among customers, with some praising the food and atmosphere while others express dissatisfaction with food quality and customer service. The restaurant has a loyal customer base who appreciate the traditional African cuisine, but recent changes in ownership have led to inconsistent experiences.

googleReviews: Food was amazing!! This is where you go if you know you want to eat some good Liberian food. I had the potato greens, no notes.

I order fish, dirty rice and potatoe greens in red oil. The potatoe greens had mold in them. I called the store to talk to the owner to make them aware of the situation. A man answered the phone I told him what happened and he hung up in my ear.

I went to get the dry fish and rice like I always get and it's good. I went today 9-2-25 and my fish haven't been cleaned. It's a lot of scales on it. I love the way the fish skin taste but not with scales on it. More money less fish. They are losing their touch on the food. I will not be going back.

I’ve been coming here for yearsss, they use to be so good, fresh & reasonable far as price, now the food goes bad very fast. The dry rice It has a foul smell after I put it in my fridge & warm it up the next day. & the vegetables have a foul smell as well, & unfortunately I put it in my fridge soon as I got home from picking it up, so it wasn’t out long from the time I’ve got it, I also got plantains they were fine taste as if I just bought them & I’ve had this issue other times before, I’m not sure if they are selling day old rice & vegetables, but this isn’t good as it has made my relatives sick, & also they went up on the red snapper & dry rice it’s now $25 a platter, but I don’t understand why or how if the rice is only $6, so they are selling one Red Snapper for $19?? That’s diabolical!! If I didn’t have a long time relationship with this restaurant, they would get 1 star, however I figured maybe if they get a warning they will stop selling bad rice & vegetables, that’s possibly days old , & be a little more reasonable for the price of one red snapper.

I would have given them five stars. If the pieces of meat they gave me was not full of bone. I literally got two big pieces of bone no meat. The potato greens were good. Just wish I had some meat. Not to mention the bone took up half the container.
customer_insights: Emma's Liberian Kitchen has received mixed reviews, with many praising the authentic Liberian dishes while others express concerns about food quality and freshness. The venue is casual and family-friendly, but recent complaints about food safety and customer service suggest a decline in standards.

address: Underground in the suburban station, 1500 John F Kennedy Blvd, Philadelphia, PA 19102, USA
neighborhood: Underground in the suburban station, 1500 John F Kennedy Blvd, Philadelphia
googleReviews:
As a Nigerian myself, I am always eager to try Nigerian restaurants. The reviews weren’t great, but I try to form my own opinion. That being said, the reviews were spot on. Before I review the food I want to say that the owner was very kind and welcoming. The restaurant located underground of JFK was clean and inviting. I wish I could say positive things about the food. I ordered jollof rice with peppered goat, and the seasoned spinach , 2 meat pies and a bag of chinchin. My total was $61. Never have I paid that much for African food, and I have frequented many African restaurants in Philadelphia. I was literally flabbergasted when I reviewed my receipt. There was a 15% gratuity automatically included. How do you as a business owner do that, for a take-out order no less? The food took about 20 mins to come out after we ordered. We didn’t dine in. When we got home to eat, the portion was crazy… as in crazy small. I had to laugh because  surely this was a joke.

The jollof rice Smokey and tasty, but it was so salty.
The peppered goat: by far the worst item, was also salty and SO OILY. Literally baptized in grease and tough to chew.
The spinach was really tasty, good flavor but unfortunately also oily.
The meat pie, has no taste. The dough was nice and flaky. We welcomed the meat pie, it was a much needed palate cleanser.
The chinchin was crunchy and delicious with the right amount of sweetness.
All in all, I would not recommend this restaurant. It is overpriced and the food quality and quantity does not justify the price.

I tried New Era for the first time and it was great. Chef T was very friendly and had no problem explaining the menu to me. When I tried to order multiple things from the menu, she showed me a combo that already contained those things so I could get more bang for my buck. I really appreciated her honesty. Also, when the food took a little longer than expected, she offered me a free beverage for my wait. Her customer service was impeccable. You can tell she really loves what she does. The food was amazing! The jollof rice had a nice smoky flavor to it. The pepper chicken was juicy with a nice spice but somehow Chef T was able to get a crispy skin on it. The plantains were sweet and caramelized. The portion of food was great too! I will definitely be returning.
The food was absolutely amazing and the customer service was great. Everything came out fresh, flavorful, and served with a friendly attitude. Definitely worth a visit!

I ordered rice and stew (a very small portion for 48) and I have been told to pay 10 extra just to dine in ofc I didn’t but once I arrived home the food was really really salty and make the whole dish unbeatable I’m very disappointed this is my first time ever leaving a review anywhere I hope the owner would see this and improve the quality and the portions cause this is unacceptable.
The girl at the front desk was very nice btw

As a fellow restaurant owner it’s hard to write a review like this but I have to be honest. We came in and were told we were unable to do the buffet even though the sign clearly says buffet on Thursday. The table next to us told us that they were able to get the buffet so that was a little disheartening. I couldn’t even get my fork through the beef it was so tough. It tasted like it wasn’t made to order but reheated and perhaps that was what made the beef tough. Also, at checkout the server hit skip on the screen which didn’t allow me to see that it was automatically set at 15% tip. While I don’t mind tipping this felt very deceiving. $108 for lackluster food. It puts the server in an awkward position because I can tell he would refund if he could but the big sign says no refunds.
customer_insights: New Era Cuisine offers a mix of experiences, with some customers praising the friendly service and flavorful dishes, while others criticize the portion sizes and food quality. The restaurant's casual vibe and location make it a potential spot for takeout, but the inconsistent reviews suggest it may not be ideal for special occasions or group outings.

googleReviews: Got tired of mandingue bad customer service. I gave this pace a shot and I am not disappointed. Attieke was fresh and delicious. Meat flavorful. Customer service great. I ordered over the phone when I got there my food was ready. I just wish the meat had some onion sauce to it. Other than that love it . Thank you

If you’ve never had African food before you’ll probably enjoy this place. If you have, just skip it. It’s not bad but since it’s in an area with lots of African restaurants it doesn’t hold up to the competition in the area. Emma’s is a few blocks away and sooo much better. We tried the palava sauce and the pepper soup. It was not as spicy as most West African food tends to be but came with pepper sauce on the side to turn the heat up. The food had a good flavor but it wasn’t cooked long enough for the flavor to really get into the meat & bones. The cow foot was very tough and the fish in the soup was underdone. The fufu was not mixed well. It was edible but I was disappointed knowing I could have gone somewhere else nearby for much better food. Also, The bathroom smelled horribly and when I asked for soap I was informed they had none so I had to help myself to the dish detergent sitting just outside the bathroom.

The grilled fish and Achekeh was one of the best I have had in a long time. The fish was seasoned and well done and  the achekeh was not dry like other places lol. I will be coming back again for grilled fish
Authentic and delicious Liberian food. Big portions. Very good prices

(8/18/23) I unfortunately had to change my review. The young woman was going to send me off with old, nasty looking plantains until I mentioned who I was in relation to my husband (who is African and known to them), so she made new plantains and put them on top of the old ones. I was also upcharged (I questioned it and it was a sudden "change in price"). I believe in fairness across the board, and me not being born on the continent shouldn't mean I should get lower quality food.
.....
(3 years ago)
Their fish & plantains is pretty good. I was introduced to the meal by a friend and I have gotten hooked. The only thing is the price changes if you get the same thing one week versus another. It's a bit pricey, but there's probably a good reason for it. Overall, the meal is good with caramelized onions and mayo with vegetables.
customer_insights: Ecowas African Restaurant offers a casual dining experience with a focus on Liberian and West African cuisine. While some dishes receive praise for their authenticity and flavor, others have faced criticism for inconsistency and service issues. Overall, it may appeal to those new to African cuisine, but seasoned diners might find better options nearby.

address: 721 Long Ln, Upper Darby Township, PA 19082, USA

Big portions for the price. That was the plus of the restaurant The problem was that they were out of quite a few things I wanted to order with my meal. But they were still charging the same price instead of at a discount price because it wasn't a full meal as advertised. Now they are upset with me for suggesting this restaurant that cheated them. I'm appalled at why they did that?

First off by saying Dish I choose (Esgusi)  was amazing first time ordering something other than Peanut butter stew ! Art and music was a whole vibe . The man (sorry forgot his name ) that greeted us and than made our delicious dishes was super polite and also very informative on any question I did throw at him about the dishes . Definitely will be returning 🫶🏽!
The food and the service was amazing! I cannot wait to go back. You must check it out.

I ordered tonight at 8:00pm online off of their website... I called at 9:50 and asked when should i expect my delivery. The guy stated it was taken 20 mins prior and laughed. The place is a 12 min drive (I don't drive). I'm writing this at 10:22 and obviously still no food. They need to check their drivers smh...

Ever since I’ve bought from the motherland cuisine I’ve never stopped coming back and last night I’ve bought 2 friends of my friends and they got Jollof rice and I got dry rice with fish chicken beef and plantin and oh my goodness I’ve never tasted so many flavor in one platter and it was huge. And customer service and the owners are welcoming to their customers. Big up to the motherland cuisine because they are great and they have wonderful people.
customer_insights: The Motherland Cuisine offers a unique African dining experience with flavorful dishes and large portions. While the service can be inconsistent, the welcoming atmosphere and cultural vibe make it a great spot for casual gatherings.

googleReviews: The food improved my whole week! I got the fried tallapia and jollof rice. Fish was delicious and rice was a great texture. The cabbage, onions, and vegetables were flavorful and tender. I don't personally like coleslaw but even that was great! We got a ginger drink which was so spicy and the owner offered us the hibiscus drink which was sweet, both great! We had a lovely dinner.

The dibi lamb was no seasoned well and they give you very small portions of meat for the price. The jollof rice and the plantain were good. I also liked the topping that came with it. The dibi lamb was mediocre and not seasoned well at all.
Husband and I decided to try Djoliba, and the food delicious and service was wonderful! We had the lamb and jollof. The sautéed onions over the  jollof is amazing. Im glad I found this place on IG
Had the lamb shank (gigot) with rice. The portion was generous and the food delicious. The entire staff was very attentive. I would eat here again.
Got the chicken and jolof rice, It was so good I couldn't help but clean my plate! Great vibes and a great meal!
customer_insights: Djoliba Restaurant offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on flavorful African cuisine, particularly jollof rice and seafood. While the atmosphere is casual and friendly, some dishes may vary in quality, but overall, patrons appreciate the attentive service and generous portions.

address: S 61st St &, Grays Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19142, USA
googleReviews: The food was delicious, with generous portions. The staff was friendly, and the food was ready before the given time. First time here, indeed not my last time.

It's best to call in first and pick up your order. This place gets packed but you'll never know because most orders are done by phone.
Portions are hefty. It's family run and owned. The customer service is excellent, they make all their customers feel like family. ♥️
All the dishes are excellent.
I drive from Delaware to get this place so great and lovely food

Tomato Soup with rice was splendid!
The okra soup was NOT as good it tasted specifically of fish, which I have an allergy to. Please let customers know when a dish contains seafood

Cool people. ✌🏾
Tasty plantains, delicious chicken. 🤤🤤
customer_insights: Le Faso is a family-run establishment known for its generous portions and friendly service. Customers appreciate the delicious food, though some dishes may contain allergens, so caution is advised.

googleReviews: 5 stars for amazing service and delicious waakye, soup, meat pie fried plantain! Highly recommended.

The food and the customer service were both extremely well. The food was fresh and hot, and the owner Aku and Edem were both very helpful, friendly, and patient as I was trying to figure out what to order. I would highly recommend anyone in the Philly area to come to this genuine Ghanaian Restaraunt. Aku even signed my box I felt even more special! 5 stars ⭐️!!!

Called in ahead with my order, which was ready when I arrived.
Ordered kelewele (fried spicy ripe plantain), waakye (cooked rice and beans) with goat meat and all the trimming
Food came with a boiled egg and a side of pepper sauce.

Tasty food, good service and a cozy atmosphere in this Ghanaian restaurant.

Does not accept cash.
Only Zelle and Cashapp

Was worth the 45 minute drive.

Aku is amazing.
FYI: Takeout place only and you have to call ahead of time. We didn't know that but she didn't turn us away. She took care of 5 hungry people with delicious food!

Love her, love service and her food!

My boyfriend introduced me to Aku's kitchen and I must say I have been addicted to her food since. The food is delicious. The place is great very clean. The service is spectacular. Aku's smile is always welcoming as well as the staff.   Best Ghanian food is West Philadelphia- a true hidden gem. Too bad she is only open on weekends.
customer_insights: Aku's Kitchen is a cozy takeout spot in West Philadelphia known for its delicious Ghanaian cuisine, particularly waakye and kelewele. The owner, Aku, is praised for her friendly service, making it a beloved local gem despite being open only on weekends.

address: 5514 Rising Sun Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19120, USA
googleReviews: Terrible Potato Greens & Rice was beyond nasty i will never go back overpriced and all i been to better African food restaurants for less money and way better quality taste! CHECK YOUR food  and look at it before you leave i shouldn’t have left that restaurant with the throw and not well done chicken! Super disappointed

For $30 I got 1/2 containers of food with 4 small pieces of meat and old sticky clumps of rice! I will never return to this restaurant EVER again!! The goat was so tough even a dog couldn’t chew it!! Don’t waste your time or money going there. When I called the restaurant the man said I paid that price for the RAW fufu lol no sir I order the Okra that came with fufu! So where is the rest of my food??? Will be getting my money back ASAP!!

I got egusi and fufu and it was good! It was oily but I assume that's how it's made. I ordered take out and the food was very hot when I picked it up. I ordered  goat but I was given chicken. I told the chef it was fine as long as I was charged for chicken. It paid $21 total so I thought it was a little pricey just for one meal. The place does not really support dine in as there was about 1 table with 2 seats and AC. I enjoyed. Wish it came with more fufu though. If you want to try African food, this is a good place to try!

Their food is overpriced!! I will stick to the Liberian restaurant. Potatoes green and cassava leaves are mainly a Liberian dish, and they don't cook it right. They told me 25 dollars for some tilapia and plantain, and I was out and never returned.

I wish I could put a video in here to actually show what they gave me. Why is my cassava leaf soup? Who ever packed my ordered saw exactly how it was and you guys still gave it to me. It was not cooked properly and it was still served to me.
customer_insights: Palace African Restaurant in Philadelphia has received mixed reviews, with several customers expressing dissatisfaction regarding food quality and portion sizes. While some diners enjoyed specific dishes like egusi and fufu, many others criticized the pricing and preparation of their meals, suggesting that the restaurant may not be a reliable choice for authentic African cuisine.

googleReviews: Ordered the veggie combo and it was an amazing burst of flavor in every bite! Food came out fast, environment is cozy and staff is very friendly. Definitely will be coming back!

Great little place to get really good Ethiopian food in the city.  We had the restaurant to ourselves and enjoyed everything we ordered.  Only complaint is they put one of the chicken dishes on the player with the vegetarian sampler and my wife is vegetarian.

Ive been here several times, always amazing quality food! The Ethiopian food is really well spiced and tender meat, lots of vegetarian options too. Smoothies, great coffee, and some simple wraps and sandwiches as well. Friendly staff, fun atmosphere. Nice to eat in but also casual enough to chill if youre coming by yourself. Huge portions, I usually take leftovers. Super close to Rittenhouse Square!

Truly delicious!
Veggie combo is healthy and filling. One order was enough for two hungry people, but we got a second just for the left overs!
Very delicious food. Great variety of dishes. I've been to a couple of Ethiopian restaurants, but they had even more dishes available here than I've seen before. Friendly staff.
customer_insights: Almaz Cafe offers a cozy atmosphere with a focus on flavorful Ethiopian cuisine, making it a great spot for casual dining. The restaurant is particularly praised for its vegetarian options and large portion sizes, appealing to both individuals and groups looking for a laid-back dining experience.

googleReviews:
Went here for a late night dinner since my friend had never had Ethiopian food before and wanted to try it. This is a neighborhood restaurant with 2 bars and a dining room. Both bars were busy. The downstairs bar was updated, but the dining room was pretty nondescript and empty.

I confirmed the kitchen was still open and we sat in the dining room. The server for the dining room was helping out in the downstairs bar so it took a while for him to take our order. My friend had to go to the bar and order some drinks in order to get his attention. When he came in to deliver our drinks and take our order he only brought my friend’s drink (spicy margarita). My drink (mango tequila sunrise) took a while to come out so he comped it.

We waited for quite some time before he came in again to check on us. He told us he went to check on our food and the kitchen was in the process of closing and hadn’t made our food. I was waiting for him to say just kidding the food is coming out, but he never did. He had to go work it out with the kitchen.

Our food finally came out and it was tasty. I ordered the veggie combo and he had the Abyssinia 1 and meat combo together. My friend really enjoyed the beef tartare. He got it cooked medium. I enjoyed the veggie combo.

I suggest going to the bar and ordering food there if you go late night. That’s what I’d do if I go back.

I got Meat Combo and the Kurt Tibs and the meat was so tender and seasoned well (the veggies were seasoned well too). It was the first time me and my friends tried Ethiopian food and we can't wait to have it again! I just wish the Baklava was bigger for the price it is. We spent a total of ~$80 for 2 meat combos one order of Kurt Tibs and 2 orders of the baklava. There was definitely more than enough to share with 4 people.

Last Friday, I went to Abyssinia and I LOVED IT. My 4 friends and I ordered 6 entrees (3 non vegetarian & 3 vegetarian) on a platter. We had the best social time finishing the HUGE platter; the portions are insanely good! All of us 5 were full by the end. However, I cannot emphasize how delicious every single bite was. The meat was so tender!! I will be back!! And prices were relatively good too for what you get!

Abyssinia is a wonderful find. The food is high quality, flavorful, and beautifully presented — you can taste the care and freshness in every bite. The décor is simple, but the warmth of the staff and the excellence of the cuisine more than make up for it.

A relaxed, welcoming spot that delivers authentic Ethiopian flavors and great value. Definitely worth a visit.

I don't drink anymore, but I love the quirkiness of this restaurant/bar building and if I did drink still, this place would be a really awesome stop.

Solely based on the food, it's decent. The injera was too dry and thin for me, but everything tasted good. Service was good, but the place is really worn down.

I probably won't come back, mostly because the food was just so so.
customer_insights: Abyssinia offers a casual dining experience with authentic Ethiopian cuisine, making it a great spot for late-night meals and social gatherings. While the service can be slow at times, the generous portions and flavorful dishes, like the veggie and meat combos, leave a positive impression on diners.

googleReviews: Ethiopian cuisine is easily among the top ten in the world when it comes to variety and flavor, and if marketed like other international cuisines, it could have a huge impact on the culinary scene. Unfortunately, this place doesn’t do it justice. The food lacks authenticity, with weak seasoning and poor cooking techniques. Most dishes don’t come close to the rich, flavorful, and finger-licking goodness of real Ethiopian food. The magic of Ethiopian cuisine lies in its seasoning and slow cooking, both of which are missing here.

Nice resturant. Its very low key which I like. The food was good and well priced. Ordered a vegetarian platter with kaffa tibs. Everything was delicious. Huge portion. Could definitely feed 2-3 people. There was 2 of us and we still had leftovers to take home
One of my favorite West Philly spots! Very relaxed atmosphere and usually not crowded. There is wifi and no one minds if you hang out for a few hours. The food is great too!

Excellent experience! Located in a less than desirable part of town but the food did not let us down at all! Everything was high quality and tasty. While some food may seem bland at times, you can simply salt to taste. Many spicy options are available. Great smoothies also! Menu is online, just scan QR code.

I don't like leaving bad reviews on local owned places, but I do it here in hopes that they make a change. The food, vibes and service were great. I was about to leave with a very positive experience, then I got the check and my tea was over twice the price listed on the sign!

I asked the server and she gave me an apologetic smile and said she knows, everyone complains about it, those signs are the prices from 10 years ago... Okay? So shouldn't those have been changed, I don't know, 9 years ago when you changed the prices?

The tea and hot chocolate options don't even come up on the QR code menu, so there is no idea to know what you're being charged. Negligent at best, manipulative at worst.

I'll try another spot next time.
customer_insights: Kaffa Crossing offers a relaxed atmosphere with generous portions of Ethiopian cuisine, making it a great spot for casual dining. While some reviews highlight inconsistencies in food authenticity and pricing transparency, the overall vibe is friendly and accommodating, appealing to groups and casual diners alike.

address: 36 E Lancaster Ave, Ardmore, PA 19003, USA
googleReviews: I really enjoyed my time at this place. I got the Doro Wot, and it was delicious! I will say that the injera is very filling, and the taste was a little surprising. It was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I was very pleased. Their banana bread is so good and tastes really fresh/homemade. The service was great, the chef walked around to each table greeting everyone. Thanks guys!

This mom and pop owned restaurant is a hidden gem. The owners are so sweet and are very patient explaining each dish as well as showing the proper authentic way to eat the dishes. Great atmosphere and the food was delicious. You will not be disappointed even the left overs hit. The traditional macchiato was really good of course.  Side note the restroom was so pretty and very considerate having feminine productions (pads & tampons), lotions, and soaps. There are no negatives with this spot.

Tesh and his family own this amazing, quaint gem of a restaurant and it is phenomenal vibes, food, flavor, and comfort. I brought my dad who has never tried Ethiopian food and historically doesn't love food with as much flavor as African cuisine tends to. But this family blew it away with their delivery! Every dish was amazing and created with love. I can't wait to come back with more of my friends and family. Thank you for a great dinner!! highly recommend!!

This was my first time trying Ethiopian food and I am so happy I went here for it! The food was excellent, flavorful, and fresh. The smaller meat platter was enough for 2 people to share, the tea was delicious, and the atmosphere was so warm, comforting, and artistic. The price to food quality/quantity was very fair. The staff was so welcoming, kind, and patient. You can tell they care a lot about their work and are excellent in their craft—especially the owner who came over to us! It felt like a home-cooked meal and I will absolutely be coming back.

Eshkol Ethiopian Restaurant is an absolute 10/10. From the moment we walked in, the hospitality was unmatched—warm, inviting, and truly caring. The food was incredible, bursting with authentic flavors and rich spices that clearly come from deep cultural roots. What made the experience even more special was learning the history behind each dish; you can feel the love and tradition in every bite. It was genuinely a pleasure to dine here, and I can’t wait to come back!! 🍽✨
customer_insights: Eshkol Ethiopian Cuisine & Cafe is a cozy, family-owned restaurant that offers an authentic Ethiopian dining experience. Patrons rave about the warm hospitality, flavorful dishes, and the inviting atmosphere, making it a great spot for both newcomers to Ethiopian cuisine and seasoned enthusiasts.

googleReviews: Really enjoyed their awaze beef tibs, lamb stew, and the beef dish that’s mixed with greens. Vege combo is ok not too impressive. (Got lamb tibs last time which was not very good.) glad that we gave it another try and the other meat dishes are so good. Injera is super good too! Price is very reasonable. Would come again or get take outs!!!

Great spot!! We started with the Tematim salad (order this, so unique and fresh and zingy) and veggie sambusas.  Yebeg awaze tibs was amazing, such a flavorful dish and perfectly spiced. My girlfriend had never had Ethiopian food before and absolutely loved the veggie combo. The injeera was fresh and delicious. Service was good and staff were friendly.

We are a couple with two young kids, and we have been coming to Amsale Café on Walnut Street for years. Without a doubt, this is our favorite restaurant in Philadelphia, and it is also our children’s favorite! The food is as close to home-cooked traditional Ethiopian as you can imagine. It is delicious, affordable, and served by a family that is kind, friendly, gentle, and sweet.

Over the years, our kids and the owners have developed a special relationship. Our kids always hug them when we arrive, draw them pictures, and it is beautiful to see. When we tell our kids we are going to Amsale Café, they are thrilled, and so are we.

Our kids, who can be quite picky eaters, absolutely love the different options here, especially the amazing, delicious beef Alcha, which they ask for every time. We always order the meat and veggie combo, which is an incredible amount of flavorful, beautifully seasoned food with a huge variety to enjoy.

There is no doubt this is not only our favorite restaurant in Philadelphia, but our favorite restaurant ever!!! It has truly become like a second home. We all feel unbelievably comfortable there, and we will continue coming for years.

Thank you to the owners and their family for being so wonderful and for making every meal feel special!

Incredible Ethiopian food made by a kind family--such a cozy spot too! We had the meat and veggie combo and got to try a dozen or so different dishes. We loved all of them. The meats were especially delicious, wonderfully spiced, and all very unique flavors. I can't wait to return to try more dishes. This was the best Ethiopian food I've had in Philly, DC, or NYC, and it is remarkably affordable too. Glad to see they are getting some well deserved recognition on the Philadelphia Inquirer's 76 list.

I only got takeout tonight, but the food was wonderfully authentic and delicious. My order was ready when I got there and I was able to get home quickl and enjoy my dinner. I look forward to coming back and eating at the restaurant.
customer_insights: Amsale Cafe is a beloved Ethiopian restaurant in Philadelphia known for its authentic, home-cooked meals and friendly service. Families appreciate the cozy atmosphere and the variety of flavorful dishes, making it a great spot for both casual dining and introducing new diners to Ethiopian cuisine.

googleReviews: First time. Popped in here one late afternoon. Three other folks were sitting at the bar with me. Super chill environment. The service was accommodating because I asked to change the TV channel and they were very obliging. Agreeable.

Came here cause we heard they have a Kenyan chef. Servers had a flat effect and didn't make any effort, the dude behind the bar seemed like he didn't even want to be there. Injera bread was cold, could've at least put it in the microwave for 10 seconds. Ugali was too soggy, greens had no tomatoes and tasted like they were the frozen ones and just microwaved.  Beef fry was tasteless. I did like the beef that came with the injera and the samosas were the best item.

I can’t tell you how good the food was. I was fastening at the time I went to this retirement event. What I can say is that the atmosphere was great and the service was awesome. They didn’t bother us, they didn’t have an attitude or anything like that. We were deep up there on the second floor too. They also have a pool table which I think is great as well as two bars available if needed. Great place to throw an event.

I.....I've never had this experience before. I sat down at the bar to watch the sixers. And waited. And waited.

The kid next to me kept trying to get the bartender's attention, I thought to order....NO, they were TRYING TO LEAVE but couldn't get the bartender to close them out. Dear audience, it was an entire hour before that person got dealt with. I kept laughing as folks *right next to me* , who *arrived after me* were being served. And I was still waiting.

And yet I persisted. In the end I saw the positives: at least I didn't drink too much. I got served about 15 minutes after that poor kid got released from their sentence. I wisely paid cash (aha! No check to wait for later, haha!), but decided to throw caution to the wind and order food. Just one simple dish: ful. Room temp fava beans. After about 30 minutes, the bartender walked past me with the dish twice, not remembering that I was the one who ordered. They then poured me a drink I didn't order, not as a comp but apparently just a mistake because they asked what name my tab was under (I had no tab, I had paid cash).

Still, great vibes, and maybe one day I'll find out the secret to getting served. I probably didn't help my cause by tipping 10%, but it felt ethically wrong to tip properly after having that experience. Hey, if you've ever wanted to go to a bar, watch a game and just be left alone while surrounded by cool people who are having fun, fantastic choice. 10/10.

This place was a huge disappointment. There’s no staff, just one guy running the bar, taking orders, and serving everyone.
Service was incredibly slow, portions were small, and the food didn’t taste fresh. Then I found a hair in my food, and when I told him, he laughed and pretended to pull hair from his shirt to drop into my plate. I was completely disgusted.
No apology, no accountability, just a joke. Completely unhygienic and disrespectful. Never going back.
customer_insights: Gojjo offers a unique Kenyan dining experience in a chill environment, but service can be inconsistent and food quality varies. While it has potential for casual gatherings and watching sports, it may not be ideal for special occasions due to reported service issues.

googleReviews: I actually wanted to eat here but it took +1hr leaving Roots picnic that the kitchen was already closed when I arrived.  As such I had a couple of PBRs until the bartender gave last call an hour early.  It was a Sunday night and all the ladies left, can't fault that logic.

This review is long overdue.  My husband and I had dinner here several months ago.  We were served food that never should have seen the light of day.  The chicken was inedible, burnt to a crisp, hard as leather, mostly grizzle and completely tasteless.  It was covered in stuff, so you couldn't see it until you started eating. I can't believe that the person in the kitchen thought it was okay to put this on a customer's plate.  We also spent the evening quite sick to our stomachs once we got home. I LOVE Ethiopian food, and we regularly eat at an Ethiopian restaurant near our home.  We were in West Philly and thought we would try one of the many Ethiopian restaurants in the area - should have gone home to our lovely neighborhood Ethiopian restaurant.
Will the Bartender's !! ALL THAT !! He's a good brother that mixes GREAT drinks, just ask him. Had a vegetarian dish that to me ,was GREAT !! Don't mind the picture 😄

The food was trash. Don't ever order the lamb the chicken tibs was a waste of money. TRUST ME SAVE UR MONEY..
The bartender was nice..
Different type of atmosphere cool place to eat and mangle
customer_insights: Queen of Sheba offers a casual dining experience with a focus on Ethiopian cuisine. While the atmosphere is laid-back and suitable for social gatherings, customer feedback highlights significant issues with food quality and service, suggesting a need for improvement in kitchen standards.

googleReviews:
I think my husband found this spot on TikTok and we both wanted to try it next time we were in Philly.

We shared:
- Half Chicken, Lemon Turmeric
- Half Chicken, Spicy Berbere

The fried chicken was fantastic. I loved both seasonings. The spicy was probably my favorite. It wasn't all that spicy, but it was flavorful.

If you like fried chicken, I'd highly recommend checking this spot out.

Everything I’ve had here is great! The chicken is super crispy and juicy, and the drinks and dipping sauces are all good too. I got a chicken stew with injera yesterday, which was filling and flavorful. Can’t wait to try more of their menu!

Also the surrounding area is pretty and nice to walk in, and parking is always free and easy.

I had heard some great reviews from food bloggers - so my expectations were set to high.  Sadly I was disappointed.  My friend and I arrived right at opening time.  We each ordered the fried chicken sandwich.  It was dry and leathery.  My guess is they reheated the chicken from the previous day as it was hot on one side of the sandwich only. The pickles and sauce were tasty.  I am hoping this was a one off - and may try it again.

I’ll have to come back when I’m hungry I forced myself to come out here since I’ve wanted to try for few years.  Had the half chicken, collard greens n Mac n cheese all of which seemed under seasoned but idk the chicken was good n while I wish for more heat I forgot to add sauces.  Was hoping the collard greens would have ham hock but did not and was kind of blandish and Mac n cheese was ok wished for more cheese lol but I’ll have to come back for the doro bet which I’m told is spicy.  I got the sweet kerkede was too sweet for me this day lol.  I should have went with first gut call of the wings and doro bet. Nice staff and good service.

Trying this restaurant for the first time ordering through uber eats. I ordered the spicy fried chicken, Mac and cheese and fries. The packaging for the Mac and cheese and fried chicken was fine . The packing for the fries was horrible!!! They put my fries in a paper bag! Unsanitary!!!! Why wouldn’t you put the fries in a platter style package????!  The flavor on the fries and chicken was good , but the Mac and cheese was bad. Not cheesy or baked. It tasted like instant Mac and cheese.  presentation sucked! I will not be ordering from here again.
customer_insights: Doro Bet is a casual eatery in Philadelphia known for its flavorful fried chicken, particularly the spicy options. While many patrons rave about the crispy texture and unique seasonings, some have experienced inconsistencies in food quality, particularly with takeout orders. The venue is suitable for casual outings and is a local favorite for groups.

googleReviews: Quiet, cozy, friendly.  They also offer a small selection of Ethiopian groceries.  Coffee was delicious. Deep flavor without being super bold.  Excellent place to have a cup of Joe and relaxe for a few min. Took off a star for food my bagel wasn’t super fresh but it was still good🤷🏾‍♂️

I love this cafe - normal coffee options and delicious sourdough bagels. Most of the food options are Ethiopian - everything from small sambusa pastries perfect for a snack, to cheap injera wraps perfect for a light lunch, to full on brunch and lunch options. Quiet but lively atmosphere

Follow me on Instagram for more reviews! @hopeless_ramen_tic

📍 Alif Brew & Mini Mart - Philadelphia, PA
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Food:

Injera Platter
– The spicy chicken was perfectly cooked, with just the right amount of heat and flavor.
– The beef tibs were tender and packed with rich, smoky berbere spice.
– The mild lentils had a bright, subtle flavor that my boyfriend loved.
– The spicy lentils were my favorite of the lentils—flavorful with a distinct taste from the mild ones and not overwhelmingly spicy.
– The green beans and carrots were well-seasoned and delicious.
– The sides were awesome: the homemade cheese, stewed mushrooms, and more—you truly can’t go wrong with any of them!

Drinks:

Lavender Latte
– Hands down the best lavender latte I’ve ever had, and I’ve tried plenty!
– Perfectly balanced with sweetness, creaminess, and a strong lavender note.

Alif Special
– Wonderfully fragrant, with bold ginger notes that made it feel cozy and seasonal.
– Such a unique coffee, perfect for fall and winter.

I was so grateful to be invited to this incredible spot. My boyfriend and I had an amazing time exploring their menu. The staff were incredibly warm and welcoming, and everything from the coffee to the food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented.

What sets Alif Brew apart is their dedication to creating a true “third space”—a much-needed communal place for people to gather, relax, and connect. They even host Ethiopian Buna ceremonies, roasting coffee beans on-site and inviting guests to enjoy the fresh brew while socializing.

To top it all off, they have an adorable mini mart filled with unique international snacks. I highly recommend stopping by this gem of a café. I’ll definitely be back!

Date Visited: 12/1/2024

Outside of the traditional Ethiopian food and Coffee being great at Alif Brew, they offer many Ethiopian Groceries like Teff Flour, Ambo Water, Berbere Seasoning, etc.

I always stop by to grab the Vegetarian Platter but today specifically, I ended up pairing it with the Biriz (which is a drink they made with fermented Honey and Turmeric) which was great.
I went in for dinner, and the food was absolutely delicious. I definitely recommend this place for proper Ethiopian food.
customer_insights: Alif Brew & Mini Mart Inc. is a cozy and friendly Ethiopian café in Philadelphia, known for its delicious coffee and unique food offerings. The venue creates a communal atmosphere, perfect for casual gatherings, brunch, or a relaxed first date.

googleReviews: The atmosphere of the restaurant was good for a game night dinner, go eagles. Service was good and the bartender was attentive. Food was okay, however as it could have been warmer and the Njerra fresher.

Good food but the waitress seriously messed up. She said it was her first day but she clearly doesn’t speak English. We ended up paying extra for entrees we didn’t want because she misunderstood us. Would go here again but would leave if she was working that night.

Picture a neighborhood dive bar with folks watching baseball and a huge beer list! Then an auntie in the back making delicious Ethiopian food. Does that sound good to you because it sounds good to me! A delightful place to hang out, grab food and drink!

I love coming here for an early dinner and a beer. I get the beef and rice or the bigger plate with injera if I'm starving. I've been here at least five times and I've found the food pretty consistent and delicious, although I love food and am easy to please. I love that its unpretentious and reliable and something other than fries and wings.
Had the chicken over rice is was splendid , flavorful and perfect portions. Came with a side salad for only $12.00. The customer service was amazing !!! Will be back
customer_insights: ERA is a casual neighborhood dive bar that offers a unique blend of Ethiopian cuisine and a lively atmosphere, making it a great spot for game nights and casual hangouts. While the food is generally well-received, service can be hit or miss, particularly with new staff.

googleReviews: I’m not sure why this hasn’t really been mentioned but their Ethiopian food offerings are legit! Run.. don’t walk! Really cute hole in the wall that while yes.. they offer pizza, their Ethiopian is what you should be going in for!! So glad I found this neighborhood gem! Get the meat combo, it’s a little bit of everything including veg!

I ordered a Buffalo chicken Stromboli with certain instructions,  not only was it not made to my desire it wasn't made as described and had some odd tangy hot sauce. I decided to give it another go however I tried a cheese calzone this time simple as can be. Haha so I thought!! Come to find out it literally mozzarella and bread.
