googleReviews:
Delicious!!! Literally so unexpectedly good, I didn’t know what I was walking into, my girlifriend took me as a surprise. Apricot Stone blew me away, truly! It was so incredibly flavorful and filling. The Shrimp Saganaki was the best dish I’ve had in a long time in Fishtown, if not the best. Marvelous.
Grape Molasses ice cream is a wonderful accompaniment to the Armenian Coffee. Feels like  a cozy home cooked meal. Thank you mama Ishkhanian!

Our waitress Summer and the owner Ara were so kind and hospitable ❤️

This place is awesome. I was honestly blown away. The staff really knows the food and explained the cultural significance of the dishes, which made the experience even better.
We ordered a bit of everything. It took a little while to come out, but everything was super fresh and full of flavor.
The highlight of the night was definitely the dessert. If they ever opened a dessert shop, I’d go every day. The ice cream was incredible—so creamy and made with really high-quality ingredients.
This Armenian restaurant is so so good! Such delicious food. If you like Middle Eastern food in general you owe it to yourself to visit this place!

Ok. First off. Great food, hands down. As a person who has traveled to the Middle East and Mediterranean, this is some high-quality food. They clearly are a family from the counties in which the food is served and the food is authentic. If stopping in, they have a selection of dishes for two people that allows you to choose, and it is delicious! The skewers, the eggplant, the hummus, the tabbouleh was fantastic. The atmosphere was a little lacking but it's ok because it felt like a family-oreiented place, and the service mirrored that. I felt special just eating there. I am looking forward to coming again. If you crave Middle Eastern Arabic/Greek food, you need to go there. It is worth the time!

My husband and I first had their food when they catered for a friend’s wedding. Seriously the best wedding food we’d ever had! We were planning our own wedding, so we visited for a date night to try more dishes and were impressed again. Apricot Stone catered our wedding last year and we are still getting compliments to this day, no joke. This evening we had another date night and were not disappointed. We did the dinner for two, tried some new dips and had our favorite skewers and shawarma. Everything is excellent. The service was prompt and friendly, our server was very helpful with her recommendations. We sat on the patio - we do miss their old location but it was still a pleasant evening to be outside. Family friendly. Can’t recommend enough!
customer_insights: Apricot Stone BYOB offers a delightful Armenian dining experience with authentic, flavorful dishes that evoke a cozy, home-cooked feel. The attentive service and family-oriented atmosphere make it an excellent choice for date nights and casual gatherings.

googleReviews: Lovely little Greek restaurant near the penitentiary with fresh food. Went on a Saturday night at ~6:30pm without a reservation and were seated quickly. We ordered the fries and charcoal sampler for 2. Fries were cut circular which I had never seen but doesn't come with any sauce. Charcoal sampler was good but the chicken breast was dry, tzatziki saved it.

This place was great, we got the spicy feta appetizer, calamari, and some lamb dish (my friend ordered for the both of us so I’m not sure specifics).
The spicy feta app was probably my favorite thing, but also dang the calamari was so fresh tasting. Also our waitress was incredibly sweet and made our experience all the better. I have nothing bad to say about our experience!

They allow BYOB (we didn’t bring anything so I’m not going to let this impact my review)but have an uncorking fee of $15 which is quite steep imo.

My wife and I stopped in after touring Eastern State Penitentiary. We ordered the cold appetizer sampler, a salmon sandwich, and a lamb sandwich. Everything tasted amazing. It was a treat to have authentic Greek food we can't get at home. I highly recommend Zorba's for anyone in the area looking for a bite to eat. We paid about $45 before tip for the two of us but we did have the appetizer and all of the food was high quality.

I thought Zorba was pretty good. The service was pretty slow but could have been the time we got there maybe transitioning from lunch to dinner. The food was serviceable but I think the appetizer sampler was the best thing; other stuff was kind of weirdly thrown together and under salted. The spicy feta dip, however, I would eat that with a spoon.
Grilled octopus was absolutely amazing. The other dishes we’re too. I’ve always wanted to try this place and it did not let me down. So fire. Will be back.
customer_insights: Zorba's Tavern is a casual Greek restaurant known for its authentic and fresh dishes, making it a great spot for a relaxed meal. The BYOB policy with an uncorking fee and the friendly service enhance the dining experience, although some dishes may vary in quality.

googleReviews:
Beautiful modern interior with cool music vibes, made our evening dinner even more awesome. Our server was Kevin S. and he was excellent throughout the meal. We were here on the early dinner (6pm) on a weeknight so it was not crowded when we arrived. But, definitely filled up as the night went on.
We began with the 3 spread mezza plate which was excellent. Next was the Cretan Village Salad which we split, and that too was perfect. Entrees were the Lamb Chops and the Short Rib dinners. I could not ask for better on either of these dishes. Lamb cooked perfectly as requested. And the short rib just pulled apart beautifully and had a great juicy flavor. We were both very very happy with all aspects of this evening a Almyra.

Dining experience was exceptional, characterized by both the quality of the cuisine and the inviting atmosphere. The ambiance was truly remarkable, complemented by outstanding food.

Specifically, the lamb ribs, various spreads, cocktails, lamb chops, Chilean sea bass, and gelato were all prepared to an excellent standard to our taste buds.

The atmosphere was further enhanced by the music selection, the lively crowd, the sophisticated lighting, and the overall positive vibes.

The service provided by Alex and Sky was amazing; they were not only welcoming and engaging but also prompt with Smiles

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit  and highly recommend it as a must-visit destination in Philadelphia.

10/10 recommend! This was my second time going for a birthday dinner and we were not disappointed at all! The food was delicious and the drinks were great. I'll definitely be returning for a third time. The dips are amazing. The hummus was my fav!!

Best greek in Philly, we had 5 spread apps, crispy spanakopita, lamb chops and lobster pasta, everything was so delicious authentic tastes. Meat so soft and tender, amazing flavors combined with european atmosphere. DJ was awesome also

The food at Almyra is delightful. I love that the patrons take the dress code seriously. Everyone was dressed to the nines, and many were celebrating birthdays. The staff ensured that our water glasses were never empty and that empty dishes didn't linger on our table too long. Truly appreciated the attentiveness. It is a bit loud in the restaurant and I didn't like that diners sit so close to each other, but all in all, it was a good experience and I would definitely go back again. Dress up!
customer_insights: Almyra Restaurant offers an exceptional dining experience with a vibrant atmosphere and high-quality Mediterranean cuisine. Guests rave about the attentive service, delicious lamb and seafood dishes, and the stylish ambiance, making it a popular choice for special occasions and casual nights out.

googleReviews:
I wanted to share some feedback about my order from yesterday. My husband and I called ahead and specifically asked if the baklava was made with pistachios, because we did not want walnut. The gentleman on the phone confirmed that it was pistachio, so we placed the order and picked it up.

However, when I opened it at home, it was the opposite of what we were told. The inside was completely walnut, with just a small sprinkle of pistachios on top. Pistachio baklava should be filled with pistachios inside, not just decorated on the surface, so this was very misleading.

In addition, the baklava was extremely heavy and soaked in honey syrup, which overpowered everything. It didn’t taste like traditional baklava at all, and I wasn’t able to eat it.

We only came for the baklava, so this was very disappointing. After this experience, I’m honestly not comfortable trying the food again unless the quality improves. I’m sharing this so the issue can be addressed and other customers don’t have the same experience.

Sahara Grill really hit the spot. Prices are super reasonable, the place feels cozy, and everyone working there was so friendly. Food came out fast and everything was tasty. Honestly, no complaints—just a really solid meal.
Lovely meal and friendly service. I got the Couscous with Chicken and Hummus and Baba Ganoush. Everything was healthy and delicious. Highly recommend.

The restaurant was really welcoming, we felt like at home. The food was great, comforting food, amazing seasonings, and good portion.
The server was so nice, and welcoming!
I recommend 100%.

If you’re going here I recommended getting the Tayouk Chicken as it’s that great traditional Lebanese crispy on the outside and tender & juicy on the inside! However, make sure to review the bill at the end carefully because the tip may be included.
customer_insights: Sahara Grill offers a cozy and welcoming atmosphere with a focus on Mediterranean comfort food. While many customers praise the friendly service and tasty dishes, there are some concerns regarding the consistency of specific items like baklava. Overall, it's a solid choice for casual dining and pregame gatherings.

googleReviews: I stopped by Kamal’s in Reading Terminal Market and had one of the freshest smoothies I’ve ever tasted! I got the strawberry, kiwi, and mango blend—it was perfectly balanced, refreshing, and full of flavor. If I hadn’t been heading straight to the airport, I definitely would’ve ordered a larger size. Highly recommend for a delicious, fresh pick-me-up!

My husband and I stopped in reading market for some fresh juice and falafel sandwiches. The guy who took our order was very friendly and the service was fast. We asked to make it Spicy and they had a really good harissa! Really crispy falafel. 5 star falafel sandwiches.

This shop is in the Reading Terminal Market in Philly. It’s a very crowded place as there are so many food shops in this market. I purchased the large sized  Turkish coffee shake with dates, flaxseed and chia seeds. The taste was bitter even with the dates. It will be nice if they have the options to add  nuts to the shake. If you like the taste of bitter coffee then you will like this Turkish coffee shake.  The queue gets long in this store but they are able to deliver the drinks and food items pretty quickly.

Got a lamb gyro, 2 beef kibbeh, and a potato somosa. There was only one person taking orders and answered the phone while taking my order. I get it was busy, but the customer that is standing in front of you is already there and should really be priority. The gyro and kibbeh was good. Gyro came with a lot of meat. Kibbeh had good flavor but did not come with any sauce. Samosa was very dry. Totally not recommended for $4.16 after tax. No sauce came with the samosa. Overall, ok food will try the Greek gyro right across from them next time.

ordered at the counter today and my order was ready in less than 5 minutes! extremely fast and friendly service. I ordered the Kiwi, Orange, and Banana Smoothie and it was the best smoothie I've ever had! the falafel platter is also delicious and so filling. can't recommend enough
customer_insights: Kamals Middle Eastern Cuisine is a fast-casual eatery located in Reading Terminal Market, known for its fresh smoothies and crispy falafel. While the service is generally quick and friendly, some items may lack sauces or flavor balance, making it a good spot for a quick bite rather than a formal dining experience.

googleReviews: This establishment was excellent from start to finish. I was warmly greeted as soon as I walked in, promptly seated, and offered a menu along with a starter of pita bread and various sauces. Since it was my first time dining here, the staff kindly suggested meal and beverage options, which I truly appreciated. Every recommendation arrived exactly as it should—fresh, hot, or refreshingly cold. To top it all off, after my meal I was treated to a complimentary cup of hot tea, which was both excellent and exactly what I needed after such a spectacular dining experience. I will definitely be returning—and bringing friends and family with me!

The bread and sauces were delicious but the entrees were 3/5. The chicken was very dry and felt something was missing. The rice also didn’t feel too good. May be just a bad day. High chair available for kids.

Bon Kif Grill absolutely exceeded my expectations! I ordered the branzino and it was perfection —fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The salad was crisp, bright, and easily one of the best I’ve had at a Mediterranean spot. I finished the meal with their delicious tea as my “dessert,” and it was the perfect warm, soothing touch to end the night.

A special shoutout to Mr. Fathi — his service was truly top tier. Attentive, welcoming and very appreciative, he made the entire experience even better.

The food and service was excellent. I’ll definitely be back!

Best Mediterranean food I've had in years! We ordered the platter a selection of different meat. It was amazing. My favorite was the lamb chops it was perfectly cooked and so juicy, the beaf and chicken Shawarma was also really good.
You have to try the hummus with olive oil, amezing! so authentic, I felt like I was having hummus for the first time. We also tried the lentil soup for our apps. It was so rich and tasty.
If you like mint, you have to try the mint tea! I will  definitely be back.

We had our best feeling in this restaurant. Mr. Fathi welcomed us with gracious smile and served food in a way it seemed like we were guests who he was waiting for. I noticed that he also did the same courtesy to the other tables. One of my children was exhausted on the way to Philadelphia as we didn't find any vegetarian food on the way, but once we entered the restaurant, we all felt very homely. We arrived late, less than half an hour before their closing time, but the hospitality Mr. Fathi showed to us made us feel extremely grateful.
The restaurant was very clean, the food was very tasty, and was all served with love. The baklava was so delicious! A visit here can definitely make your trip more memorable. Thanks to the amazing service and food, we had a beautiful welcoming to Philadelphia after our long journey.
customer_insights: Bon Kif Grill offers a warm and welcoming atmosphere with attentive service, particularly highlighted by Mr. Fathi's hospitality. While the food quality is generally praised, there are mixed reviews regarding specific entrees, suggesting a focus on their standout dishes like lamb chops and branzino.

googleReviews: This is a Lebanese/French spot with an interesting menu that fuses the two together. Shakshuka, Mediterranean burrito, and many items that came with baguettes. The food was great, with lots of different dishes that were meat or fruit forward, carb heavy like sandwiches with fries or carb light with a wrap. I liked that the quality of meat was better than I expected and the skirt steak on my sandwich was great.  The bread on both dishes (avocado toast and le fou) was really good and I loved that the fou was rich and heavy. The brioche was good, the meat was good, and they even provided a really hot hot sauce. Overall, I liked this place a lot

Was glad to have visited one of Philly's hot spot brunch places. The food was delicious and generous in size. Despite the seemingly smaller menu there's great variety in options, each bringing a different flavor profile. The workers were also really nice and accommodating. When they heard there was a birthday they put a candle in one of our orders.
Overall the food was not that pricey which was a bonus to see at the end. As long as you come early enough you can get seated right away avoiding the brunch crowd rush.

A popular spot in Philly for Lebanese x French fusion brunch 🇱🇧🥐✨

🥘 Red Shakshuka — rich tomato base with perfectly baked pita, absolutely amazing! Pair it with their Harissa Labneh, and it’s a flavor match made in heaven. 😍🔥

🥗 Mediterranean Platter — overall pretty solid! The za’atar pita was a bit on the strong side, but the Labneh was cool, refreshing, and super unique. 👍🏼💫

We came here for brunch and the line was long — clearly a popular spot! The wait to be seated took a while, but it was worth it once we sat down. The food was absolutely beautiful — honestly, it looked like art. Each plate was carefully presented, from the layers of whipped cream and fruit to the drizzle of sauces across the plate. And it tasted just as good as it looked — perfectly balanced sweetness that didn’t feel heavy at all. Only one critique — I think the coffee could be a bit better — it wasn’t bad, just not as amazing as the food. Overall, such a lovely experience.

Very yum !!! Was looking for a good brunch spot with my friends, no reservations but the wait wasn’t too long! Spend the time in the plant shop next door. Sooo many good interesting menu items I wanted to try so I will be back. I got the fromage omellete and my friend got the red curry something (the one with meat!!!)
customer_insights: Cafe La Maude is a popular brunch destination in Philadelphia, known for its unique Lebanese-French fusion menu that offers a variety of flavorful dishes. The atmosphere is trendy and casual, making it suitable for groups and casual dates, though it can get busy during peak hours.

googleReviews:
⭐️⭐️⭐️ (3/5)

We really wanted to like Laser Wolf. With a new baby at home, nights out are rare, so we hoped this would be a special one.

The setup overlooking the kitchen seemed fun at first, but the fixed chairs made it awkward to get in and out. The menu also isn’t as straightforward as it looks — “Salatim included” is confusing, and even after dining, it’s not 100% clear how it all works. Our server Eddy was helpful in explaining, but overall it feels like you’re paying for a bundle of food, much of which you may not want.

We ordered the sirloin shishlik ($52 for ~8oz) and the merguez. The meats were good but not worth the price. The salatim spread is plentiful, but I only took a few home (hummus, Lebanese potato salad, lutenitsa). Fries were easily the best dish of the night, the wings were tasty but messy with no wet nap provided, and the halloumi was very good. Dessert is included — we got both soft serve and sorbet — but again, it felt like cost buried in the mains rather than a bonus.

Eddy was kind and attentive, but the overall value just isn’t there. $50+ entrees paired with forced sides and dessert doesn’t add up, especially in a city with so many options. Glad we tried it, but unlikely to return.

Pros
•	Attentive and kind service (thanks, Eddy)
•	Fries and tehina ketchup were excellent
•	Halloumi and wings were solid
•	Dessert included (soft serve + sorbet, thanks again Eddy)

Cons
•	Confusing menu structure
•	Overpriced mains ($50+ for 8oz steak)
•	Too many “included” sides you may not want
•	No wet nap for messy wings
•	Overall poor value compared to other Philly spots

I’ve come out of my Google review slumber, just so that I can spread the message about how amazing Laser Wolf is (although I’m sure you already know that). I’ve heard so many good things about Laser Wolf… to the point where I started questioning if it was overhyped - I was terribly mistaken.

I decided to make the trek out to Philly (unknowingly on the worst day, due to all the political protests). However, I didn’t let that keep me down. I was on a mission - Laser Wolf.

As a quick prelude, I do want to mention that reservations here are hard to get. So be sure to book out weeks in advance … I was actually on the waitlist, until a 5PM dinner spot opened up. A bit early for me, but beggars can’t be choosers.

I get to Laser Wolf around 4:45PM, eagerly (and awkwardly) pacing around the building until the doors opened. Once 5PM hit, I was surprised by the volume of the people that showed up at the opening. Upon entry, I was greeted by warm smells and spices and a cool/casual interior. Plenty of space, comfortable seating, and nice decor.

The service was phenomenal. Our waiter was super kind and knowledgeable - explained how the whole process worked in perfect detail. For those who don’t know, when you come to Laser Wolf, you are just paying for the entrees, the salatim and the desserts are included. The salatim is basically a huge plate (with 10 smaller bowls) with different types of spreads, bites, appetizers. It also comes with hummus. The salatim by itself is already incredible. So fresh, so flavorful, and the hummus is by far the best hummus I’ve ever had. Also, don’t sleep on the fries… they are amazing - apparently they are brined and flash frozen to make them super crispy - so good! Our waiter actually hooked us up with a free order of fries, since we said we heard good things about them! What a legend! And then on to the meats, I got the chicken shishlik and the steak shishlik, both cooked to perfection. The juiciest kebab style meat I’ve ever had - and a great portion size, not too much, not too little, perfectly balanced with the salatim.

I really can’t express how much I enjoyed the entire experience. From the vibes to the service to the food, everything was on point. They even had specifically designed take away containers with 4 compartments for the salatim - they really thought through everything!

A quick heads up that a 20% service charge is already included on the bill. You don’t normally see that in US restaurants, but honestly the staff deserves every penny, and even some.

An absolute MUST try. There’s also a location in Brooklyn, but Philly is the OG. 10 out of 5 stars.

I had an absolutely amazing experience here! From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. The food was outstanding—each dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. The drinks were just as impressive, perfectly crafted and refreshing.
What really stood out, though, was the service. The staff were incredibly attentive, friendly, and genuinely seemed to care about making sure we had a great time. They were quick to offer recommendations and made sure everything was perfect throughout the evening.
Overall, this place exceeded all my expectations. Whether you're going for a casual night out or a special occasion, I highly recommend giving it a try. You won’t be disappointed!

Fantastic service, fantastic food. The server was wonderful and made us feel very valued as we chose to celebrate a special day at this restaurant. The Salatim has a variety of flavorful and interesting dishes, and the pita is fresh and fluffy. All the entrées were good as well. The dessert was the cherry on top. Would recommend for a delicious and hearty meal.

Amazing, innovations on Mediterranean food. The Hummus alone is worth the trip. Silky smooth and the pita is made per order.

We've been here several times. Parking can be tricky on certain nights. Plan an extra half hour for that.street parking tends to be full up.

Originally we had reservations for a Friday. We couldn't find parking and the local lots were full. We called to let them know and the honored our reservation and moved it to two weeks later on a Sunday.

We got in with no waiting and sat at the counter. Great view of the grill and cook stations. The food was great as always. After the pop slowed down, we wound up talking to one of the lead chefs about the menu, upcoming winter items being tested in the kitchen, how well everything ran and how everyone stepped in without being asked to cover.

Great experience, food, staff and vibe.
FYI, they put this on the bill that 20% is added so all employees get a good hourly rate. Way to look after your own. Points on that.
customer_insights: Laser Wolf offers a unique Mediterranean dining experience with a focus on grilled meats and a variety of flavorful salatim. While the service is noted as attentive and friendly, some diners find the pricing and menu structure confusing, leading to mixed reviews about overall value.

googleReviews:
I made the mistake of going there by myself. Unfortunately, I don't think I'm able to eat half a Peking duck all on my own, so I had to order the duck appetizer rolls.

And they were some of the juiciest, tastiest nibbles of duck I've ever had. If the full duck meals are just as good, then this place is legendary.

I decided to order the Sweet and Sour chicken - pretty good, large portion, enough to take half of it home. Food came out quick, and service was great. It's a nice place for a sit-in lunch.

10/10! One of my new favorite spots in Chinatown. We got the roast pork noodle soup w shrimp dumplings - the broth was unbelievable, roasted duck and pork over rice- amazing, and the beef chow fun, my personal favorite! My wife loved the lychee sake and I got an iced Thai tea. For all this, it was about $60, and we took so much home!
Highly recommend and will definitely be back.

Food here is amazing!
But their lazy Susan in the middle of the round tables is weird. It’s a glass top and there are no ball joints (?) under it to make it glide so you can spin it and share food. You actually have to manually turn the glass, and it’s super awkward and heavy and clumsy.

Aside from that, everything was great. Peking duck was great, of course. Very nicely crispy on the outside, with great flavors. The dumpling soup is not something i usually get, and the broth was just ok, but the dumpling was a big surprise! It was actually filled with a yummy meatball like filling, super tasty.

We were a big group so got a lot of different foods - i can’t remember all the names, but we did get a spicy beef dish that was also delicious. There was also one non spicy shrimp dish was was so good… but the chicken dish was just so so. That was the only dish i didn’t like. Everything else was super good.

We are just going through town, but my local friends tell me this is one of their local favorites. No wonder!

Do you like duck? Apparently this is the place to go if you’re looking for it. I had the sweet and sour chicken which was a 3.5/5. Mg gf didn’t care for the duck (sadly). The pork dumplings were amazing…not crispy but just so good. Service was pretty slow, and they weren’t busy but I wasn’t in a rush so who cares. Very friendly service. Liked the cocktail and the snow beer wasn’t bad.

Was in the area and remembered that this was one of the highest rated restaurants in the city. Sadly I’m not really sure how because while the service was decent the highlight of my meal was the cold glass of water to finish the meal. Was stunned when the fried dumplings had arrived at the table and they were deep fried dumplings with a wrapping bigger than the size of my palms. While the pork filling was good I just couldn’t get past the wrapping and couldn’t finish the portion. Decided to try the three meat vegetable plate as nothing could really go wrong with this but I was let down. Most of the meat came cold but the pork was pretty standard and tasted alright. Now one of my main issues came with the duck that came with skin that was the opposite of the expected crispy and half the pieces coming of bone. One of the pieces being entirely bones. They had to replace one of the meats with the beef which is totally fine but when the beef itself is mostly fat and tasting odd there is a problem. Not sure if this is every time but the sauce poured over the rice had a very strong alll spice flavor too. Not one of my favorite meals in the city and for them to be considered “one of the best” I was highly let down this time around.
customer_insights: Sang Kee Peking Duck House is a popular casual dining spot in Philadelphia's Chinatown, known for its delicious Peking duck and hearty portions. While the food receives high praise, some customers have noted inconsistencies in service and dish quality, particularly with certain meat dishes.

googleReviews: Would recommend making a reservation ahead of time. This restaurant gets really busy, especially during dinner hours. The food is good but I would say there are other great restaurants that will also fulfill your expectations. I would recommend the double fried mini skewers, it’s spicy and flavorful. The servers are very friendly and would occasionally check on us.

We ordered a few dishes, but only two truly stood out as five-star worthy! the Szechuan-style fish and the wood ear mushrooms. Both were bursting with flavor and perfectly balanced. The cucumber with garlic sauce & snow pea leave with garlic sauce are decent, though not as impressive as versions I’ve had at other Chinese restaurants. Unfortunately, the salt and pepper shrimp was a bit disappointing  because the shrimp didn’t taste very fresh, and the seasoning was too light to bring out much flavor.
Overall, it was still a good dining experience, and I’ll definitely come back to try more dishes from their menu.

We went on Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the place was packed full. We waited a long time to order but once we did the food came pretty quickly. We got mapo tofu, beef with peppers, twice cooked pork, spicy fried chicken, dumpling soup, and scallion pancake. Twice cooked pork was probably the best dish of the night, but everything was excellent, with the exception of maybe mapo tofu, it was just good but not addictive. A lot to look forward to the next time we go.
Food was delicious served family style. Party of 6 and bill was under $200. We didn't get acholic beverages. Everything was fresh! Celebrated my daughter's 19th bday! Parking across the street.

I will say everything I ate here was fantastic, but my most favorite dishes were the Cold Noodles, the Cumin Lamb, and the spicy white fish. Who doesn’t love a fried dish?!
The wood ear mushrooms had a wonderful tangy and spicy numbing flavor, I just wasn’t a big fan of the rubbery texture. Tea was comforting and a good palate cleanser. The potatoes were an interesting crunchy texture, and I liked them, but it was oily.
Service was fine and the atmosphere was great. It is a bit chilly so bring a jacket!
customer_insights: EMei offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on Szechuan cuisine served family-style. While some dishes stand out for their bold flavors, others may not meet expectations, making it a good spot for groups looking to explore a variety of flavors in a lively atmosphere.

googleReviews: Such a great experience. The waitress (owner? manager?) was great from the time I was seated. She provided recommendations for each area, from the tea, to the dimsum, to the main dish. I have only the best to say about each dish. The sweet soy on the shrimp rice roll, the dipping sauce, the soup in the soup dumpling-each was unique and flavorful. The atmosphere was great as well, giving a relaxed vibe while enjoying my dinner.

The restaurant is small, there is a long booth with tables and chairs on one side, a few tables in the corner and a small bar. I walked in and was seated with no wait. They dropped off a plastic menu with pictures and an order sheet, and you checked off what you wanted. There is no talking or communication with the server. The food comes out quickly in batches. I ordered soup dumplings, which looked small but were packed full of meat and had just the right amount of soup inside, pan-fried dumplings, shrimp balls, and shrimp fried rice. Everything was very tasty.
Food was delicious and was served quickly. The scallion pancakes are really fluffy. Highly recommend and it is great to share if you’re with a group.
Loved this meal. Everything was awesome. Veggies were delicious, bao was great and dumplings total joy 🤩 IPA beer to go with meal was nice too! Recommended

We arrived right after a massive event. There were several groups that had arrived before and after us, and no vacant seats. Despite how busy it was, the staff were well on top of it all, and got us seated quite quickly. Seeing them work so efficiently was honestly a bit mesmerizing. And even though they were so busy, they were still polite and friendly! Some of the best service I've had.

The food itself was spectacular, and arrived quickly as well. We're ordered several plates of dim sum, and everything was delicious. It's hard to recommend any specific item when every plate was great. Definitely worth checking out
customer_insights: Nom Wah Philadelphia offers a casual dining experience with a focus on delicious dim sum and quick service. The atmosphere is relaxed, making it suitable for groups and a good pregame spot, though it may not be ideal for more intimate occasions like first dates or anniversaries.

googleReviews:
TLDR: Avoid, I would not recommend to my enemy unless I really hated them.

🤢 Potential health violation? Dirty dishes replaced with “fresh” dirty dishes. (the new place setting had dried pieces of leftover food from the previous use)

💀 Sticky! Everything was sticky, grime sticky, not dumpling sauce sticky. The bottom of dish plates, the individual plates, the bowl, the spoon

💰Cash-only restaurant that charges tax (pick one, you know?)

—————————

We had tried this restaurant as a late night option at 9pm. Our one server was a gem—which is why I gave a 2 star instead of a 1 star. Other than that, the sheer cleanliness (or lack thereof) ruined the whole food experience—I was too grossed using the sticky utensils and plates let alone think about how “clean” the kitchen where the food is made is. 😷

decent food:
- shanghai soup dumplings (heavy hand with the sauce) 3/5
- crispy garlic lettuce — crunchy! 4/5
- salt and pepper wings — salty! good fry 3.5/5

Other food (1/5)
- shrimp dumplings had thick wrapper that was too chewy and felt frozen
- fish sour soup lacked flavor and spice
- garlic bean sprouts looked old and wilted, there was a layer of white film on top and the sauce was a little too thick and corn-starchy

This place has always been a favorite of mine, but the renovated location two doors down is down adds an amazing atmosphere and upscale ambience to the always fantastic food. On top of that, Ryan provides a level of service that is unmatched. I moved away years ago, and every time I come back to town I bring whoever I’m with to get pork soup dumplings. A favorite experience of mine, and I never leave hungry. Every time I leave, I can’t wait to come back. Love this place, don’t miss out!

We got a table right away on Sunday afternoon before it got too busy. The service was very fast. We order a pork soup dumpling and it was delicious. Then we had a salty duck and white rice. Duck comes with small pieces of bone in it. So be careful. Dried nodules with beef was very good also.
Only cash. Place was packed. I’d go back next time.

Cash only!  Dinner was great. I would have liked the Shanghai rice to be fried a little harder. But that would be my preference. It was good.
The crab rangoon was large and full.
The pork buns are soft and fluffy.
It was a great experience because of Mindy's attention to us.

Had heard a lot about this place and hence came here with high expectations. Unfortunately, it did not deliver. The pork soup dumplings were decent, but the chilli wantons and stir fried noodles missed the mark.
customer_insights: Dim Sum Garden is a casual spot known for its dumplings and late-night hours. While the food has its highlights, such as the pork soup dumplings, cleanliness issues and inconsistent quality have led to mixed reviews. It's a popular choice for a quick bite with friends, but may not be ideal for special occasions.

googleReviews: On this cold Thanksgiving day, all we wanted was something warm. This experience was more than I expected. The restaurant was warm and cozy. The music was relaxing, it was well lit, and clean. We choose this place because of it's high rating, it did not disappoint. The food was great.

Great food and GREAT experience. Jamie was so kind and heard my friend loved labubus so he brought out his whole collection and let us take photos! The food was amazing too and HUGE portions. I highly reccomend this restaurant to anyone. It’s a one of a kind in china town and they care about the quality of food they put out

bsolutely outstanding experience at Ji Bei Chuan in Philly’s Chinatown! The food is incredible—fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care. The hand-pulled noodles are some of the best I’ve ever had.

What really makes this place special is the personal touch from the owner. He greets guests warmly, checks on every table, and takes pride in explaining the dishes and their origins. You can feel how much love goes into both the food and the service.

If you’re looking for authentic flavors, generous portions, and genuine hospitality, Ji Bei Chuan is a can’t-miss stop in Chinatown. Highly recommend!

I'd give 100 stars if I could because Ji Bei Chuan is absolutely brilliant and knocks every single dish out of the park.  We flew into town for the weekend and although we sampled other eateries, we went back to Ji Bei Chuan because it is THAT AMAZING and I knew I'd regret it if I didn't.  No other places came close.  Picture perfectly tangy cucumber salad, delectable and savory braised beef, egg drop soup with an unmatched texture of egg and broth, and flawless, golden potato fritters.  The dumpling choices are numerous. We tried several and each one was full of respective flavor and a wonderfully rich, chewy texture.  Everything on the plate was impeccably fresh and beautifully presented.

For each dish that came with a dipping sauce, the server mixed the specific sauce directly before serving, for the table.  They served water with lemon already in it, as well, so this brought an additional clean and bright taste to every new bite.  I loved that.

It's meticulously clean and comfortable, and the service was incredible, as in they anticipated what we needed before we even asked and it was provided.

The owner was so funny and also so very kind, as well!  We ordered a whole bunch of stuff at once (everything looked so good we just ordered a lot of stuff - both times) and I'm so glad we made that choice.  Also, when we left, I asked if I could buy one of the reusable bags they have so I could take it home and remember how delicious everything was and he gave me a couple!  It was so kind of him because he didn't have to do that.

What I also appreciate is that they have dishes for every palate.  So, this is also a perfect place for picky eaters or someone who has specific food needs.

My companion said his only regret was not coming earlier each day so we could just eat 2 meals there and that day.

I could go on and on but I won't.  In short: the excellent reviews you see and the hype is real.  Everything is delicious and I cannot recommend this establishment enough.

I've never been to Philly before this trip but 100% I'll be coming back, and as soon as I get off the plane you'd better believe I'm making a beeline for Ji Bei Chuan.

Magnificent.
Great restaurant, we had the signature Fish Maw Chicken Soup and Mala Noodle Soup (spicy!). The owner was very kind too. Nice music in the background. Would recommend.
customer_insights: Ji Bei Chuan Philly is a beloved spot in Chinatown known for its authentic Chinese cuisine, particularly hand-pulled noodles and dumplings. Guests rave about the warm atmosphere, generous portions, and exceptional service, making it a must-visit for both locals and tourists.

venueName: Dim Sum House By Jane G's - Rittenhouse
googleReviews:
This resturant single handedly made me love coming to Philly. I'm already in love with Asian cuisine but this resturant is by far one of the best Asian restaurants I've been too!

I went and I got a lot of bit of everything. The sesame seed chicken was amazing, crunch with sweet tasty sauce WOW. The crab fried rice was another one of my favorites dishes! Never had it before and now I got to other places asking for crab fried rice. The dumplings, CHIEF KISS!

Please if you're in Philly, go to this restaurant! I'll be back in Philly next month and best believe to catch me there.

The food was good. However, there were several issues with the overall experience.

When I placed my order over the phone, I was charged slightly more than what the total would have been online, even after the usual online fees and tax. That doesn’t make sense.

They also don’t accept tap-to-pay, which is unacceptable in 2025.

No utensils or napkins were included in the bag, and I had to ask for chopsticks. That should’ve been automatic for takeout.

Lastly, there were a few feathers still on the chicken wings, which means they weren’t cleaned properly.

We came last night with 4 small children and had a great meal. The service was great, the food came quickly, and everything was delicious. The kids devoured the green beans, the egg tarts. I also loved the Dan Dan noodles and the pumpkin pancakes.

The dim sum here was a miss for me. It still tastes like Chinese food, but having tried dim sum in many places before, I felt that the food here was lacking in flavor. They also stopped making a good portion of the dishes that they show in the photo menu. The only ones they still offer are listed in the paper ordering menu, which was disappointing because we wanted several dishes shown on the photo menu. My favorite dish would be their pork soup dumplings. The egg tarts weren’t very crispy and the pickled garlic cucumber didn’t taste as good. The cucumbers also had some numbing spice, which might not be for everyone. Overall, it’s not a restaurant I’d be craving to visit again.

The staff was kind though! Decor looked nice and the restaurant was clean. They do take credit card.

Slightly above average Chinese food. It’s great for groups and sharing everything family style. My favorites were the Dan Dan noodles (super soft noodles and yummy sauce) and stewed beef and turnip. I did not like the spicy tofu fish as the fish was too fishy, and did not like the texture of the string beans, which felt like it was not cooked thoroughly, altho the taste was pretty good with the pickled vegetables on top. Other dishes were good as well, including the soup dumplings and dry pot chicken. We ordered a tequila shot but it tasted like it was diluted with 50% water. It also took a very long time for the waiters to even get us a pencil for marking the menu. But after we ordered the food came out quite quickly.
customer_insights: Dim Sum House By Jane G's in Rittenhouse is a casual dining spot that offers a variety of Asian dishes, particularly dim sum. While many patrons enjoy the food and find it family-friendly, there are mixed reviews regarding the flavor and service consistency. It's a good place for groups and casual outings, but may not be ideal for special occasions.

venueName: Nan Zhou Hand Drawn Noodle House
googleReviews: Amazing dumplings (recommend the sampler), scallion pancake, and hand pulled noodles. Each dumpling had a unique flavor. The scallion pancake was fried to perfection with each flaky layer standing out. The pulled noodles had the perfect amount of add-ins (vegetables, meats) and a flavor that stood out, but wasn't overpowering. Service was great from the time I sat down all the way through. It was busy, but the food came out hot and fast. Looks unassuming from the outside, which just adds to the vibe. Only note is that they only take cash or venmo, so be prepared.

Great classic noodles! This is the best noodle restaurant, in my personal beliefs, in Chinatown of Philly! I remember coming here when I was in high school. That’s how long this place has been open for!

I got the knife shaved noodles with lamb, overall very good with no complaints 5/5. The cold jellyfish appetizer is good, but maybe I just had the better version my mom made, so I gotta give this one 4/5. Lastly, the tomato egg noodles my husband got was just okay. It  was lacking in flavor, the noodles did not take on the flavor of the soup, 3/5.

I do however recommend anyone visiting Philly to visit this restaurant, given that there’s a variety of noodles and dishes that can satisfy lots of different people. Service is impeccable.

Nan Zhou is perfect for a hot bowl of hand pulled noodles. There isn't a lot to say about this small shop- compared to other spots in Chinatown they focus acutely on their famous noodle bowl and  that's the star attraction, and they don't do much else. This time I got the braised sliced beef noodle soup, which was spicy and rich with great pickled and leafy elements on the bowl as well. All the other noodle bowls seem pretty much the same but you can swap the protein for something else of your choice.

We also got a chicken skewer and peanut noodle sides which were nice, and standard. This is just a place that is an outstanding value ($14.50 for a huge noodle bowl) that hits the spot when you need it. Service is pleasant and the food came out very quickly. It knows what it's good at, and is a great option on a cold day!

If you have not tried hand pulled noodles, this place might be worth a visit.  They have a good diverse menu that offers hand pulled noodles in a wide variety of preparation, both soup style noodles, or fried noodles.  Besides the main attraction, they also have a good selection of Dim Sum, and classic Chinese dishes.  Portions were large for all of their entrees/dishes.  Bring a big appetite when you visit!

The interior has been updated since our last visit.  It seems to be more spacious.  Staff is very attentive to our needs.  I do believe they only take cash, but an ATM machine is available.

Nice spot for late night hand pulled noodles. The texture of their homemade noodles is perfect, and the broth is really nice as well. Great for a cold day or night. Loved the different flavored dumplings set as well.
customer_insights: Nan Zhou Hand Drawn Noodle House is a beloved casual dining spot in Philadelphia's Chinatown, known for its authentic hand-pulled noodles and dumplings. The venue offers a cozy atmosphere, making it a great choice for late-night cravings or casual gatherings with friends, though it may not be ideal for formal dates or anniversaries.

googleReviews: I love the roasted duck over rice here. The duck is very well-seasoned, and the price is so affordable. For $9 you get a plate of meat over rice with veggie and a bowl of soup. I also like the hong kong style pan fried noodle, very similar to mì xào giòn. The only thing I would do next time is ask for less sauce cuz I like my noodles crunchy. I don't recommend the cheung fun or steamed rice noodles here. It's just too much rice noodles and very little filling. Chow fun is kinda bland while lo mein is too salty. Fried rice is decent. If you go with ~3 people, you can do a meat combo, side of veggie and white rice for roughly same price as meat over rice but more food (esp veggie).

Good old-fashioned Cantonese cuisine in Chinatown Philadelphia.
Nothing fancy but great food, especially theory BBQ items and congee.
Great place for an authentic Chinese breakfast in the morning.
You may also place to-go orders on the machine by the front door.

Great dishes with plenty of selections. Sizzling pork intestine is so delightful while the duck and chicken are very savory. Their vegetable noodles just got the right amount of saltiness. Highly recommended!

I'm thrilled to share that Ting Wong surpassed my expectations with its remarkable Cantonese cuisine, earning the enthusiastic endorsement of my mother.

The exceptional service from the waitstaff elevated the dining experience, complementing the outstanding food quality. With its clean and inviting atmosphere, Ting Wong is perfectly suited for both dine-in and takeout.

For a truly delightful culinary experience in Philadelphia's Chinatown, I strongly recommend visiting Ting Wong – a standout choice that exceeds expectations.

Their roasted duck is a must. We tried rice, noodles and roll with duck. Every item was super delicious! We were so impressed with the food that we went back the next day.

First day, we took wonton noodles soup. The noodles tasted bland but other than that, everything was good. Broth was well seasoned. Next day, we took HK styled noodles with duck. On that, the noodles was rich in flavor. Also, the price was very reasonable compared to the other restaurants in the area.
customer_insights: Ting Wong offers a delightful selection of authentic Cantonese dishes, particularly known for its roasted duck and BBQ items. The casual atmosphere and affordable prices make it a great spot for a quick meal or breakfast in Chinatown, although it may not be ideal for special occasions or nightlife.

googleReviews: We are big fans of the NYC outposts of Han Dynasty so it was fun to visit the mother ship. Food was delicious as always, staff was young and fun, but dishes and vibe were different too. We loved the happy hour menu which goes to 6:30. It encouraged us to try fried chicken dumplings and spicy pork belly which were delicious. Seemed like a lot of locals in there having fun. Then we had the dan Dan noodles (spicy!!!), shredded duck and a plate of fresh peas greens, two favorites. All yummy!

Really large portion sizes for a very reasonable price and quick service. Overall the taste of the food was pretty good, but I think I'd order something different next time or at least come with a group to share in the sheer amount of food

Had the black bean style beef + mapo tofu + bok choy w/ mushrooms — all very yummy! forgot to take a pic because it was so good once we started eating. there’s big portions and we had a good amount for left overs.

our server, Nia was super informative, thoughtful, and went above & beyond to ensure we had best dining experience — she deserves a raise for such excellent service!

This place had the best Dan Dan noodles I ever had. Also had dumplings bathed in chili oil and a crispy rice chicjen dish. So delicious. The also had Down East Cider donut on tap, which is my favorite fall cider in the world. What a great spot!

First time here, we were in the area and Googled some options for food and this place popped up so we decided to walk over and give them a try. Walked in, no wait time.. greeted nicely..good amout of indoor seating...we were seated immediately... staff was was very friendly and knowledgeable.. we really appreciated our server, he was awesome.. we were offered complimentary tea.. we ordered the dry pepper shrimp (i was able to get my spice level adjusted which i really appreciated). Food was delicious, good atmosphere..i definitely would recommend!
customer_insights: Han Dynasty - Old City offers a vibrant atmosphere with a focus on delicious, spicy Chinese cuisine. The restaurant is popular among locals and provides generous portion sizes at reasonable prices, making it a great spot for groups and casual dining experiences.

googleReviews: Very nice setup and welcoming decor. Staff was very friendly and accommodating even though no reservations. Scenery was very authentic and menu was solid. Drinks where tasty and the food was outstanding. Came out fairly quick and was well done. Will be going back again.

My family and I just an exceptional dinner and I would easily come back the next time I’m in Philly. There were 6 of us, so we were able to get plenty of food to share and got to try a ton of different dishes. Some favorites included the shrimp bao buns and pork belly bao buns, the calamari salad, and the ribs, which fell right off the bone. Another one of my favorite bites were the edamame dumplings, which contained truffle!

Next time, I would probably skip the caesar salad and the crab fried rice since the salad was a bit overdressed and the flavors in the crab fried rice were subtle and I thought it could have used more acid.

For dessert, we got the winding road, which was this delectable chocolate dessert with banana and peanut components. It made for an excellent finish to the meal!

We had a nice dining experience here and would recommend it. I would like to return to try more things on the menu.

Everything we ordered was really good.
We got the Peking Duck, chargrilled aged beef, and dim sum sampler (added a third of each one for our party of 3).

My only complaint was the Chinese mustard sauce drizzled all over the Szechuan fries with the steak. It didn’t taste good and it made the fries soggy. If the menu had mentioned it, I would have asked for the mustard to be on the side.

The Peking Duck was really good! They deboned the entire duck which is unusual.

The dim sum sampler was tasty. The edamame dumpling was a pleasant surprise. The shrimp dumpling was ok (the filling was too chunky and it fell apart after one bite). The pork wonton and chicken Ginger dumplings were very good.

We got the strawberry dessert and the chocolate cake with banana buttercream and caramel peanuts. The strawberry one was described to us as a “deconstructed strawberry shortcake” but there wasn’t really any cake. The presentation was nice but we didn’t care for it. The chocolate/banana/peanut butter one was better.

Our service was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu.

Iconic Asian restaurant. Service ia nice, professional and tall ceilings which make it feel nice. Giant Buddha a nice touch and a favorite for the photo loving crowd. Which there tends to flashing lights from people attempting to make their best Instagram post. Menu has lots of options, not much sushi, go to Morimoto for that. Would dine here again and understand why its still a Philly favorite.

We came here for my birthday dinner and had a wonderful time! Our server Patchus was very kind and helpful. We especially loved the chargrilled dry aged beef and wasabi mashed potatoes. The enlightenment drink was also very tasty. Overall a relaxing environment and delicious food. We will definitely visit again!
customer_insights: Buddakan offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on Asian fusion cuisine, highlighted by dishes like Peking Duck and various dim sum options. The ambiance is upscale and trendy, making it suitable for special occasions and social gatherings alike.

googleReviews: The food here is the best! So fresh and flavorful! Their wonton and filling are so good! And the BBQ spareribs, my gosh, taste like they’re right off the grill! IYKYK! There is just one person’s job of basting and turning! Today I saw the owner shelling roasted peanuts! She says it’s the tastiest and  freshest ingredients for their food! Yep! I agree! No one yet compares to China House’s food! No matter time you go, it’s always packed and everyone is happy waiting  for their orders! 👍🏽👏🏽👏🏽👏🏽

Haven’t had Chinese take out for quite a while. Decided to have some wings and shrimp roll today and I’m glad I’ve ordered from here. The food is amazingly good. The wings are crunchy and juicy. The shrimp roll has enough shrimp in it. Will order again next time.

This is not how I remember China House. Shrimp lo mein was tasteless. Instead of chicken and broccoli I got shrimp and broccoli. The shrimp was tasteless as well. And they changed their dumplings. Their steamed dumplings used to be the best. This place went downhill and it's sad. They once were the best in south philly.
Pretty good American style Chinese food. Well made, not overly greasy. The food was nice and hot when I got it. I would definitely go back. Just keep in mind it’s cash only!

I’ve been coming here for about 10 years now. It’s like the best Chinese take out in south Philly. No matter what time of the day you go they’re always busy. We love their fried chicken wings, sesame chicken, shrimp and broccoli. We used to go a lot more often before covid then we’ve notice since covid the prices went up like crazy. We used to be able to get 4 wings and fried rice platter for like $6 but about 2 months or so ago we went and paid $12.50 for 5 wings with no fried rice which is a bit steep. Their lunch special used to be like $6 now it went up by about 20-25% post covid and I’ve also notice the shrimps are much smaller in sizes. Flavor wise it’s still as good but I feel like if you going to charge more at least give me the same size shrimp. Don’t charge more and give less that’s just not right.
customer_insights: China House No. 5 is a popular casual Chinese takeout spot in South Philadelphia known for its fresh and flavorful dishes. While many customers rave about the quality of the food, some have noted a decline in consistency and portion sizes post-COVID. The venue is always busy, indicating a strong local following.

neighborhood: University Science Center, 3711 Market St, Philadelphia
googleReviews: We went there yesterday and were warmly welcomed from the moment we arrived! The food was absolutely delicious, and the ambiance was wonderful — cozy, friendly, and full of good energy. We’ll definitely be coming back!

Lunch portion- laughable. No condiments were included. $12+ fees

Tasty (Dry hot chicken)- 11/10!
Added brown rice. (Meh.)

Asked for GF pption... Umm... I think that was my fault.

They increase the prices when you order online for delivery rather than pickup which is kind of lame since they don't even use their own driving staff. Paid $50 for 3 things and all 3 things were just ok - chicken fried rice, dan dan noodles, and chicken dumplings. The flavors you want out of these dishes were secondary to the flavor of salt and didn't love the texture of the chicken in the fried rice. It was ready quickly for dinnertime hours on a Friday night and I appreciated the option to not include utensils with the order. Overall it was not worth the $50, unsure if we would order from here again.

I drove over an hour to High Dynasty after leaving the hospital, just wanting to sit and eat comfortably. There were about ten people in a restaurant with over 100 open seats, yet when I asked for a four-top for myself and my partner, the manager refused.

He claimed we “needed three people” to sit at a four-top — even though the place was nearly empty. The two-top he tried to force us into was cramped and had nowhere for my bag. His tone was cold, dismissive, and condescending, even after I mentioned I’d just come from the hospital.

The way he selectively enforced a policy in an almost empty restaurant made the experience feel racially biased and completely unwelcoming.

And what’s sad is that he had no idea who he was speaking to. I was actually considering bringing my staff of 40 here for a team appreciation event — money, support, and repeat business. After today’s treatment, that will not be happening.

High Dynasty needs to seriously address their customer service and the discriminatory attitude shown toward guests. I will not be returning.

Hearing about this place from so many UPenn staff and students, I was excited to give them a try. I stopped by on several occasions- two weekdays and two weekends- to give myself multiple opportunities to review.

The food was generally tasty, though like the service, it was inconsistent. I received different portions of the same dishes for the same cost, and their service is a gamble of whether you will get a server who cares versus one who thinks you should be grateful for their presence. The best thing about the restaurant is the atmosphere. It's trendy and looks cool, looking its best at night for dinner.

For the price, I can see why students would like it. But it would be great if they can reel in a more consistent food portion and presentation and service standard.
customer_insights: Han Dynasty University City offers a trendy and cozy atmosphere with a focus on spicy Chinese cuisine. While the food is generally well-received, service can be inconsistent, and some customers have reported issues with portion sizes and customer service. It's a suitable spot for casual dining and pregame gatherings, especially popular among students.

googleReviews:
Had a great meal and an even better experience at Mana – Modern Chinese. The standout of the evening was the Shiitake Bao — pillowy buns filled with perfectly seasoned shiitake mushrooms. I could easily eat a whole plate of these!

Next up was the Jade Harmony Fried Rice, a vibrant vegetarian dish wok-tossed with fresh mixed vegetables. It was flavorful, beautifully presented, and definitely another highlight.

For the main course, we shared the Clay Pot Braised Salmon — slow-braised in a soy-infused broth with ginger, scallions, Chinese broccoli, basil, and bell peppers. This dish was a favorite among my dinner companions, with the rich, aromatic broth complementing the salmon perfectly.

The only slight miss for me was the Forbidden Ribs. While the ribs themselves were tender and well-prepared, the sweet-sour balsamic soy glaze wasn’t quite to my taste — so that may just be personal preference so I don’t see as negative.

Overall, Mana delivers an elevated and creative take on modern Chinese cuisine. The service was top-notch, the staff attentive, and the atmosphere comfortable. I highly recommend visiting — and I’ll definitely be back!

MANA MODERN is one of a kind, like no other. Its uniqueness will take you by surprise.  They serve delicious Chinese-style food with a modern twist, presented in a style reminiscent of a Michelin-starred restaurant.

Food: When typical Americans think about Chinese food, dishes like orange chicken, kung pao chicken, sichuan beef, shrimp fried rice, and beef noodles come to mind. Here at MANA’s, you can expect a diverse culinary experience featuring juicy duck served on curry, American-style ribs cooked in a sour and spicy sauce, Japanese katsu served with broccoli, unique flavored and tasty soup dumplings, sweets presented in realistic food shapes, and savory dishes that are to the soul.

Service: The team works seamlessly together—friendly, down-to-earth, yet professional and highly knowledgeable. It’s clear they take pride in making guests feel welcome and cared for.

Atmosphere: The vibe is bold, modern, and unmistakably infused with a Chinese essence that sets it apart from typical restaurants.

Value: For the quality of food and experience, the prices are excellent.

Parking: There's plenty of street parking out front, but it can get crowded at times. Also, be mindful of the time limit.

Overall: MANA MODERN offers a dining experience that is unique, flavorful, and unforgettable.
Highly recommended by @WineDinenVacay.

Mana Modern Chinese in Northern Liberties delivered start to finish. Chris and Katherine ran the front-of-house with warm, dialed-in service - fast, friendly, and with spot-on recommendations. The Forbidden Ribs stole the show: tender, lacquered, deeply savory. The duck noodles were a close second with rich flavor and great texture. Don’t skip the matcha tiramisu; light, balanced, and not overly sweet. Prices are fair, portions satisfy, and the menu keeps evolving, which gives real reason to come back. If you want fantastic food, an authentic-feeling vibe, and a team that makes service look effortless, Mana is the move. Definitely will be back to try everything on the menu!

We went for dinner on Sunday night around 7. It was busy but not packed. The restaurant has a modern look, not overly fancy but nicely done. It’s a byob so remember that is you want wine or cocktails. We had the Red Ember Wantons, they were wonderful, great flavor and just a little bit spicy but not overwhelming. We added the shrimp spring rolls, they were average but served hot and fresh. We also enjoyed the Mala Spicy Pork Dumpling, they were nice and juicy with great flavor. After those items we had the very flavorful Black Truffle Mushroom Beef. It was served in a nice bit of broth with white rice on the side and we really enjoyed it. We finished with the Everyday Fried Rice, I found it a little extra salty, my boyfriend thought it was just as it says, everyday.

Overall the meal was very good. The service was fine. Order entered table side and about average of this type of restaurant in the area. Definitely worth a try.

Every aspect of my experience at this now spot was absolutely 5-star. The service was attentive from start to finish, the atmosphere was so relaxing yet stylish and modern, and the presentation of each dish was truly beautiful. Most importantly, the food was outstanding. Every bite was full of flavor and clearly made with care.

I had a particularly wonderful experience with our server, Julia, who went above and beyond to make the evening special.

This will surely become a regular spot for me, as I’ll need to try everything on the menu!
customer_insights: Mana Modern Chinese offers a unique and elevated dining experience with a creative twist on traditional Chinese cuisine. The atmosphere is stylish and modern, making it suitable for various occasions, from casual dinners to special celebrations.

googleReviews:
Great Dim Sum！
Grand Palace Restaurant was delicious! All the dim sum dishes were fresh, hot, and full of flavor. Huge variety, fast service, and everything we tried
-dumplings, siu mai, buns, chicken feet, and more-tasted amazing. They also host weddings and special events, making it a perfect spot for great food and celebrations.
Highly recommended!

All around my favorite place to go when I am in or even passing by Philadelphia. The food is fresh and authentic. My favorite thing to get is the dim sum and salt and pepper squid/shrimp. The staff and attentive, friendly and and fast. This a great place for a date, solo eating, birthday party for any age. The provide live music some nights.

We are visiting Philly and stopped by for some dim sum around 1:30 in the afternoon and were seated right away, no wait at all. I love the traditional push carts; they give the place such a nostalgic vibe. Of course that means you'll have the push carts ladies always coming by to ask if you want more and more and more! You'll just have to let them know no is no when you've had enough. The food was solid overall. Our favorites were the shrimp rice rolls and the beef balls. We also ordered the beef offal, and I was pleasantly surprised that they gave multiple pieces of spleen, usually you only get one, so that was a nice bonus. The tripe was a little tough, but everything else hit the spot.

I absolutely love this place! I called this place home when I moved to the area. The staff are extremely friendly and caring. The food is undescribably good!! Authentic well seasoned food!! The tea verity is the best. Great music. Sometimes they have live music. Great decore and calm loving atmosphere. Best place to come!! Highly recommend

We attended a friend’s wedding at Grand Palace and were pleased with the service, which was friendly and attentive. However, the food was disappointing. The sashimi was not fresh, and the overall presentation of the dishes was lacking — it didn’t meet the standard we expected from other similar venues. Additionally, the candy and snack bar had mold on some of the items, including the peanuts. Thankfully, we noticed it in time and prevented our kids from eating any.

While the service was commendable, the food quality and cleanliness issues were concerning and not what we anticipated for such an important event. We hope they take these concerns seriously and improve moving forward.
customer_insights: Grand Palace Restaurant is a beloved spot for authentic dim sum in Philadelphia, offering a nostalgic dining experience with traditional push carts and a friendly atmosphere. While most reviews praise the food and service, there are some concerns regarding food quality during events, highlighting the need for consistency.

googleReviews: The restaurant was clean and very easy to get seating. The service fast the food hot, fresh and good. They give enough portions to take home and eat another day. The owner and servers were very nice and welcoming. A great place to eat at in Chinatown Philadelphia.

Fine dining professional of 15 years.
Place was empty but shouldn't be. The vibes and food were Chinese/American but well executed. Our server "Young" was a bit overbearing but ended up adding to the charm of the entire experience.
We were looking for more adventurous options but we were very satisfied with what we received.
Ordered,
LULU Rice (server recommendation). Imagine country style pork lardon and bok choy in a rich, dark brown gravy over rice. It was filling and so satisfying, especially with some added spicy sauce.
Fried Squid with XO, best dish of the dinner, fishy and fresh. Excellent fry on the squid, crunchy despite being saturated in the XO sauce.
Grandfathers Chicken ended up being a spicy/acidic version of General Tsos chicken, personally it was far too sweet but we still finished the entire plate and beats the hell out of your neighborhood Gen Tsos.
We will be back.

The Chinese food tasted so fresh
.service was fast and our server was friendly and funny.

I dined in here for dinner. I ordered Hot & Spicy Hunan Wings, Red Cooked Beef w Chinese Broccoli, and a Mango Smoothie. The wings were crispy and maintained their crisp despite the lovely wet, sticky sauce that they were served in. All of the vegetables that they came with tasted very fresh. There was something about the flavor of the wings that I couldn’t quite place and it may have been reused cooking oil, but this mostly seemed to give the flavor of the wings a more positive complex character, rather than detracting too much from the experience.

The beef had an amazing rich, complex flavor and was a very lovely tender texture, but it was a bit too salty. I still very much enjoyed it as it was very tasty otherwise. It was definitely worth the price and was probably one of the best beef dishes I’ve had.

The smoothie was alright, and a refreshing relief from the spiciness of the wings, but it was not very homogenous in texture.

The server was friendly and attentive, which was much appreciated. However, he asked if I wanted tea when I first arrived, which is usually not an extra charge at Chinese restaurants, so I was disappointed to find a charge for this on my bill without having been informed in advance about it. The same happened with the plain white rice - it is often included, so I didn’t know it would be an extra charge until I received the bill. This would be less of an issue if customers are informed in advance that these are separate charges.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is overall warm and comfortable. The dining room appeared very clean. They do have a TV, on which they had the news playing and in my opinion, no matter what is playing, a TV detracts from the atmosphere.
Most notably, the service was really great; there was only one server but he was attentive and friendly. There was a good selection of both authentic and Americanized options.
customer_insights: Ho Sai Gai Restaurant offers a blend of authentic Chinese and Americanized dishes in a casual and welcoming atmosphere. Customers appreciate the friendly service, generous portions, and the freshness of the food, making it a great spot for casual dining or pregame meals.

googleReviews: A really delightful first experience here! Loved the atmosphere, a chill vibe, great for a relaxing Friday night meal. My husband and I devoured the dumplings in chili oil. Just the right amount of spice. That was our absolute favorite! We also had the scallion pancakes, which were deliciously crispy. I got the ginger shredded duck and loved it. My husband got the special - a spicy braised duck with vegetables. It was huge! He was very happy. 😋 We will definitely return.

this place had the best food i’ve ever hand in my entire life by far. me and my mom were absolutely astonished by how great the food was and the customer service was great too. if you want the wind knocked out of you because of how good the food is definitely come here. it’s a family style restaurant so beware and not order a whole bunch of food like me and my mom😭😭😭
The spicy beef noodles and the wontons are always out of this world. The big shrimp pot could have used a bit more flavor but was still very good. DanDan is always worth the visit

I’m unable to attach my video to this review, but the food and ambiance are great! I ordered a chicken pot, and it came with a bowl over its own flame. There was the perfect amount of spice without compromising the flavor.

Will be coming back, I really liked this place! It was worth coming to on an off/day time (good luck getting in on a Saturday night with no reservations). The cumin lab noodles were so good and so spicy with great flavor. Next I want to try the spicy beef noodles it was that good. Wontons in chili oil were great, definitely save the oil and put it on your rice. The eggplant and garlic sauce was good and a good balance to the spice of the lamb. Cute spot for a date night, highly recommend!

Edit:
Have come back multiple times one of my favorite spots for a nice night. Continues to be fantastic quality.
customer_insights: DanDan Rittenhouse offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on flavorful Asian cuisine, particularly known for its dumplings and spicy noodles. The atmosphere is casual yet trendy, making it suitable for various occasions, from casual outings to date nights.

address: 2842 St Vincent St, Philadelphia, PA 19149, USA
googleReviews:
Had dim sum at China Gourmet after a basketball game and it was the perfect call. One of the few places that still has the push carts for fresh dim sum, which makes the experience even better. As soon as we sat down, the cart was right next to us with food ready to go. Can’t ask for faster service than that!

We got our usual favorites, shrimp dumplings, shui mai, sticky rice, rice rolls with pork ribs, and roast pork buns. Everything was fresh, hot, and delicious. We were in and out in about 30 minutes, which was perfect since we were short on time. Great food, quick service, and definitely a place I’d come back to again.

Great authentic dim sum! Good portions. They don’t skimp on the good ingredients. The restaurant itself is quite large and could use a refresh, but food and service were great on a Friday morning. Parking was easy, but don’t leave anything in your car. Area seems sketchy. Pork buns were delicious. Pork & shrimp wrapped in dried bean curd had plenty of vegetables as well. Pan fried Chive dumplings. Chicken feet. Tripe. Shrimp dumplings. Delicious!

Really nice dim sum place in the NE Philly region! Huge banquet hall, with nice ambiance. This place was fullll on a Saturday morning with patrons of all ages. Quick service, large variety of options (their dessert menu is truly impressive!!), good food, and kind staff. Everything is very affordable too. I came with a group of 5 total and we got close to 25 dishes to share, and split among us the price came to ~$25 each! A remarkable deal given the amount of food we tried.

Shrimp dumplings, fried taro, and spare ribs were good (And I’m very particular about these 3 dim sum dishes). Pineapple buns and pandas sesame balls were truly extraordinary. I do have to add that their vegetarian and gluten free options were quite sparse. Other than that, it’s a very delicious and lovely place to spend a weekend morning with a group of loved ones!

This place opens till dinner, but dim sum closes at around 3pm on weekend. There wasn't a lot of options, maybe because we arrived at 2pm. Everything was overcooked because the skin was too soft and broke apart. The fillings are good though. The sauce of the rice roll is good; recommend you ask for a lot so you can dip other stuff. Congee has pork and century egg. Pretty spacious place with shared public parking lot.

I love this place 🥺 everything on the dimsum menu is delicious, especially the pork buns and liushabao. The service is super fast, most times I’ve been there will be two carts stopping by within 2 minutes of us sitting down. It’s loud and pretty crowded but that doesn’t impact the service. 10/10
customer_insights: China Gourmet is a lively dim sum restaurant in Northeast Philadelphia, known for its authentic dishes and quick service. The venue is spacious and family-friendly, making it ideal for group dining, especially during brunch hours. While the ambiance could use a refresh, the food quality and variety keep patrons returning.

googleReviews: Loved the chefs tasting menu option. $56 per person and you choose 7 dishes and the chef  sends them out family style as they are made. The cocktails were very good. The waitress Izzy had good vibes and she was knowledgeable since she worked there for 5 years. I also liked the dark fluorescent wall paper on one wall which brought up the atmosphere to another level. I would definitely recommend this place. Everything we had was amazing.

Came during happy hour and ordered a ton of the menu to try. There were lots of delicious options, my favorite were the pork bao buns. It was busy inside so we were seated outside on the street side. The side walk is a bit slanted so you feel like you're tilted if you're seated facing the building.

They also brought little ice creams with sparklers on top because it was my birthday.

Me and my dined in for anniversary. The food was amazing! We did the tasting menu and from first dish to last I was impressed! Portions sizes were great(even too some food home), taste was amazing, and service was quick! Meals come out as there don’t which he didn’t have an issue with and display was beautiful. Sara was server and did an amazing job guiding us through the menu and staying attentive with drink refills and any issues with the food. All around great experience, minus the fact of us needing to put a card down before we received any food.  Not sure what the reason for this is, but not something I enjoy needing to do; this is the reason for the 4 star review.

Incredible meal and cocktails! Highly recommend the tasting menu to get the full experience — and it’s a great value. We asked our knowledgeable server to curate our selections, and he absolutely nailed it. Every course was perfectly balanced and beautifully presented. Would definitely come back!

Went to Sampan on a Saturday night with no reservation and was told it’d be a little over a two-hour wait. They texted us after about an hour, and when we came back, we were seated at the bar overlooking the kitchen. At first I was annoyed it wasn’t a regular table, but it ended up being a great spot to eat and watch them prepare the food.

I had the edamame dumplings, roasted broccoli, salmon entrée, and Korean beef BBQ — all absolutely delicious. One of the most consistently great spots in Philly.
happy_hour_details: 4-6pm weekdays, various small plates and drinks
customer_insights: Sampan offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on Asian fusion cuisine, particularly through its popular tasting menu. Guests appreciate the attentive service and lively atmosphere, making it suitable for various occasions, from casual outings to special celebrations.

googleReviews:
Had an excellent meal here after rock climbing on a Friday night, I was able to walk right in and be served immediately.
