Lee How Fook has been around in Chinatown for a long time it seems, and  while the interior and atmosphere won't blow you away the food was solid and classic and I'm excited to return for more.

I had heard a lot about the salt-baked squid and it was actually the main reason I tried this spot in the first place, and it definitely lived up to the hype! Perfectly lightly battered, salty, and every bite made you want to take another. It had a touch of freshness underneath with some jalepeno and green onion which was appreciated since it's a fairly one-note dish. While I 100% recommend this dish, I would note a couple things: first, I would recommend splitting it as more of an appetizer since it is fairly simple and salty, and second, I think if you pay like $1 more you can get the salt-baked squid AND scallop, which would probably be great! I also ordered the crab rangoons which were very good and quite surprisingly large. They were rich and creamy and a solid choice.

There isn't anything negative I can really say, but at the same time nothing has quite blown me away YET so I'm leaving a 4-star review. However I do plan to return for some other Chinese-American classics so maybe I'll amend my rating after a second visit. Overall, I think Lee How Fook is an overlooked spot that you should give a chance!

Went here for dinner with some friends.
The food was delicious.  It's small and cozy inside but worth the coziness for the delicious meals.
The good was very reasonable and easy to get to. Parking wasn't easy for Philadelphia, but that's nothing new.
The service was amazing as well.
Will definitely be back.

Excellent food!! Nothing to rave about inside but the service was amazing and the food was incredible. Mongolian beef melts in your mouth, scallion pancakes are delicious and the shrimp rolls are 100% full of shrimp and lightly panko fried. Nothing like I’ve had before. Highly recommended!! This was 2 weeks ago and I’m going back tonight 🥰

This place will definitely be a pre-AMC movies spot from now on. Enjoyed its small unassuming nature, the hello kitty and Disney decor. The service (one woman team) was excellent, as was the sweet and sour chicken.

Excellent dumplings, top 5 easy. I didn’t get any sauce but they honestly didn’t need it. Great texture, good filling, would definitely order again.

Hot and sour soup is also excellent, comes in a monster portion and is packed with veggies, tofu and meat.

Pork buns were also a hit. Not the best I’ve had, but they were solid enough. I would order again.

Orange chicken blew my mind. Tender and moist chicken inside a fantastic tempura breading smothered in thick sweet sauce. This is definitely a winner here.

Fried rice was also good, the chicken is quality cubed dark meat and I wouldn’t hesitate to order this again.

Singapore noodles were nothing special, I would try something else next time. Not enough curry or spice or something. That being said, it did have plenty of meat and veggies mixed in so it’s not like I left hungry.

Pad thai was not pad thai… tofu had good texture, noodles were fine, just no flavor. Stay away from this.

Pretty small dining area, 8-10 tables but there was no one around on a Wednesday night, though lots of takeout folks passed through.
customer_insights: Lee How Fook is a cozy, unassuming spot in Philadelphia's Chinatown known for its solid and classic Chinese-American dishes. While the ambiance is simple, the food, including standout items like salt-baked squid and Mongolian beef, has garnered positive reviews for its flavor and quality, making it a great choice for casual dining with friends or a pre-movie meal.

googleReviews: Bai Wei is my favorite spot for spicy food! The flavors are bold, authentic, and packed with heat — perfect for anyone who loves a good kick. The dishes are always fresh, well-seasoned, and full of variety. The staff are friendly and welcoming, and the restaurant has a cozy, inviting atmosphere. Every visit is a delicious adventure, and I always leave satisfied. Highly recommend for spice lovers!

This restaurant was recommended to me by a friend. It was new to me that they charge 50cents for rice, it doesn’t come with the entrees. Their eggplant dish and Japanese tofu dish was super good!! I highly recommend to try those and portions were good sized. I got three entrees to share and one rice to share w three people and I would say I left pretty full.
The soup dumplings and vegetable dumplings are amazing! It was my birthday, and they gave me a complementary slice of cake! I’ve been coming here for years and always enjoy my experience.

Really love the food here. Probably one of the best food I had in Philiy in this trip. I ordered spicy beef noodles and sour doujiao with Chicken gizzards. The taste is very authentic and really reminded me of home.
Will definitely come back again if I am ever in town.

A Gem in Philly's Chinatown 价格便宜，饭菜好吃
Tucked right at the corner of Chinatown, Bai Wei delivers an excellent dining experience. The space is spacious and clean, the service is friendly, and the prices are reasonable-but the real star is the food: authentic, flavorful, and downright delicious.
customer_insights: Bai Wei is a beloved spot in Philadelphia's Chinatown, known for its bold and spicy flavors, particularly among fans of authentic Chinese cuisine. The cozy atmosphere and friendly staff enhance the dining experience, making it a great choice for casual outings with friends or a laid-back date night.

address: 4 W Palmer St, Philadelphia, PA 19125, USA
googleReviews: Kalaya’s strength are their strong flavors, with many creative dishes featuring something about them that just makes them so good. Accompanied with a beautiful interior makes for a very fun dining experience. The Taste of Kalaya menu is the perfect value to try some cool stuff. The Mussels Golar were fantastic, and one of my favorite mussels preparations to date. The Gaeng Pae was very good and well spiced, and the Branzino was a great move! Sitting in a delicious and spicy broth and in great portion. Finally… the Coconut Pineapple Shaved Ice, unexpectedly one of my favorite desserts I’ve ever had. It’s huge, tons of great bites with the strawberry and the bottom molds into harder ice cream with Tapioca at the bottom. There’s so much to like about this dessert and I would 100% get it again.

Kalaya is an absolute gem. From the moment we walked in, the service was incredible, warm, attentive, and full of genuine smiles. We ordered the whole bronzino fish and the shaw muang dumplings, and honestly, they were the prettiest and most flavorful dishes I’ve ever had. The goat and lamb curry was next level rich, spicy, and bursting with flavor in every bite.

We chose to experience “The Taste of Kalaya,” which included appetizers, entrées, a curry, two side dishes, and a sweet treat for $75 per person. Every course felt like a journey through authentic, vibrant Thai flavors.

Our waiter, Michael, made the entire evening even better. He was fantastic—knowledgeable, patient, and radiated such a good aura. You could tell he truly loves what he does. The entire staff was just as kind and welcoming, creating an atmosphere that felt both elegant and comfortable.

This restaurant will always hold a special place in my heart because my boyfriend asked me to be his girlfriend here, and the staff helped make that moment unforgettable. I’ll never forget their warmth, their smiles, and the magic of that night.

Kalaya isn’t just a restaurant, it’s a full culinary experience. 10/10 recommend.

Kalaya is really special! As someone that used to live in Thailand and has a Thai spouse, I can say that this is the most authentic Thai food I've had in America. Many of the dishes were very authentic, and yet even better than the best version I have tried in Thailand!

The Tom Yum with giant river prawns is a must, the broth is so rich and concentrated. The steamed fish with lime sauce is a hit as well. Everything is seasoned perfectly and not overpowering. Considering Southern Thailand has the spiciest food in the country, I'm happy to say the team at Kalaya manages the flavors well to deliver an authentic experience without killing you with heat.

Every single dish we had was amazing. My spouse from Thailand walked out saying the food is 100/10.

I had a fairly good experience. I absolutely love the interior. The palm tree and the paper light shades each sets a mood but they’re too dissimilar. This place was so hyped so I might have had too high of an expectation. Their food is good but it is still a Michelin guide type. Plating could be better on some dishes like that roasted pork belly dish? - this one might be better served together in a half/half plate together and veggies on the side yktv just a suggestion. and the half chicken is giving thailand night market plastic lookin plate. also a restaurant with this much reputation and hype using chipped plates shows they do have some aspects to work on. in terms of food taste is overall okay. they were all good but as an Asian there wasn’t anything special about the taste. the roasted pork belly dish tasted just like miss saigon. Nothing special about chicken and duck sauce. Hard to eat bc chicken kinda skinny 😭 chive rice cake tastes like korean pajeon. could be served a little more chilled for better rice cake texture. Sticky rice was great. Tiramisu is overdone. too much flavor for me lowkey didn’t blend so well. Overall it’s definitely worth the experience. Willing to return for different menus.

I had an amazing experience at Kalaya! The $75 tasting menu (3 apps, 1 entree, 1 curry, and 1 dessert) offers fantastic value for the incredible food. The flavors are authentic and genuinely Thai-spicy, with generous portions. The ambience is a perfect blend of genuine and elegant. Service was a bit slow, likely due to how busy the place was, but it didn’t detract from the experience at all. Already made my reservation again for next month. Can't wait.
customer_insights: Kalaya is celebrated for its authentic and vibrant Thai flavors, offering a unique dining experience with a beautiful interior and attentive service. The $75 tasting menu is highly recommended for those looking to explore a variety of dishes, making it suitable for special occasions and date nights.

googleReviews: Incredible service here, with a good value happy hour menu. Items listed in happy appear to be full portions just like the regular menu, making it a bang for your buck. I ordered the chicken satay. They were smoky and juicy, I liked the peanut sauce was on the side. I had a chefs special curry noodle dish. It was fab, just ask for their spice condiments, so you can adjust the heat to your liking. Def recommend.

Their menu doesn't have a lot of dishes. The first dish is a chicken with veggie in a special curry sauce. It tastes pretty good but takes quite a long time to be served. The second dish is a noodle soup that suppose to has a Tom Yum base but we didn't taste any tom yum flavor. It is neither spicy nor sour; all we taste is the coconut milk so kinda disappointed. It comes with like a pad thai noodle, pork, fried shallot, and peanut. The appetizer is good; it's very crispy with meat/shrimp filling, dip in a sweet and spicy sauce.

Incredibly friendly and accomodating staff. I was very very impressed with my experience here.

The food is good. Their vegetarian pad thai is amazing.

Highly recommended spot!

Literally one of, if not, the best Thai restaurants in Philly. The decorations were so beautiful and the service was nice. All of the foods we got were surprisingly delicious, and we just kept devouring them. My favorite was the Khao soi, a noodle curry dish!!’
Don’t leave Philadelphia without having a meal at this restaurant. Food was totally orgasmic. The ambience and customer service is to die for. Mango sticky rice my favorite dessert.
customer_insights: Chatayee Thai is praised for its friendly service and vibrant atmosphere, making it a great spot for casual dining. Customers particularly enjoy the happy hour menu and the flavorful dishes, although some have noted inconsistencies in certain menu items.

googleReviews:
STAY AWAY!!! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!! My family and I were a party of four and all of us ended our dining experience being very agitated. Why? We could not figure out what we going to do for our next dining experience after having absolutely the best Thai food ever! Where would we go that could match this place? If we continue to come back we will go broke.

I have never eaten with a group where everyone loved every single item that was ordered, from the appetizers, to the main course and finally dessert. There was not one item that was disliked. The lamb, the duck, the salmon and the chicken were so flavorful that you could taste it when you put it in your mouth before you actually took a bite! The sticky rice was fantastic! The flavor of the food was enhanced by the various sauces that came with each dish.

To top it off, all of the drinks (non-acoholic) were delicious and offered a very smart after taste. The desserts were just too good! I would like to write a much longer review but just do not have the words to describe how wonderfully amazing all of the food was. If you decide to come here and dine, I guarantee you that you will be hooked and have a serious urge to return to the restaurant at least once every month. So beware, you have been warned.

Philly’s best kept secret! Our favorite Thai place in the city! The food is delicious and they always have seasonal specials, like the soft shell crab, that are amazing. They have a lot of unique dishes making it always so hard to choose! The massaman short rib is one of our go-to. The staff are kind and thoughtful and take the time to get to know their locals. Mimi is the best!

Have visited 2x and both times were great experiences. Very friendly and appropriately attentive service. Menu has something for everyone. Short Rib was fantastic. Our table also had seared tuna. Can't wait to return and enjoy more dishes. Loved the soundtrack, too.

I came here with my husband driving through Philly. The thai food was delicious! I ordered the massaman curry and thai tea. It was served extremely hot and I did burn my tongue. Service was a little slow but they were busy so it was understandable. Overall, the food was good. I recommend this place!

Today was my first time here and I decided to take some pictures and leave a review. I got the shrimp and crab spring rolls and I enjoyed them. I also order the mussels with white wine, the mussels wasn’t done. They was very slimy. I ate one and left the bowl.
customer_insights: JJ Thai Cuisine is a beloved local spot known for its delicious and authentic Thai dishes, with a menu that features unique seasonal specials. While the service can be slow during busy times, the friendly staff and flavorful food make it a great choice for casual outings or pre-dinner gatherings.

googleReviews:
Atmosphere: Dara is a new Thai spot in Philadelphia that I’d been excited to try. The restaurant is on the smaller side, but it feels warm and inviting, with a clean, modern look.

Food: I ordered Gai Yang Somtum. This was the grilled chicken with sticky rice and somtum salad, which included green papaya, string beans, tomato, dried shrimp, and peanuts, all tossed in a bright lime-chili dressing. The flavors were fresh and nicely balanced. I was surprised by the unique presentation. I also tried the vegetable spring rolls, which were crisp, light, and served with a sweet dipping sauce. Overall, the food tasted fresh and felt healthy!

Service: Service was quick and friendly! I recommend trying this restaurant.

Went to this restaurant for the first time a couple weeks back because I was craving Thai food and Chatayee Thai was closed.

Dara had the atmosphere you would describe as cozy. Light music, soft lighting, ambient chatters of life throughout the restaurant.

Their food was immaculate and the staff was very patient with explaining each dish and how to eat it to me. The drink I ordered tasted like an enhanced pina colada.

Overall, would recommend and would definitely come back.

ordered the Thai iced coffee, vegan basil fried rice, and vegan Pad Kee Mow all three were absolutely top-notch! Each dish was bursting with flavor and perfectly seasoned.

The only downside was that we felt a bit rushed toward the end of our meal. Our plates were cleared immediately after we finished, and the check was placed on the table without asking. We were there on a Saturday afternoon around 12:30 PM it did get busier, but there were still several tables open, so the quick wrap-up felt unnecessary.

That said, the food itself was fantastic, and I’d still recommend this place for anyone craving flavorful Thai dishes.

The place had a space themed vibe. We ordered basil fried rice, roasted mixed vegetable Massaman curry, spring rolls, and their non alcoholic cocktails. Overall, it was a pleasant experience and the food was decent. The only drawback was the flashing ice cube they placed in the drink it got stuck in the glass and made it uncomfortable to drink

Dined here in June 2025, very cute interior design.  Service was exceptional, food came out fast.

All the dishes were delicious 😋 and good sized portions. Ordered, Thai tea, and lemon Thai tea. Their Tom yum soup is one of the best I’ve had so far in Philly! Obviously had to taste calamari, drunken noodles, pad Thai and mango sticky rice.
customer_insights: Dara offers a cozy and inviting atmosphere with a modern design, making it a great spot for casual dining. The food is praised for its freshness and flavor, although some guests noted a rushed service at times. Overall, it's a solid choice for anyone craving Thai cuisine in Philadelphia.

googleReviews:
I love a good Thai place. I give this place an 8 out 10. The food was perfect, the spice level we selected “medium” was the perfect spice level for my husband and I.
Parking can be a bit difficult(street parking) it is Philly, there is a mini parking lot across the street that can be used if not already filled.

This spot is an absolute gem. The food was INCREDIBLE and the atmosphere was extremely cozy. My partner and I got red curry and khao soi and everything was flavorful, hot, and delicious. We really appreciated the lighting and beautiful textile art all over the restaurant. Extensive menu with tons of vegetarian and vegan options. The servers were extremely kind and quick. New favorite spot in the neighborhood and I only wish we had gone sooner.

This place deserves to be the best Thai place in Philly in my life so far. They have the most authentic Thai&Lao menu and vibe. The service was perfect, lemon water, and strong spices. I truly can’t find any flaw, except for the slightly fancy price. But I didn’t regret to pay at all. More than worth trying if you like southeast Asian food.

We saw a reddit recommendation for this place and so glad we went! We went after the lunch rush and didn’t have to wait for a table. The drunken noodles were yummy. It had the “wok” flavor we love and the addition of spice was a nice touch. We also got the Penang curry which was also very good. We’d definitely add this spot to the regular rotation if we lived in Philly.

My Thai wife and I go to Ratchada regularly and it’s always a great experience. Service is always friendly and attentive and the food is always great and authentic. For our last visit, I ordered cashew chicken and my wife had the Ka na moo krob and as usual it was fantastic!
customer_insights: Ratchada Thai & Laos Cuisine is celebrated for its authentic and flavorful dishes, with a cozy atmosphere that makes it a favorite among locals. The restaurant offers a diverse menu with plenty of vegetarian and vegan options, making it suitable for various dining occasions, from casual dinners to special celebrations.

address: 800 W Moyamensing Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19148, USA
googleReviews: This is my go to Thai spot in South Philly. Their hours are great and the food is even better. I normally get the drunken noodles but tonight me and my little bro decided to get the Thai Street Noodles, Pork Dumplings,  Thai Glazed Chicken Wings and to wash it down a Thai Iced Tea is a must!!!! Everything was superb!!! I like spicy and got mild spicy. It was perfect for me. My little brother on the other hand couldn’t handle it as much. He sure did keep eating it though because it’s that good!!!!

I recently ordered takeout from Every Thai for my son, who is a big Pad Thai fan and very particular about how it’s prepared. They did not disappoint. He ordered the beef Pad Thai, and the flavor was excellent with a generous amount of beef. The spice level was spot on. We asked for medium, and it had a good kick without being overwhelming. I also appreciated the thoughtful touches like the lime wedge and cracked Thai chili pepper on the side.

Diving into Golden Triangle unveils not just a meal, but a passport to a culinary expedition specializing in the Southeast Asian flavors of Thailand, Malaysia, and Myanmar. Tucked away in the heart of Philly, this humble gem offers an intimate escape to distant lands with its quiet, casual ambiance and a cozy dining room that boasts no more than eight tables.

Our adventure began with the Malaysian classic, Roti Canai -- a delightfuly crispy, flaky, chewy marvel that serves as a prelude to the symphony of flavors awaiting us. Paired with a rich curry chicken potato dip, this dish was a standing ovation in the making.

Then came the Sambal Shrimp, a bold ensemble of shrimp reveling in a spicy brown sauce, creating a festival of taste that had every fork in the room longing for an encore.

The Beef Rendang, while a masterpiece of flavor and tenderness with its slow-cooked, aromatic curry, left us longing for a second act, as the disappointing portion size was more of a soliloquy than a full-fledged aria.

Despite the small dining room, Golden Triangle played the perfect host to our group of six (including a baby car seat), accommodating us at their sole large table--a testament to their ability to harmonize space and service.

While the Mee Goreng and Penang Char Kway Teow flavors were well balance and added depth to our culinary journey, both dishes lacked a bit of the smoky "wok hay" that I was yearning for. The Burmese Kimchi introduced a zestful twist to the meal as it was our first time trying any Burmese food, but it wasn't particularly memorable. In the end, the Roti Canai and Sambal Shrimp emerged as our favorites of the night.

Overall, Golden Triangle is more than a dining destination; it's a quiet nook where flavors dance and diners are invited to a show that tantalizes the taste buds and warms the heart. With its intimate atmosphere and welcoming vibe, it stands out as a beacon for those seeking an immersive culinary experience in Center City. Here's to more explorations at this quaint culinary corner, where the world feels both vast and intimately close, all within the confines of its quiet, casual dining room.

This time I had the chaat (it was lacking a bit of flavor), the paneer bhurjee (very good, spicy), and the salt lassi (incredibly, very cooling, tasted great). I would definitely come back, even more so if the menu prices dropped a bit. Overall, I think if the menu adds back those favorites, it will be my #1 indian spot in Philly!

I used to go to Amma’s Kitchen when it was on Chestnut Street, and the food was amazing back then. It had real South Indian flavor and a good amount of heat. They’ve moved to a new spot now, and while the place looks great and the staff was friendly, the food was a letdown.

I ordered the biryani and chicken curry, and both tasted like they’d been Americanized. The biryani in particular was disappointing. It came out more like mushy rice with chicken — almost like a chicken khichdi — instead of the layered, flavorful biryani they used to make.

From the moment we walked in, the experience was flawless. Went here on. Holiday July 4th.The ambiance was warm and inviting.The staff greeted us with genuine smiles and attentive service that made us feel like honored guests.
We ordered non veg thali every dish in it was bursting with flavor and freshness. You can taste the love and tradition in every bite.I ordered pina colada which tasted much like diluted pineapple juice and was not matching the menu description.
Our server was courteous, knowledgeable, and quick to offer and they checked in just enough to make us feel cared for.Highly recommended for anyone seeking authentic flavors with exceptional service!
Update: for the next 2 days we ordered food from here for lunch or dinner and must say every new dish we tried was excellent. Highly recommend this place especially if you have kids and want something as idly this is the place.
customer_insights: Amma's South Indian Cuisine offers a beautifully designed space with an intimate atmosphere, making it a great choice for special occasions. While the food is generally well-received, some diners have noted inconsistencies in flavor and authenticity compared to previous locations. Overall, it is a solid option for those seeking halal South Indian cuisine in Philadelphia.

The tandoori chicken was juicy tender and delicious! I also had samosas that were light and crispy on the outside and packed with potatoes and just the right amount of peas.

We recently moved to the area and have been trying different Indian restaurants to find our new usual spot. I am very excited to have found it here! We ordered padri chaat, chana masala, chicken tikka masala, butter naan, bullet naan, and kheer for dessert. Every single dish was wonderful! The tikka masala is the best I have ever had! Everything was flavorful and balanced. We dined in and really enjoyed the vibe of the place, especially how kind the gentleman working was. Raindrops is definitely going to be our go to Indian restaurant!
customer_insights: Raindrops Indian Restaurant is a cozy spot in Wynnefield Heights known for its authentic and flavorful Indian cuisine. With a small dining area primarily set up for takeout, it offers a friendly atmosphere and a variety of vegetarian and meat dishes that cater to different spice levels.

googleReviews:
Incredible Indian food here and I would easily come back the next time I’m in Philly. I tried a whole bunch of items from the dosa to the fish tikka masala to the malai kofta. All excellent! I don’t even eat cooked salmon, but it was great in the tikka masala. Definitely try the mango lassi too. So refreshing and tasty! This is a spot you don’t want to miss!

Also, they were great about bringing out more waters and as an FYI, they take a student discount.

Never had bad Indian food but this was not it. I got the butter chicken, dark meat, with garlic naan bread. My chicken was so dry and tasteless…Do you know how hard it is to dry out a chicken thigh?? Just disappointing. The garlic naan was excellent tho, one star for that.

Dum chicken biriyani barely had any chicken … the pieces were all bones per my buddy.

I ordered achari chicken and it was alright.

However the location, vibe, decor, and service were great!

Absolutely incredible and authentic Indian food! The Gobi Manchurian was hands down the best I’ve ever had—perfectly crispy, flavorful, and just the right amount of spice. The Butter Chicken was rich and creamy, the Malai Kofta was melt-in-your-mouth delicious, and the Orange Kulfi was such a unique and refreshing treat to end the meal. Amazing flavors, great portions, and fantastic service. Will definitely be coming back!
The Indo-Chinese noodles were delicious! The quantity was great, and the spice level was perfect, just like the noodles you'd find in India.
customer_insights: Virasat Haveli offers a vibrant dining experience with a focus on authentic Indian cuisine, praised for its flavorful dishes like Gobi Manchurian and Butter Chicken. While some reviews mention inconsistencies in dish quality, the overall atmosphere and service are well-received, making it a suitable spot for casual gatherings and pregame outings.

address: 4612 Woodland Ave 1st Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19143, USA
googleReviews:
This is the best Indian food I’ve ever had. When you ask for it spicy, they actually deliver — the medium has a kick, and the spicy takes it all the way. I’ve had naan that’s burnt on the bottom before, but not here — it was cooked to perfection.

The Shrimp Chili appetizer is excellent. I ordered the chicken masala (yummm!), and we also tried the Aloo Gobi, which was amazing. I can’t wait to go back!

Visited here for the first time in August 2025 and had a solid first experience. Great Indian food all around. Atmosphere left a bit to be desired with the distracting TV playing music videos, and the servers were more attentive to the delivery orders than those of us in the restaurant. But otherwise, no complaints on the food!

This is my second time ordering. The first time I ordered, they didn't appropriately package the rice to make sure it was the correct portion. The second time, the Korma had so many pieces of ginger that was not appropriately chopped made it very difficult to enjoy. The Carrot Cheese Cake is $6 and they gave me a slither of a slice not appropriate at all for the price. In this economy it is important for people to ensure they are getting their money's worth. Two times too many on messed up orders, so I won't be ordering again. It is ashame because the food is good, they don't have attention to detail which is very important for delivery.

EXceptional!!! Food was absolutely authentic and delicious! The server was so accommodating and attentive. Prices reasonable. Sauces and seasonings were so tasty, and layered with flavors. Best Indian food Ive ever had. HOMEMADE naan bread was epic! Appreciated all the vegan and vegetarian options! I had the lentil vegetarian and the cauliflower/potato ginger garlic dishes, both were so good!! Its small inside, so people were coming in for takeout, but the host asked people to turn their phones music down, which was kind to those dining in. 2 hr free street parking, safe area.

I would give 6 stars if I could. I’ve been a regular customer for over a year now, and they never disappoint. The lamb mains/currys are delicious (particularly recommend their butter and saag options), and so is the biryani. They also have halal options, which is great. The service is impeccable and pretty fast, and, finally they have a loyalty program for people ordering through their website. Highly recommend!
customer_insights: Indian Char House is praised for its authentic and flavorful Indian cuisine, with a particular emphasis on spicy dishes and homemade naan. While the food receives high marks, the dining experience can be affected by service issues and the atmosphere, which some find distracting due to music videos playing on TV.

googleReviews:
Curry Leaf Nepali and Indian Cuisine
in Philadelphia offers an exceptional dining experience, combining warm hospitality with beautifully prepared dishes. We especially loved the garlic naan, which arrived hot, fragrant, and perfectly blistered, easily among the best we’ve had. The vegetable samosas were crisp and flavorful, with a well-spiced filling that tasted fresh rather than heavy. The standout was the chicken tandoori, served tender, deeply marinated, and packed with smoky, vibrant flavor from the tandoor. Altogether, it’s a restaurant that delivers authentic Indian cuisine with finesse, making it a place we’d gladly return to.

tl;dr definitely the best Indian food I’ve ever had.

Initial vibe: Stopped into Curry Leaf (2046 Sansom St) and was hit with that warm, comforting spice cloud the second I walked in. It’s a Nepali & Indian spot right in Center City, low-key and welcoming.  ￼

Ambiance: Cozy, casual, and clean—tables are close enough to feel lively but not cramped. Lighting’s soft, music at a chill volume, and it’s the kind of place where you can actually talk. Nothing fussy; just the good stuff.

Food: the garlic naan…insane. Blistered edges, pillowy middle, tons of garlicky bite—outrageously good. (They list Garlic Naan on the menu, and it lives up to the hype.) Mains were deeply flavored without being heavy—sauces tasted freshly built, bright spices, and you can tell they care about balance. Prices are super reasonable for Center City: naan around $6–7 and classic curries ~ $19–20, and the portions are big—one entrée plus naan easily fed two of us with leftovers.  ￼

Service: Friendly and fast without hovering. Water refills kept coming, food landed hot, and they checked spice prefs without me asking. Felt like they actually wanted me to love what I ordered.

Value: For the quality + portion sizes + location, it’s a steal. I’d come back just for the naan, but honestly the whole meal slapped.

Bottom line: 5/5, def a new go-to. If you’re anywhere near Sansom, run for that garlic naan and a curry. Best meal I’ve had in ages.

Came here with some of my friends and it was delicious! It was a cozy vibe and the food was very good and felt home-cooked. The service was also very good…my friend’s dish was slightly spicy (not the restaurants fault), but they so kindly gave us a complimentary dessert. Definitely recommend and will come back soon :) Thank you!!

I know you might be hesitant, but this place is legit and absolutely delicious. In the mood for Indian? Then look no further than Curry Leaf. Food is made to order, pipping hot and tasty. I ordered spicy on a scale of mild, medium, spicy, very spicy. It was perfect. Don’t mind the water bottles, paper menus and small seating area if you dine in. Minor details considering the high level quality of food you’re being treated to. The garlic naan was the best I’ve ever had by far. So much garlic flavor, exactly what you would dream of!

Atmosphere is 10/10. Walls are red like chicken tikka masala. Come here on an off school day and you might see a kid chilling in the corner playing roblox at this cozy family run place. They have American palate classics like Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala. The Indian food we tried was yummy. They have different levels of spice and mango lassi on the menu for those of us with a baby mouth.

We ordered Tandoori chicken, samosa chaat, and lamb saag. Tandoori chicken takes about 25 min because they make it fresh so make sure you call in advance if you’re in a hurry. The lamb saag was good. This place uses cubes of lamb instead of bone in, making it easier to eat. Rice is complimentary to some dishes! Samosa chaat was delicious because the samosa was hot and still crunchy- you can tell they made it to order.

My main feedback is they should put on the menu which food is Nepalese because most people in the area would not know. There are far fewer Nepalese restaurants in the area compared to Indian so this would help for those looking specifically for this type of food. Makes me nostalgic for Jackson Heights momo crawl. Sadly no momos on the menu yet but maybe I can convince the owner.
customer_insights: Curry Leaf Nepali & Indian Cuisine offers a cozy and welcoming atmosphere with authentic dishes that are well-prepared and flavorful. The garlic naan and chicken tandoori are standout items, making it a great spot for casual dining with friends or a relaxed date night.

googleReviews: We had an awesome lunch here!  The food is As authentic as can be right on Penn‘s campus.  Very flavorful and not crazy spicy.  My kids are going to be on campus for the next four years and I expect that they will probably just live here!!

I was really excited when I saw they were going to open Masala Kitchen earlier in 2025 and since I’ve become a regular. It’s one of my favorite quick service restaurants in University City. Biryani here is really good and they got me craving Limca with each meal. As a regular, would recommend!

Masala Kitchen in University City is one of those reliable spots you can count on when you’re craving flavorful Indian street food on the go. Their kati rolls are the real deal—soft paratha wraps filled with perfectly seasoned meat or paneer, onions, and chutneys that hit just the right balance of spice and tang. I’ve tried a few variations, but the chicken tikka and paneer masala rolls are my personal favorites—fresh, messy in a good way, and totally satisfying.

The menu’s not huge, but what they do, they do well. If you’re pairing up something sweet, don’t skip the mango lassi. It’s chilled, creamy, and tastes like a dessert after a spicy roll—definitely a must-order. Portion sizes are generous for the price, and service is fast enough for a quick lunch stop between classes or errands. The vibe is casual and bustling, so it’s great for takeout or a laid-back bite with friends. Worth coming back again!

I got the biryani and it was fine. but it definitely felt like the tame version of what you would actually get. It felt like it needed more flavor. Not salted enough and the spices felt like it needed to be stronger. Staff were nice and quick. The music was not my fave but whatever.

This place is no frills, but has an ample amount of indoor and outdoor seating. You order off a touch screen, which was super easy to navigate. My family tried two different Katie rolls and the chicken/lamb platter. All the food was absolutely amazing, packed with flavor, spice, and texture. We are visiting from Virginia and the his was not only our best meal we had, but the best value also. I highly recommend this place to everyone!
customer_insights: Masala Kitchen offers authentic Indian street food with a focus on kati rolls and biryani, making it a popular spot for quick meals in University City. The casual atmosphere and fast service cater well to students and families, although some dishes may lack the expected spice levels.

googleReviews: I've been making my way to all the indian spots around my block and this one's my favorite of the three I've tried so far. I had Chicken Tikka Masala Hot, Samosa, Raita, and Garlic Naan. All delicious and very generous portions, I'll have food for at least another meal or two. And Holy Samosa! They're huge. Only took about 10 minutes from walking in and ordering to having my takeout ready. I'll definitely be back.
Worst ever indian food. The taste was not good and most importantly the foods were not fresh at all. Felt sick after my dinner here

The all you can eat buffet spread was fantastic, with a variety of delicious options. From tender chicken, flavorful lamb, and succulent goat dishes to plenty of great vegetarian choices, there’s something for everyone. The flavors were rich and authentic, and everything was perfectly spiced.

The highlight for me was the Gulab Jamun for dessert – it was absolutely delicious! Soft, warm, and perfectly sweet. I can’t wait to return for another round. Highly recommend this place for anyone craving great Indian food in Philly.

I’ve ordered from New Delhi dozens of times through Grubhub and have always enjoyed them but after this experience, I am VERY impressed and plan to see their location in person at some point. When I ordered today, my Grubhub driver (to be clear, this driver is NOT affiliated with New Delhi directly) canceled my order and refunded me out of nowhere claiming the restaurant was closed. New Delhi called me to tell me that the restaurant was not actually closed though. The Grubhub driver was not telling the truth. New Delhi was very apologetic and said that if I just placed the same order again through Grubhub, a new driver can be sent out. The food was already made and they wanted to make sure I got it! When I tried placing the order, Grubhub was once again glitching and telling me that I needed to wait until 5pm when they claimed the restaurant was open. I called New Delhi back to explain the issue and then they reached out to Grubhub to see what was going on. New Delhi then called me back again to tell me the issue had been resolved and I could place my order again. They really went above and beyond to ensure I got my food and it was still warm when I finally got it! And they even threw in a free mango lassi for my trouble. It was very unexpected and kind. High praises for New Delhi!

Indian buffet is back! 10% discount if you have student ID. See hours in photo, they don't quite match what google has on file.

This spot rules!
customer_insights: New Delhi Indian Restaurant is a popular casual dining spot in Philadelphia known for its generous portions and flavorful Indian cuisine. While many customers rave about the buffet and specific dishes like Chicken Tikka Masala and Gulab Jamun, there are mixed reviews regarding freshness and taste. Overall, it's a solid choice for takeout or a casual meal with friends.

googleReviews: This is absolutely the Best FOOD in Manayunk!! Very fresh, tasty cuisine, small, quaint atmosphere and LOVELY staff. This is my go-to restaurant for a great meal and great vibes!

Walking along Main Street and popped into Manayunk Indian Grille! Had a delicious meal.

We started with the vegetable samosas, which were some of the best I’ve had. They were fried well and super flavorful, and the sauces that came with it were delicious.

For my entrée, I got the chicken tikka. I mistakenly got this instead of chicken tikka masala, but it was still delicious. The lemon and onions added great flavor and the yogurt sauce had garlic in it which I enjoyed. Put it on some garlic naan = perfect bite!

Atmosphere and service was lacking, but I assume this is a primarily takeout spot so I don’t count it against the rating. I would get takeout from here in the future!

Got To Give This One A Thumbs Up! 👍
Had A Thunder-Thumbs Up, Lamb Kabob & Rice For Lunch! What A Day To Have A Break & Festive Day Today! Take A Rest With M.I.G!

The food was solid here at Manayunk Indian Grille.
I went for lunch and it wasn’t crowded. My order came out quickly.
Pictured is the Chicken Tikka Masala with Butter & Garlic Naan. The creamy sauce had a nice flavor and spice to it.
The staff was also friendly.
Highly recommend if you love Indian food or looking to try it out. We had the fried pakora, garlic naan, chicken tikka masala, and i think kadai chicken is what my friend had. Food was delicious.
customer_insights: Manayunk Indian Grille is praised for its fresh and flavorful Indian cuisine, particularly the vegetable samosas and chicken tikka. While the atmosphere may be more suited for takeout, the friendly staff and quick service make it a solid choice for casual dining or a pregame meal.

googleReviews: The duck is worth the price.  Everything is the best version of itself plus some other flavors that really add something special.  The staff is lovely and the presentation divine. Highly recommend the savory crepe, the eggs and tuna.

Amazing food, great atmosphere, and great service. We got the tasting menu, which included several appetizers, a main, and desert. One of the best meals we've had. The dishes were suprising, complex, and well composed. We will definitely be going back.

I went to Forsythia for the first time, and was so excited especially because of the recent recognition from Michelin! The service was substandard, but most of our food was tasty.

For 10 minutes after we were seated, nobody came over. Eventually, a staff member did and just asked do you want to put in any drinks? No introduction, name, or information on the menu. We said we would like a rundown of the cocktails and she passive aggressively said well what do you need to know. It was condescending and not helpful.

They brought out complimentary focaccia which was so hard it was inedible. My friend said its not normally like that. Im shocked they would serve us that.

The food we ordered was good - frog legs, mozzarella beignets and scallops. The scallops were outstanding and presented beautifully. When we ordered them, the server asked if we wanted mushrooms or potatoes with them. We got mushrooms (so tasty) but when we got the bill, there was a $14 for a side of mushrooms. She didn’t tell us it wasn’t included with the entree, we didn’t appreciate the sneaky way of trying to get us to spend more money.

Overall, I’m very hesitant to come back because of how poor the service was. The prices are HIGH and I have been to several restaurants in the city with way better service for lower prices. Its unacceptable.

My husband and I went here for his birthday and everything we ate was wonderful and beautifully presented. We started with happy hour at the bar and rolled right into dinner. Service was friendly, attentive, and helpful throughout. My husband ordered the chicken and thought it was one of the best things he’s ever eaten. I loved the desserts. We will definitely be back.

Always a great experience. Chef Chris creations amaze every time. Devon my server surprised me with a Tuna carpaccio with Lobster - was awesome and gave great recommendation for the French Omelette. Literally melted in your mouth. Another Great Brunch!
customer_insights: Forsythia offers a refined dining experience with a focus on beautifully presented Italian and Mediterranean dishes. While the food receives high praise, service experiences can vary, making it a great spot for special occasions but with some caution regarding service consistency.

googleReviews:
From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with genuine warmth and promptly seated. Opting for the Let Us Cook experience turned out to be an excellent decision. Our server, Dan, was exceptionally knowledgeable and guided us through the menu with thoughtful recommendations. The entire staff, including Dan, was friendly, attentive, and detail-oriented—service was truly impeccable.

The food was outstanding. Highlights included the seafood platter, especially the sea urchin and pickled shrimp, which offered a delightful balance of freshness and acidity. The main course, a bone-in pork chop, was cooked to perfection—each bite was rich, tender, and deeply satisfying. The Let Us Cook option gave us a well-curated sampling of dishes, and we left feeling both full and impressed.

I wholeheartedly recommend My Loup for its exceptional cuisine and top-tier service. It’s a place where hospitality and culinary artistry come together beautifully.

We first visited in October 2023 and had an incredible experience — everything was spot on. The food and drinks were fantastic, service was top notch. The steak with pumpkin , eel Caesar, and fish crudo were true standouts.

Unfortunately, when we returned last night (September 2025), the experience was far from the same. The new menu felt underwhelming, and the overall food quality had declined noticeably.

We ordered the tuna tartare appetizer, sungold tomato appetizer, and the Escar-roll to start. For mains, we tried the “à la David” chicken and the skirt steak, followed by the Mille-feuille for dessert.

The biggest disappointment was the skirt steak. We weren’t asked how we wanted it cooked, and it arrived nearly raw (blue, not even medium rare). The server didn’t check in until later, and when we explained the issue, the steak was taken back. A few minutes later, the same steak returned, reheated in the same jus. Unfortunately, it was still very rare, overly gamey from the reheating, and extremely chewy — inedible, really. We couldn’t finish the steak and informed the server again, but despite the clear issue, we were still charged the full $70 for the dish and seemed like she didn’t even cared about this issue.(The photo attached shows the steak after it was “recooked.”)

On the positive side, the chicken was enjoyable, and both the escargot dish and the dessert were highlights of the evening. Still, given our excitement to revisit after such a stellar first experience in 2023, this return was deeply disappointing. Between the service and the food, we left unsatisfied and, sadly, don’t see ourselves coming back and unfortunately had to update my review from 5 stars to 3.
One of our top 3 favorite restaurants in Philly. The cocktails and the food are both unreal. There is no weak part of the menu so no matter what you choose you will be blown away.

Disappointed experience. Got the $125 per person tasting menu. It started strong but ended very weak. Lamb and snail appetizer were very good but main course (steak, bake potato, and salad) was mediocre at best. They accidentally brought us the break down price receipt. Steak was definitely not worth $150.

Service was good. People are nice. But environment/music was way too loud. The bartender was yelling sometimes. Difficult to have a conversation.

My fiancé and had a incredible dining experience at My Loup.
Beautiful lively atmosphere, and an attentive and helpful staff, ready to answer any questions regarding food and beverage options.

We ordered from the a la carte menu and all dishes were fantastic. The oysters were fresh and the pickled shrimp and crackers was unique and delicious. I am also a big fan of sour dour bread, so I had to order that, and it was amazing (the butter too). Save some to dunk in the sauces of the main courses.

The duck ribs were my favorite dish of the evening, tender, flavorful, the meat slide right off the bone.

For mains, we ordered the roast chicken and the Roasted Skate Wing ‘Piccata, both delicious, fresh and quite large portions. It was a nice touch when the chef (Alex Kemp) delivered the fish dish and explained the proper way to cut it.

Lastly, the blueberry frangipane tart was a perfect dessert to the end the meal.

The wine and cocktail list is also extensive.

I highly recommend reservations, the bar also requires reservations, we arrived about 15 minutes early and enjoyed a cocktail near the hostess stand until our table was ready.
customer_insights: My Loup offers a blend of exceptional cuisine and attentive service, making it a popular choice for special occasions. However, recent reviews indicate inconsistency in food quality and service, particularly with the steak dish, which may affect repeat visits.

googleReviews:
Not impressed.
The food was just okay. The oysters were sandy, the escargot was made with a weird creamy sauce with pork and croutons in it. Not your typical French escargot. I guess some might like it, but I did not care for it.
The beef tartar was so bad we returned it.
The quiche was good but I was super hot which makes me think it was reheated. This level of heat can only be obtained with microwave handling. But it tasted good after it had a chance to cool down a little.
The drinks were really nice but quite expensive. A non alcoholic drink should not cost $10. Everything else is fairly priced.
The service was really good and our waiter was very attentive, friendly and available.
I probably won’t be back and wouldn’t recommend this place.

I found this hidden gem while searching for dinner during a recent trip to Philadelphia. The weather was perfect, and it was a delight to sit on their charming patio and enjoy the evening. The food, service, and atmosphere were all excellent. I ordered the pork chop, and it was absolutely delicious—perfectly cooked and full of flavor. The staff was friendly and attentive, making the whole experience feel warm and welcoming. I highly recommend stopping by Caribou Café if you’re in the area. A great spot for a relaxed, satisfying meal.

We've been to Caribu several times over the past few months.  We've enjoyed all our visits!  First, the ambiance is great...very French, friendly, and unpretentious.  The decor is beautiful and moody in a good way.  They have accordion glass doors that open the whole place up to the street with sidewalk tables under an awning.  Can't wait to bring our pup here for a bite.  Second, the food is on point for casual French.  My favorite is the Salad Nicoise and hubby loves the burger and Pan Bagnat sandwich.  We've had these more than once and they are consistently great!  Third, service is excellent.  We always sit at the bar and Aaron is their primary bartender.  Not only does he have great suggestions for drinks, wine, or beer...but he is an amazing DJ.  He curates the best music for the mood of the room and spans so many genres and timeframes, often choosing deep cuts from popular musicians...it's very impressive.  Lastly....they show the games!  So if you want to drink delicious belgian beers or a beautiful french wine, while listening to Soft Cell's Tainted Love, and watching the Phillies on TV....this is the perfect bougie "in a fun way" spot for you!  We are becoming regulars for sure.

I sit here as I type, feeling lucky to have found this place to have a dreamy lunch on my day trip from NYC for work. Lovely vibe, great service, amazing playlist, tasty wine, best Niçoise salad I’ve had in quite a while. Just go. You won’t regret it. Happy hour from 4-6pm

I stopped in here for dinner and some beer because I love French food and Belgian beer. The place did not disappoint. The atmosphere is lovely with really fun, decorations, all through the bar and in the restrooms. I had the escargot and a side of hericots verts (green beans) which were absolutely delicious. The bartender Ellen was lovely. Highly recommend this place for the food and drink selection and service.
customer_insights: Caribou Cafe offers a charming atmosphere with a casual French dining experience. While reviews are mixed regarding food quality, the ambiance and attentive service are frequently praised, making it a suitable spot for casual outings and pregame drinks.

googleReviews: We came here for an afternoon apero before dinner.  Excellent place for shares and drinks we considered canceling our plans.   Next time we would stay for dinner.

Duck is delicious. I was enjoying the music playlist. Had a reservation and highly recommend one. I had the chicken special, didn’t love it but that’s just about me rather than the food quality.

It can get loud in here. Clean but dark bathrooms.

Easy to get to via the BSL

The food wasn’t bad overall, though most dishes were on the salty side. The socca was burned and had a bitter taste, but the mussels were great. The music was a bit loud and didn’t really match the French vibe. Overall, it’s a nice experience.

So. Good. This is one of the best restaurants in Philadelphia. An eclectic cocktail list, a rotating duck special, tasteful desserts. Bottom line, the entire menu is just... *chef’s kiss*

Cannot recommend the duck specials enough!

**UPDATE** More than a year later, TGKT doesn’t fail to dazzle. My partner and I just visited for outdoor dining and it was a phenomenal, comfortable, fantastic experience. Food is just as great as ever, and the cocktails may be even better than ever!!

It’s worth noting that we’ve also gotten their burgers for takeout numerous times now, and they’re absolutely amazing. One of my top burgers in Philly no question.

Tasty food, nice heated outdoor seating, friendly staff! Some unique food items in the menu. We and the kids especially enjoyed the chickpea pancakes (Socca). The cocktails are also surprising, most have unusual ingredients in them. If you feel like experimenting, you should try one of their cocktails.
customer_insights: The Good King Tavern is a lively spot known for its eclectic cocktail list and rotating duck specials. While the atmosphere can get loud, it offers a trendy and casual dining experience, making it suitable for various social gatherings, including dates and group outings.

googleReviews:
I had the opportunity to eat at the Bistro Perrier on a few occasions. Booking a reservation online is quick and easy. Upon arriving I was greeted by a host who took us to our seats. I have been able to sit in different parts of the bistro to enjoy different scenery.

We ordered Raclette Potatoes, Mussels (which has been a favorite), Pan Roasted Salmon and Steak Frites. We also had a variety of desserts.

The students are really able to showcase their skills whether greeting, managing tables, taking orders and the students making the food.

This precious student run dining features specials developed solely by them as well as other favorites. Keep this in mind as aside from your host (also their professor) 100% of the staff are students. Think of it like Culinary Institute but in University City

I started with a glass of wine and a salad based on arugula with a spring pea purée. I followed that with a lamb dish that had probably the best roasted carrot I ever tasted, perfectly cooked lamb and a parsnip purée that had deep umami. I splurged on a side of the  mushroom fricassee which had a great variety of mushrooms in a light cream sauce. I wish I had room for the in house desserts but I may have accidentally eaten one of the baked breads with sea salt encrusted butter which filled me up!

A few things - the students are also servers so they are learning different parts (front bs back of the house). So I had to ask for a wine list and a little more detail than she was able to provide in some entrees. Also the plating is a place they could improve so keep that in mind - the food tastes great even if it’s not decked out in microgreens etc.

The atmosphere in the back is like a French bistro and the bar area is a throwback charmer. Perfect for friends or a date night. Any tips go back to the program enjoy!

Bistro Perrier is a restaurant that puts in a effort to make itself authentically French.The service while a little bit nervous was good.The food quality was above average.The taste of the food was what you expect from a French restaurant,which isn’t that easy for it being in Philadelphia. The extras that you get with your meal is also a nice touch.The food however could use(like the rabbit)a bit more seasoning,and better Execution.

Loved this place. Got their Valentine’s Day menu (the day after). Had a smoked salmon dish, parsnip soup, steak dish, halibut. They even made my daughter a fettuccine Alfredo dish, how nice of them! The dessert where a chocolate pot de creme and a mocha tart (not my favorite but I really don’t care for coffee, so that’s on me). We where do pleases with the dinner it’s hard to believe that students are in the kitchen cooking it. I think it speaks volumes about the teachers instructing them. Good job all around.

A real amazing restaurant.  Everyone was ready to help us, always kind and happy.  The manager, sorry I don't remember his name, is fantastic!  He came to the parking lot to show us where was a handicapp space.  He took the wheelchair out of the trunk and pushed me all the way inside.  (Made my husband happy too! ;)
They helped us choose a wine, and advise on the menu, because of allergies.
It was my birthday so they made a vegan dessert for me.
I wholeheartedly recommend this place.  You can splurge with a meal, wine, dessert and all; Top of the line menu and help, without the pocket suffering much.
Thank you so much!!
customer_insights: Bistro Perrier is a unique student-run French dining experience that offers a taste of authentic French cuisine in a charming atmosphere. While the service is provided by students, the food quality is noted to be above average, making it suitable for romantic dinners and special occasions.

googleReviews:
The food here is simply phenomenal. I come here very often and it’s consistently great. The Omelettes and sandwiches are amazing. They know how to cook an egg!

You’re in for a treat if they still have pastries or bread pudding (the bread pudding is out of this world - they use their own croissants).

Every Saturday they typically have a special sandwich or something like that - often very good.

Jordan the host / waitress /  part of family team and her parents are amazing hosts. It’s always so warm and friendly.

The cafe is well lit. The prices are reasonable. It’s a neighborhood staple that has been around for a long time and gets a lot of regulars. You’ll feel like you’re in a small town in southern France but in the heart of Philadelphia.

They play relaxed level music that doesn’t distract and allows you to talk.

A good place to bring a dog if sitting outside.

Can’t say enough great things!

The best quiche in town! We got the classic quiche, crab/corn chowder, Brie and tomato quiche and the hot pancetta BLT sandwich. We also got two ice lattes and everything was so perfect. One of the best breakfast/ brunch spots in Philly!

Review: Cafe Lutecia – A Hidden French Gem in Philly

Tucked away in a quiet corner of Philadelphia, Cafe Lutecia is the kind of place that makes you feel like you’ve stumbled into a cozy Parisian café by accident—and then never want to leave. From the moment I walked in, the warmth of the space and the staff made it clear this was going to be something special.

The service was exceptional—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming without being overbearing. It's the kind of place where the staff remembers your name and your favorite order if you come more than once.

One standout detail that really elevated my visit? The fresh juicer behind the counter. I ordered a glass of fresh-pressed orange juice, and it was nothing short of perfect—vibrant, sweet, and just the right amount of tang. You can taste the difference when something is that fresh.

Whether you're stopping in for a coffee or a light, thoughtfully prepared lunch, Cafe Lutecia delivers on every front. It’s quaint, it's charming, and it’s easily one of Philly’s best-kept secrets.

Very friendly place with great service and very decent food. Lots of the patrons knew each other and greeted each other coming in and out, and the staff seemed to be all family. Food was fast, good and reasonably priced

Love Café Lutécia! Croissant is to die for, the daily quiches are always so good, and that tomato bique is chef's kiss.

The people who run it are always sweethearts and the vibe is lovely, highly recommend 👌
customer_insights: Café Lutécia is a beloved neighborhood café known for its exceptional brunch offerings, including quiches and pastries. The warm, welcoming atmosphere and attentive service make it a perfect spot for casual gatherings or intimate meals.

googleReviews:
Spent a great evening at Fleur's with friends.  We ordered several appetizers, including Beef tartar, Pork & pistachio terrine, Sesame carrots. Also got a complimentary salad from the kitchen, which felt like a nice touch. All appetizers were top-notch, each with its own palate treats and nuances, creatively made and perfectly presented. For the main courses we had fish and chicken, and both were delicious. I was surprised by the fact that despite being open for 2+ months only, the restaurant has already got the warm, friendly, special vibe.
It's my second time at Fleur's, and some new seasonal offerings have been added to the menu, which added to the diversity. Our server Anya deserves a special mention, as she was extremely professional and warm at the same time. We felt like we were at a friends' house for dinner. You need to try and save some space for the dessert, which is challenging but absolutely worth it. We were full, but the desserts were so unbelievably good that we almost ate the decorative flowers (they are edible 😊). We will definitely be back, together with numerous friends.

A new addition to the philly food scene! The inside is awesome with a classy vibe. The bar and seating on the first floor is comfortable and inviting and also seating on a wrap around balcony overlooking the first floor. Service is outstanding, alcant say enough about that. The food is delicious! Had to Google a few words from the menu lol, or you can just ask the server. The scallop appetizer and onion Tarte were delicious. The steak frites was great as was the fresh pasta with crab. Other great dishes in our group (with no complaints) the trout, the eggplant, shrimp and oyster apps. Desserts were delicate and delicious. The French vanilla custard and the fois white chocolate croissant with cherry compote. Definitely worth a try!

Fleur’s is clearly a labor of love. We had dinner there on opening night. Despite being new, the restaurant ran smoothly. Everything was beautifully executed—the food, the atmosphere, and the service. The renovation is gorgeous and detail oriented. Love how the new owners preserved so much of the original building. They’ve got great taste!

Every dish we tried was creative but delicious. The uni custard tartlet was so creamy, and paired well with caviar. The foie gras and white chocolate croissant topped with sour cherry marmalade was such an unexpectedly cool combo. The smoked whitefish tartine with duck fat brioche (gluten-free!) was surprisingly light with nice pops of salt from trout roe. Sesame carrots were nutty and hearty, one of many vegetarian options. Chicken was juicy with crispy skin, on top of a punchy sweet pepper piperade. Steak was perfectly cooked topped with a zesty Thai chili vierge. Fries were thin and crispy paired with an insanely addictive sunchoke soubise. All in all, a daring yet approachable menu. Hats off to Chef Sabatino and his team!

Our server, Anthony, was really attentive and knowledgeable. Service in general was top notch. Prices were reasonable given the quality of food and hospitality. So happy to have Fleur’s in the neighborhood! Looking forward to seeing the rest of the building get transformed as well. Can’t wait to come back!

Loved my experience at Fleur’s! The service was excellent and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. The “Two Sisters” non-alcoholic drink was so refreshing and flavorful. My top picks were the steak frites, half chicken, and chilled corn nage. Every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented. Don’t skip the French vanilla custard for dessert, it’s the perfect sweet ending!

Fleur’s is East Kensingtons newest restaurant! My friend and I came in a few weeks after they opened and had a mixed experience.

Starting off, they sat us at a 2 seat table in the back of the restaurant. The table was so close to the one next to it that I could hardly squeeze through them (I wouldn’t consider myself a large person either). We asked if we could sit anywhere else and they said that was the only table available, so we found ourselves at the bar. The bar had large comfortable seating luckily.

Our server, Ethan, was very knowledgeable about the cocktails and menu. We started with the mission statement cocktail, similar to a French 75. It was delicious.

For an appetizer, we got the mussels vinaigrette. Amazing! It tasted like an elevated McDonalds filet-o-fish… I know that may not sound appetizing, but it was incredible. Crispy potato cake and so many fresh flavors.

For our entrees, we were a bit disappointed. We got the steak au poivre medium rare and it was tough and chewy. I did enjoy the thai chili sauce on top for an added kick. The bone marrow fries it came with were also not crispy and had too much seasoning on them. The parisian gnocchi in a mushroom ragu was good, not great. The flavor profile was pretty one note and nothing wowed me about it. I wouldn’t reorder.

For our dessert, we saw they had Mighty Bread croissants filled with white chocolate and foie gras, topped with berries. For $19 it was just not worth it. I heard their other desserts are better and wish I ordered something else.

Overall, we enjoyed our service, cocktails and appetizers. The entrees have some work to do, as well as the seating arrangements. For the price point, it wasn’t what I hoped for… but I do hope they can make some adjustments as they settle in!
customer_insights: Fleur's offers a warm and inviting atmosphere with a creative and delicious menu, making it a great spot for various occasions. While the service is consistently praised, some diners have noted inconsistencies in the main courses, suggesting room for improvement as the restaurant continues to establish itself.

googleReviews: This place delivered on food, service, menu selection, and vibes. Eat outside if you can! Super chill and romantic outdoor seating. Ratatouille was gorgeous and came with two pieces of warm bread. Cheeseburger and fries were great too. Flavor could’ve been improved a bit for both. This place definitely scores points for the vibes and service.

This brunch spot was exactly what you’d expect from a solid brunch joint. They were really accommodating when we showed up a little late, which we appreciated. We got the chicken and waffles and the Dutch baby, and both were great. No complaints at all. We ended up adding some fries to round things out and that hit the spot too.

Phenomenal BYOB upscale restaurant. Small menu which helped me decide on the burger with fries (absolutely stunning!). Would definitely love to come back! Also they were very good with gluten free restrictions

We also got burrata to start us off and the chocolate pudding type thing for dessert. Everything was very very good and our server was awesome. To quote him “this is the best burger in Philly” and I haven’t had any other burgers in Philly yet but I wouldn’t be surprised, it might have been the best burger I’ve ever had

Love!!  I came here for brunch with a friend and we ate outside.   The inside is small but it feels cozy and intimate.  The service was excellent, the waiters were so friendly and helpful.  I ordered the croque madame which was amazing - the ham had the perfect thickness, cheese melted perfectly, and egg cooked to order.  The salad was fresh and had the tastiest, light poppy seed dressing.  I also tried my friend's turkish eggs which were delicious - light, lemony, and creamy.  You could taste the care and quality with which the chef cooks every meal.  For a relaxed, leisurely weekend brunch, this is the place to be.

Came here for Sunday brunch with my 12 year old daughter.  She said the pork katsu breakfast sandwich was the best she ever had and enjoyed the mustard aoili on it.  I had the shrimp and grits and liked the lemon flavor and the heartiness with corn and peas.
customer_insights: Mabu Kitchen is a cozy, upscale BYOB restaurant in Philadelphia, perfect for brunch or intimate dinners. 🤗

breakfast, lunch or dinner. The food was consistently good on all occasions. An omelette for breakfast, Philly cheesesteak for lunch or spicy crab noodles for dinner, it was all good. The Red Owl Tavern was a fantastic choice for lunch in Old City, Philadelphia.

We stopped by Honey’s Sit ’n Eat for breakfast and really enjoyed it. The Honey’s platter was solid—the eggs were just okay, but overall the breakfast was satisfying. The pancakes stood out: fresh, fluffy, and delicious. The real star, though, was the breakfast quesadilla. The cheesy eggs wrapped in a warm tortilla and topped with avocado were absolutely perfect.

Absolutely, positively one of the best breakfast restaurants I've ever been to. The customer service is always amazing. This time I got the breakfast bomb, which was eggs and meat inside a pancake. Absolutely delicious. The dirty chai latte was also great. I truly can't recommend Honey Sit n Eat enough.

Let me first start by saying that we were seated within 15 mins of getting to the restaurant which was great considering it was Sunday at 1130am prime brunch time. Our server was great albeit a little slow, but was taking care of the entire bar section. Prices for the food were pretty good and the portions were generous. Now let's talk about the food. I had the special chipotle chicken eggs Benedict absolutely amazing, eggs cooked perfectly, the chipotle hollandaise was rich and coated the eggs beautifully. Also they give you an option for a latka instead of breakfast potatoes. This is going down a new favorite spot in Philly for me. 10/10 Ill be back!

We have been bringing our son to Honey's on and off since he was just six years old, not long after they first opened their doors. Today, my family decided to visit while our son was in town from out of state, now at the age of 26. On this particular visit, we were met with food and service that did not meet our expectations, leading all four of us to come to the same disappointing conclusion.

My son's mother ordered the toad in the hole, a dish that is supposed to be served with a poached egg and truffle oil. However, upon receiving her meal, she noticed that there was no truffle oil to be found on the micro greens or the egg. We pondered whether it was simply forgotten or omitted intentionally. Truffle oil is known for its distinctive aroma and taste, which was sorely missed. Furthermore, the egg itself was overcooked, bordering on hard when it should have been slightly runny, as per tradition.

The issues continued as my son's burger arrived without the server asking for his preferred doneness, and my son forgetting to inform her of his preference. Despite his excitement to reunite with us, this oversight led to a less-than-ideal experience. Additionally, we noticed discrepancies between the menu available in the restaurant and the one displayed on the website. Items such as ramps and grits, favorites of ours, were missing. The limited vegan options offered no alternatives, with the veggie patty melt arriving tasteless and on toasted bread instead of the expected grilled cheese style, resulting in a dry and unsatisfying sandwich.

Even the fries failed to impress, arriving lukewarm as if they had been sitting out for some time without being freshly prepared. The absence of vegan cheese options added to our disappointment. Despite our visit taking place during a relatively quiet time around 1 PM, the lackluster presentation and experience left much to be desired.

Having always cherished our visits to Honey's in the past, we hope that they take this feedback as a wake-up call to improve their offerings and service. As evidenced by the pictures we took, the contrast in our experiences was stark. Our fingers are crossed that this will prompt them to realign their standards and get back on track.
customer_insights: Honey's Sit 'n Eat is a beloved breakfast spot in Philadelphia known for its hearty portions and friendly service. While many patrons rave about the quality of the food, there have been occasional inconsistencies in execution and menu offerings that have disappointed some long-time customers.

Fantastic Meal with Thoughtful Service at Marathon Grill

Our recent visit to Marathon Grill was an absolute pleasure. From start to finish, everything about the experience was seamless and enjoyable. We had a reservation but arrived a bit early, and the staff kindly seated us right away, a nice start to what turned out to be a standout meal.

Our server, Greg, was exceptional, attentive, courteous, and well-informed. With my gluten sensitivity, dining out can be tricky, but Greg navigated it gracefully. He was knowledgeable about the menu and, when unsure, double-checked with the kitchen to ensure everything was safe for me. His care and professionalism were deeply appreciated.

The food? Excellent across the board. I opted for the special of the day, an ahi tuna salad, and it was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. I was impressed by how many gluten-free options were available, which made ordering feel relaxed rather than limiting.

Everyone at the table found something to love. My boys were thrilled with their choices, the Marathon Burger and the cheesesteak, both hearty portions served with crispy fries. My husband also selected a daily special, broiled mahi mahi tacos, and raved about the flavor and texture.

The entire meal was served quickly and arrived at just the right temperature, a testament to the kitchen's timing and quality. Beyond just being a great restaurant for those with dietary needs, Marathon Grill proved to be a versatile spot for the whole family.

Highly recommend this gem for anyone looking for a delicious, welcoming, and well-run dining experience. We’ll definitely be returning!

Our waiter was taking orders for 12 people without writing anything down... As you can imagine this didn't go well lol The food was fantastic though!

Perogies were some of the best I've had

Steak was on point and cooked properly

Mac and cheese was awesome!

Will definitely return when in the area!
The food was pretty good.   Service was great.  I absolutely loved the view.  I could people watch here all day.

The waitress and hostess could use just a little more training on acknowledging patrons. Felt like more of a burden than a customer. The shuckers were super friendly and very upbeat!
Visited for the first time in August 2025 and had a great first experience! Loved the grilled oysters, regular oysters, octopus, clam chowder. Can't wait to try it again sometime.

There is really nothing that makes you satisfied like a good lobster roll.

I was able to get the last one and it was so worth it.

The octopus side dish with the peanut sauce was so delicious.

Outstanding french fries as well.
